adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use feta cheese -- substitute a dairy-free feta-style crumble or extra olives for briny flavor.
Do NOT use walnuts -- substitute roasted pepitas or sunflower seeds.

name: Shredded Chicken Caesar Wraps
description: I make the Caesar dressing in a big batch on prep day so it's ready for wraps, salads, and dipping all week -- the shredded chicken is the same batch from Sunday, just dressed differently.
steps: Whisk egg yolk, mayonnaise, anchovy paste, dijon, lemon juice, and garlic into a Caesar dressing; this batch keeps in the fridge for the week's wraps and salads.
Toss shredded chicken with 2 tbsp of the dressing.
Toss romaine with a bit more dressing and half the parmesan.
Warm tortillas briefly in a dry skillet to make them pliable.
Layer dressed romaine and chicken down the center of each tortilla, top with remaining parmesan.
Roll tightly, slice in half, and wrap for grab-and-go lunches.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the shredded chicken for roasted chickpeas for a vegetarian wrap.
Do NOT use flour tortillas -- substitute certified gluten-free tortillas or large lettuce leaves as wraps.
Do NOT use parmesan cheese -- substitute a dairy-free parmesan alternative or nutritional yeast.
Do NOT use egg yolk or regular mayonnaise (both contain egg) in the dressing -- substitute an egg-free/vegan mayonnaise for both, or use a store-bought egg-free Caesar dressing.
Do NOT use anchovy paste -- substitute 1/2 teaspoon drained capers, finely chopped, for the umami note.

name: Sweet Potato & Black Bean Quesadillas
description: The crispy-skillet cousin of my burrito bowl -- same roasted sweet potato and black bean batch, folded into a tortilla and griddled until the cheese holds it all together.
steps: Mash roasted sweet potato lightly with cumin and chili powder; stir in black beans.
Lay a tortilla flat, spread with the sweet potato-black bean mixture, sprinkle with cheese, and top with a second tortilla.
Griddle in a dry skillet over medium heat 3-4 minutes per side until golden and the cheese melts.
Slice into wedges.
Serve with sour cream, sliced scallions, and a squeeze of lime.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use whole wheat flour tortillas -- substitute certified gluten-free tortillas.
Do NOT use Monterey Jack cheese or sour cream -- substitute a dairy-free shredded cheese and dairy-free sour cream, or omit the sour cream and top with mashed avocado instead.

name: Peanut-Ginger Chicken & Rice Noodle Salad
description: My most involved batch-lunch, but the payoff is worth it -- one big pot of peanut-ginger sauce dresses shredded chicken, rice noodles, and crunchy veggies for the whole week without ever going soggy if you keep the sauce separate until serving.
steps: Cook rice noodles per package directions, rinse under cold water, and drain well.
Whisk peanut butter, soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, ginger, and garlic with 2-3 tbsp warm water until smooth and pourable -- this sauce batch keeps a week refrigerated.
Toss noodles with half the sauce.
Divide noodles into containers and top each with shredded chicken, carrots, and cucumber.
Store remaining sauce separately and dress each portion just before eating to keep the noodles from clumping.
Finish with cilantro, crushed peanuts, and a lime wedge.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the shredded chicken for pan-seared cubed tofu for a vegetarian version.
Do NOT use peanut butter or crushed peanuts -- substitute sunflower seed butter for the sauce and toasted pepitas for the garnish.
Do NOT use soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos in the same amount.
Do NOT use toasted sesame oil -- substitute a neutral oil such as avocado oil; the flavor will be milder but the dish still works.

name: Egg Fried Rice with Roasted Veggies
description: A five-ingredient way to turn yesterday's batch rice and roasted veggies into today's lunch -- day-old rice actually fries up better than fresh, which is exactly why this is a batch-cook favorite of mine.
steps: Heat a large skillet or wok over high heat with a splash of oil.
Scramble the eggs quickly, breaking into small curds, then set aside.
Add garlic and ginger to the pan, then the day-old rice, breaking up clumps.
Stir in roasted veggies and peas, tossing until heated through.
Push rice to the side, drizzle in soy sauce and sesame oil, then toss everything together.
Fold in the scrambled eggs and scallions just before serving.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use eggs -- substitute 1 cup crumbled soft tofu sauteed with a pinch of turmeric for color and scrambled-egg texture.
Do NOT use soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos in the same amount.
Do NOT use toasted sesame oil -- substitute avocado oil.

name: Garlic-Lime Shrimp & Black Bean Rice Bowl
description: A fast-cooking protein swapped onto my usual rice-and-black-bean batch base -- shrimp cooks in under five minutes, so this is the lunch I make when the week's batch-cook needs a quick second protein option.
steps: Toss shrimp with garlic, chili powder, salt, and the juice of one lime.
Sear shrimp in olive oil over medium-high heat, about 2 minutes per side, until pink and just cooked through.
Warm the batch-cooked rice and black beans.
Build the bowl with rice, black beans, and seared shrimp.
Top with sliced avocado, cilantro, and a squeeze of the second lime.

alternateRecipe.name: Garlic-Lime Chicken & Black Bean Rice Bowl
alternateRecipe.description: The same garlic-lime treatment as my shrimp bowl, but built on diced chicken thighs for anyone avoiding shellfish -- it reheats better too, which makes it the stronger choice for a make-ahead lunch.
steps: Toss diced chicken with garlic, chili powder, salt, and the juice of one lime.
Sear chicken in olive oil over medium-high heat, about 6-7 minutes, until cooked through and lightly browned.
Warm the batch-cooked rice and black beans.
Build the bowl with rice, black beans, and the seared chicken.
Top with sliced avocado, cilantro, and a squeeze of the second lime.

name: Turkey & Quinoa Stuffed Peppers
description: A lunch that batch-cooks itself into its own containers -- I make a double batch of turkey-quinoa filling on prep day, then just refill peppers or spoon it over greens depending on what's in the fridge.
steps: Preheat oven to 375F and arrange halved peppers cut-side up in a baking dish.
Brown ground turkey with onion and garlic until cooked through; drain excess fat.
Stir in quinoa, black beans, diced tomatoes, cumin, and chili powder; this is the batch filling -- make a double portion, since it also works over rice or greens.
Spoon filling into the pepper halves, mounding generously.
Top with shredded cheddar and bake 25-30 minutes until peppers are tender and cheese is bubbling.
Cool slightly before packing into containers for the week.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the ground turkey for extra black beans and quinoa, or cooked lentils, for a vegetarian filling.
Do NOT use cheddar cheese -- substitute a dairy-free shredded cheese, or omit and top with sliced avocado instead.

name: Batch-Roasted Chicken & Veggie Grain Bowls
description: This is the bowl that makes the rest of my week possible -- one big pan of chicken and vegetables roasted together, then portioned over rice for tonight and stashed away for two more meals.
steps: Preheat oven to 425F and line two sheet pans.
Toss chicken thighs with half the olive oil, half the garlic, oregano, salt, and pepper on one pan.
Chop peppers, zucchini, and onion into large chunks; toss with remaining oil and garlic on the second pan.
Roast both pans 25-30 minutes, flipping the vegetables once, until the chicken reaches 165F internal.
Shred or chop the chicken. Portion about a third of the chicken and vegetables over warm rice for tonight's bowls.
Squeeze lemon over and top with feta. Cool the remaining chicken and vegetables and refrigerate separately for two more meals this week.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use feta cheese -- substitute a dairy-free feta alternative or a sprinkle of nutritional yeast.
Swap the chicken thighs for a 15-oz can of chickpeas, roasted alongside the vegetables for the last 15 minutes, for a vegetarian bowl.

name: Garlic-Ginger Beef & Rice Stir-Fry
description: Built on the same batch of rice and the same garlic-ginger paste I keep on hand all week -- this one's on the table in half an hour flat.
steps: Toss the sliced beef with cornstarch and let sit 10 minutes.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat. Sear the beef in batches until browned, 2-3 minutes; remove.
Add broccoli and carrots to the pan with a splash of water; stir-fry 3-4 minutes until crisp-tender.
Add garlic and ginger, stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return beef to the pan. Add soy sauce and sesame oil, toss to coat, and cook 1-2 minutes.
Serve over warm rice, topped with green onions.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the flank steak for thinly sliced chicken breast or pressed, cubed extra-firm tofu.
Do NOT use soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos, which are soy-free and gluten-free.
Do NOT use sesame oil -- substitute a neutral oil like avocado oil, with a squeeze of lime for brightness.
Regular soy sauce is brewed with wheat -- do NOT use it. Substitute a certified gluten-free tamari or coconut aminos.

name: Weeknight Pork Fried Rice
description: Day-old rice fries up so much better than fresh -- this is where the extra batch I cook on Sunday earns its keep, alongside pork I browned once for two other meals.
steps: Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large skillet or wok. Brown the ground pork, breaking it up, until cooked through; remove.
Push aside and add remaining oil; scramble the eggs in the same pan until just set, then break into small pieces.
Add rice, breaking up clumps, and stir-fry 3-4 minutes until it starts to toast lightly.
Add peas and carrots, garlic, and ginger; stir-fry 2 minutes.
Return pork and egg to the pan, add soy sauce and sesame oil, and toss until evenly combined and heated through.
Garnish with green onions and serve.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the ground pork for ground chicken, ground turkey, or crumbled extra-firm tofu.
Do NOT use eggs -- substitute 1/2 cup crumbled soft tofu sauteed briefly for a similar scrambled texture, or omit entirely.
Do NOT use soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos, which are soy-free and gluten-free.
Do NOT use sesame oil -- substitute a neutral oil such as avocado oil.
Regular soy sauce is brewed with wheat -- do NOT use it. Substitute a certified gluten-free tamari or coconut aminos.

name: Black Bean & Sweet Potato Enchiladas
description: My roasted sweet potato batch and a can of black beans turn into a completely different dinner than the grain bowl they started in -- that's the whole point of batch-cooking.
steps: Preheat oven to 375F. Spread a thin layer of enchilada sauce in a 9x13 baking dish.
In a bowl, combine sweet potato, black beans, onion, cumin, and a third of the cheese.
Warm tortillas briefly so they roll without cracking. Fill each with the sweet potato mixture and roll, placing seam-side down in the dish.
Pour remaining enchilada sauce over the top and sprinkle with remaining cheese.
Bake 25 minutes until bubbly and lightly browned.
Top with sour cream and cilantro before serving.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use flour tortillas -- substitute corn tortillas, which are naturally gluten-free (warm them briefly so they don't crack when rolled).
Do NOT use Monterey Jack cheese or sour cream -- substitute a dairy-free shredded cheese and a dairy-free sour cream alternative, or omit both and add extra cilantro and lime.

name: Sunday Beef Bolognese over Spaghetti
description: I make a double batch of this sauce every few weeks and freeze half in flat bags -- tonight's dinner and next month's are the same fifteen minutes of chopping.
steps: Heat olive oil in a heavy pot. Cook onion, carrot, and celery until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add garlic and cook 1 minute, then add ground beef and brown fully, breaking it up.
Deglaze with red wine if using, then add crushed tomatoes, milk, and basil.
Simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, 45 minutes until thick and rich.
Cook spaghetti according to package directions; drain.
Toss pasta with sauce and top with grated parmesan.

alternateRecipe.name: Sunday Lentil Bolognese over Spaghetti
alternateRecipe.description: Brown lentils simmered the same long, slow way as the beef version -- just as rich, and it freezes in the same flat bags.
steps: Heat olive oil in a heavy pot. Cook onion, carrot, and celery until softened, about 8 minutes.
Add garlic and cook 1 minute, then stir in lentils, vegetable broth, crushed tomatoes, and basil.
Simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, 35-40 minutes until lentils are tender and the sauce is thick.
Cook spaghetti according to package directions; drain.
Toss pasta with sauce and top with parmesan if using.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular spaghetti -- substitute a certified gluten-free pasta.
Do NOT use whole milk or parmesan cheese -- substitute unsweetened oat milk and a dairy-free hard-cheese alternative, or omit both.

name: Baked Chicken Parmesan
description: The breadcrumb coating and marinara here are the same two components I use for the freezer meatballs -- I bread and bake a double batch of chicken so half goes straight into the freezer for a later week.
steps: Preheat oven to 425F and set a wire rack over a sheet pan.
Slice chicken breasts in half horizontally to make thinner cutlets.
Set up a dredging station: flour, beaten eggs, and panko mixed with parmesan and Italian herbs.
Dredge each cutlet through flour, egg, then breadcrumb mixture, pressing to adhere. Place on the rack and drizzle with olive oil.
Bake 18-20 minutes until golden and cooked through, then top each cutlet with marinara and mozzarella and bake 6-8 minutes more until melted.
Serve over spaghetti tossed with remaining marinara.

alternateRecipe.name: Baked Eggplant Parmesan
alternateRecipe.description: Same breading, same marinara, same bubbly mozzarella top -- eggplant slices stand in for the chicken and hold up just as well to the freezer.
steps: Salt eggplant slices and let sit 20 minutes on paper towels to draw out moisture, then pat dry.
Preheat oven to 425F and set a wire rack over a sheet pan.
Set up a dredging station: flour, beaten eggs, and panko mixed with parmesan and Italian herbs.
Dredge each eggplant round through flour, egg, then breadcrumb mixture. Place on the rack and drizzle with olive oil.
Bake 20-25 minutes until golden, then top with marinara and mozzarella and bake 8-10 minutes more until melted.
Serve over spaghetti tossed with remaining marinara.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use panko breadcrumbs, all-purpose flour, or regular spaghetti -- substitute gluten-free breadcrumbs, a 1:1 gluten-free flour blend, and a certified gluten-free pasta.
Do NOT use parmesan or mozzarella -- substitute dairy-free parmesan and mozzarella-style alternatives.
Do NOT use eggs for the dredge -- substitute a flax egg (1 tbsp ground flaxseed plus 3 tbsp water per egg, rested 5 minutes).

name: Freezer Turkey Meatballs & Marinara over Rice
description: I roll a triple batch of these on a Sunday and freeze two-thirds raw on a sheet pan -- future me just drops them straight into simmering marinara from frozen.
steps: In a large bowl, combine ground turkey, breadcrumbs, egg, parmesan, garlic, parsley, salt, and pepper. Mix gently, don't overwork.
Roll into 1.5-inch meatballs (makes about 24).
Heat olive oil in a large skillet and sear meatballs on all sides, about 6-8 minutes total (they don't need to be fully cooked yet).
Add marinara sauce, bring to a simmer, cover, and cook 15 minutes until meatballs are cooked through.
Serve over warm rice.
For the freezer batch: arrange raw shaped meatballs on a sheet pan, freeze solid, then transfer to a freezer bag -- simmer straight from frozen in marinara, adding 10 extra minutes.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the ground turkey for ground chicken or a plant-based ground meat alternative.
Do NOT use panko breadcrumbs -- substitute gluten-free breadcrumbs or certified gluten-free rolled oats, pulsed fine.
Do NOT use egg as the binder -- substitute a flax egg (1 tbsp ground flaxseed plus 3 tbsp water, rested 5 minutes).
Do NOT use parmesan cheese -- substitute a dairy-free parmesan alternative or omit it.

name: Sheet-Pan Roasted Veggie & Quinoa Buddha Bowl
description: This is my clean-out-the-crisper bowl -- whatever's left of the week's roasted veggie batch gets a fresh tahini drizzle and a scoop of quinoa, and suddenly it's a whole new dinner.

ingredients.name: roasted veggie medley (bell pepper, zucchini, red onion)

steps: Whisk tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and water together until smooth and pourable, adding more water if needed.
Divide quinoa and spinach among bowls.
Top with roasted veggie medley and roasted chickpeas.
Drizzle generously with the tahini dressing.
Scatter sliced almonds on top and serve.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use tahini -- substitute a sunflower seed butter thinned with lemon juice and water for a similarly creamy dressing.
Do NOT use sliced almonds -- substitute roasted pepitas (pumpkin seeds) or sunflower seeds for crunch.

name: Black Bean & Rice Stuffed Peppers
description: Stuffed peppers are secretly a batch-cook's best friend -- I fill a full tray at once using the same rice and beans I've already got going for two other meals.
steps: Preheat oven to 375F. Arrange halved peppers cut-side up in a baking dish.
Heat olive oil in a skillet, saute garlic 30 seconds, then stir in rice, black beans, corn, diced tomatoes, cumin, and chili powder.
Simmer 3-4 minutes until warmed through, then stir in half the cheese.
Spoon the filling into the pepper halves, pressing gently to pack.
Cover with foil and bake 30 minutes, then uncover, top with remaining cheese, and bake 10 more minutes until peppers are tender and cheese is melted.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use cheddar cheese -- substitute a dairy-free shredded cheese alternative or a sprinkle of nutritional yeast.

name: Shredded Chicken Tacos with Roasted Veggies
description: Five minutes of assembly on top of a batch of chicken I already made this week -- this is the dinner that makes batch-cooking worth it on a Tuesday.

ingredients.name: roasted veggie medley (bell pepper, zucchini, red onion)

steps: Warm the shredded chicken and roasted veggie medley together in a skillet over medium heat until heated through, about 5 minutes.
Warm tortillas in a dry skillet or directly over a gas flame, a few seconds per side.
Fill tortillas with the chicken and veggie mixture.
Top with cheese, sour cream, a squeeze of lime, cilantro, and hot sauce to taste.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the shredded chicken for shredded jackfruit or seasoned black beans for a vegetarian taco.
Do NOT use cheddar cheese or sour cream -- substitute a dairy-free shredded cheese and a dairy-free sour cream alternative, or top with extra avocado instead.

name: Quinoa-Stuffed Sweet Potatoes with Black Beans
description: Two of my favorite batch components -- quinoa and black beans -- piled into a whole roasted sweet potato instead of a bowl, for the nights I want dinner to feel a little more like a plate and a little less like meal prep.
steps: Preheat oven to 400F. Pierce sweet potatoes with a fork and bake directly on the rack 45 minutes until tender.
Meanwhile, toss quinoa, black beans, corn, red onion, lime juice, cumin, and olive oil together in a bowl.
Split the baked sweet potatoes open lengthwise and fluff the flesh slightly with a fork.
Spoon the quinoa and black bean mixture into each potato.
Top with avocado slices and cilantro before serving.

name: Salmon with Roasted Veggie Medley & Quinoa
description: One sheet pan of salmon goes in right alongside the veggie medley I'm already roasting for two other meals -- dinner and the rest of the week's batch-cook happen at the same time.

ingredients.name: roasted veggie medley (bell pepper, zucchini, red onion)

steps: Preheat oven to 425F.
Pat salmon fillets dry, rub with olive oil, garlic, salt, and pepper, and place on a sheet pan alongside the veggie medley (add extra veggies if roasting a fresh batch).
Roast 12-15 minutes until salmon flakes easily and veggies are tender.
Divide quinoa among plates, top with salmon and vegetables.
Squeeze lemon over and finish with fresh dill.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use salmon -- substitute boneless chicken thighs or extra-firm tofu, roasted the same way and checked for doneness.

name: Sausage & Peppers Skillet with Rice
description: One skillet, the same peppers I bought in bulk for two other meals, and rice I already have cooked -- this is a fifteen-minute dinner most weeks.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Sear sausages on all sides until browned and cooked through, about 12 minutes; remove and slice.
In the same skillet, saute peppers and onion until softened, about 6-8 minutes.
Add garlic, Italian herbs, and red pepper flakes; cook 1 minute.
Return sliced sausage to the pan and toss with the peppers for 2-3 minutes.
Serve over warm rice.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the Italian sausage for a chicken or turkey sausage, or a plant-based sausage alternative.

name: Thai Peanut Chicken & Rice Noodle Bowl
description: Balancing the peanut sauce is the one part of this bowl I still taste and adjust every single time -- everything else rides on rice noodles and chicken I've already got batched from earlier in the week.
steps: Soak or cook rice noodles according to package directions; drain and rinse with cold water.

Whisk peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, ginger, garlic, honey, sesame oil, and warm water together until smooth. Taste and adjust the balance of salty, sweet, and tangy -- add more lime for brightness, honey for sweetness, or soy for depth as needed.
Toss the noodles with about half the peanut sauce.
Divide noodles among bowls, top with shredded chicken, carrots, and cabbage.
Drizzle with remaining sauce.
Garnish with crushed peanuts, green onions, and cilantro.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the shredded chicken for pan-seared extra-firm tofu for a vegetarian bowl.
Do NOT use peanut butter or crushed peanuts -- substitute sunflower seed butter for the sauce and crushed roasted sunflower seeds for the garnish, or omit the garnish entirely.
Do NOT use soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos, which are soy-free and gluten-free.
Do NOT use sesame oil -- substitute a neutral oil such as avocado oil, plus an extra squeeze of lime for depth.
Regular soy sauce is brewed with wheat -- do NOT use it. Substitute a certified gluten-free tamari or coconut aminos. Also double-check the rice noodle brand is labeled gluten-free.

name: Batch Rice & Black Bean Cakes
description: This is the snack that makes your Sunday rice-and-beans batch earn its keep twice -- press it into patties, crisp it in a skillet, and you've got a grab-and-go snack that shares ingredients with two dinners this week.

ingredients.name: black beans, cooked and drained (from batch)

steps: In a large bowl, mash the black beans with a fork until mostly smooth, leaving a little texture.
Stir in the cooked rice, egg, panko, cheddar, scallions, cumin, and salt until the mixture holds together when pressed.
Divide into 8 patties, about 1/3 cup each, packing them firmly so they don't crumble in the pan.
Heat olive oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat.
Cook the cakes 4-5 minutes per side until golden and crisp, working in batches so the pan isn't crowded.
Drain briefly on a paper towel and serve warm, or cool completely and refrigerate for grab-and-go snacking through the week.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use egg -- substitute 1 tablespoon ground flaxseed mixed with 2.5 tablespoons water, rested 5 minutes until gelled, as the binder.
Do NOT use regular panko breadcrumbs -- substitute gluten-free panko or crushed gluten-free crackers.
Do NOT use dairy cheddar -- substitute a dairy-free shredded cheese or omit it and add an extra pinch of salt.

name: Roasted Veggie & Hummus Flatbread Bites
description: No new chopping here -- this snack is built entirely on the roasted bell pepper, zucchini, and onion medley you already batch-roasted for the week's dinners, so it comes together in the time it takes to warm the bread.

ingredients.name: roasted veggie medley (bell pepper, zucchini, red onion, from batch)

steps: Warm the flatbread lightly in a dry skillet or toaster oven, about 1 minute per side, then cut into quarters.
Spread each piece generously with hummus.
Top with a spoonful of the roasted veggie medley -- this is the exact batch already made for dinner, no extra chopping tonight.
Scatter crumbled feta over the top.
Drizzle with olive oil and lemon juice, finish with parsley, and serve at room temperature.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular flatbread or pita -- substitute a certified gluten-free flatbread or wrap.
Do NOT use tahini-based hummus -- substitute a sesame-free white bean dip or a hummus made with sunflower seed butter instead of tahini.
Do NOT use feta cheese -- substitute a dairy-free feta-style crumble or omit it and add an extra pinch of salt.

name: Shredded Chicken Lettuce Cups
description: Your batch-shredded chicken gets a quick glaze in soy, sesame, and sriracha and lands in lettuce cups -- the same chicken that's going into tomorrow's grain bowl, just wearing a different hat tonight.
steps: In a small saucepan, warm the shredded chicken with soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, and sriracha over medium-low heat, 3-4 minutes, just until glossy and heated through.
Lay out the lettuce leaves like little cups.
Spoon the warm chicken mixture into each leaf.
Top with shredded carrots, chopped peanuts, and cilantro.
Serve right away while the lettuce is still crisp.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the shredded chicken for shredded rotisserie turkey, or use pressed and crumbled extra-firm tofu for a vegetarian version.
Do NOT use soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos in the same amount.
Do NOT use sesame oil -- substitute avocado oil or another neutral oil.
Do NOT use peanuts -- substitute toasted sunflower seeds for the garnish crunch.

name: Loaded Sweet Potato Skins with Black Beans & Cheddar
description: This is where the sweet potatoes you already batch-roasted earlier in the week go for a second act -- scoop, refill with the black bean batch, and a quick broil turns them into a snack that shares two ingredients with dinner.
steps: Halve the already-roasted sweet potatoes lengthwise and scoop out most of the flesh, leaving a sturdy 1/4-inch shell (save the scooped flesh for tomorrow's breakfast hash -- another use for the same batch).
Brush the skins inside and out with olive oil and season with salt and pepper.
Broil skin-side up for 5 minutes to firm them up.
Flip, fill each shell with black beans and cheddar.
Broil again for 3-4 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and lightly browned.
Top with sour cream, crumbled bacon, and scallions, then serve hot.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy cheddar or sour cream -- substitute a dairy-free shredded cheese and a cashew-based sour cream.
Swap the bacon for crumbled turkey bacon, or omit it and add extra smoked paprika for that same savory note.

name: No-Bake Quinoa Peanut Butter Energy Bites
description: Built on a cup of the quinoa you already batch-cooked for the week's grain bowls, these no-bake bites are the easiest way to keep that batch from going stale before it gets used up.
steps: Stir the peanut butter, honey, and vanilla together in a large bowl until smooth.
Fold in the cooked quinoa, rolled oats, chia seeds, chocolate chips, and a pinch of salt.
Chill the mixture in the fridge for 15 minutes so it firms up enough to roll.
Roll into 16 balls, about 1 tablespoon each.
Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to a week, or freeze for longer -- these are built to outlast the quinoa batch that made them.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use peanut butter -- substitute sunflower seed butter in the same amount.
Do NOT use regular rolled oats -- substitute certified gluten-free rolled oats.
Do NOT use regular chocolate chips -- substitute dairy-free chocolate chips.

name: Crispy Roasted Chickpea & Parmesan Snack Mix
description: Roast a double batch of chickpeas while the oven's already hot for something else in the week's lineup, toss with parmesan and pretzels while still warm, and you've got a snack-bag mix that holds its crunch for days.

ingredients.name: canned chickpeas, drained and patted dry

steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F and line a sheet pan.
Toss the chickpeas with olive oil, garlic powder, paprika, and salt.
Roast 30-35 minutes, shaking the pan halfway through, until deeply golden and crisp.
While still warm, toss the roasted chickpeas with parmesan so it melts slightly and clings.
Cool 5 minutes, then toss with pretzel sticks and sesame seeds.
Store in an airtight container -- this holds its crunch for 3-4 days, perfect for portioning into the week's snack bags.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use parmesan cheese -- substitute 2 tablespoons of nutritional yeast for a similar savory, cheesy flavor.
Do NOT use regular pretzel sticks -- substitute certified gluten-free pretzel sticks.
Do NOT use sesame seeds -- substitute poppy seeds, or omit them entirely.

name: Freezer Oatmeal Chocolate Chip Cookie Dough Bites
description: One big bowl, one hour in the freezer, and dessert is portioned for the next two weeks -- I mix a double batch on Sunday and never think about weeknight dessert again.
steps: In a big mixing bowl, stir the almond butter and honey together until smooth -- this is the base I always double, since it keeps in the fridge for two weeks before you even roll it.
Fold in the oats, chia seeds, vanilla, and salt until every oat flake is coated.
Fold in the chocolate chips last so they don't melt into the warm almond butter.
Scoop into 1-inch balls (a small cookie scoop keeps them uniform) and set on a parchment-lined tray.
Freeze the tray flat for 1 hour, then transfer the bites to a labeled freezer bag -- flat-frozen first means they won't clump into one giant ball in the bag.
Pull out a handful straight from the freezer whenever dessert calls; they soften to a chewy bite in about 5 minutes at room temperature.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use almond butter -- substitute sunflower seed butter measured 1:1; it has the same sticky consistency to bind the oats.
Do NOT use standard mini chocolate chips -- substitute a dairy-free/vegan chocolate chip brand (check the label for milk fat or whey) measured 1:1.

name: Batch-Roasted Cinnamon Stone Fruit & Yogurt Parfaits
description: I roast a full sheet pan of stone fruit whenever the dinner oven's already on for something else -- half goes over breakfast oatmeal all week, the other half becomes this parfait the night I want dessert to feel like it took effort and didn't.
steps: Heat the oven to 400F. Halve and pit the peaches and plums; arrange cut-side up on a rimmed sheet pan.
Whisk the melted butter, brown sugar, and cinnamon together and brush it over the cut fruit.

Roast 20-25 minutes, until the fruit is soft and the edges are caramelized. This is the batch step -- I roast double what tonight's dessert needs and keep the extra in the fridge for topping breakfast oatmeal or yogurt through the week.
Let the fruit cool slightly, then slice into wedges.
Layer yogurt, roasted fruit, and granola in glasses or bowls, repeating for a second layer.
Finish with the toasted almonds and a drizzle of any caramelized pan juices left on the sheet pan.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy butter or dairy yogurt -- substitute melted coconut oil for the butter and a full-fat coconut or oat-milk yogurt for the Greek yogurt, both measured 1:1.

Do NOT use standard granola -- substitute a certified gluten-free granola measured 1:1; double-check the label, since granola is a common cross-contamination risk even when oats are naturally gluten-free.
Do NOT use sliced almonds -- substitute toasted pepitas (pumpkin seeds) measured 1:1.

name: Make-Ahead Rice Pudding from Batch-Cooked Rice
description: This is the dessert version of my rice batch-cook -- the same pot of rice that goes into three dinners this week finishes its run as a stovetop pudding, so nothing gets thrown away and nobody has to cook rice twice.

ingredients.name: cooked white rice, day-old, from the week's batch

steps: Combine the cooked rice, milk, cream, sugar, and cinnamon stick in a heavy saucepan over medium-low heat.
Simmer gently, stirring often so the rice doesn't scorch on the bottom, for about 15 minutes until it thickens and the rice softens further.
In a small bowl, whisk the egg yolks with a ladleful of the warm rice mixture to temper them, then stir the tempered yolks back into the pot.
Cook another 3-5 minutes over low heat, stirring constantly, until the pudding coats the back of a spoon -- do not let it boil once the yolks are in, or it will curdle.
Remove the cinnamon stick, stir in the raisins and vanilla, and let cool slightly.
Portion into jars while warm; it thickens further as it chills and keeps in the fridge for up to 5 days, which makes it an easy make-ahead dessert to pull from all week.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use whole milk and heavy cream -- substitute full-fat canned coconut milk for both, measured 1:1 combined (about 2 1/2 cups total); it gives the same rich body.
Do NOT use egg yolks -- substitute 2 tablespoons cornstarch whisked into 3 tablespoons cold water, stirred in during step 4 instead of tempering; simmer 2-3 minutes until thickened.

name: Big-Batch Peanut Butter Freezer Fudge
description: Four ingredients, one pan, zero oven -- I make a double batch of this on the same day I'm freezing the cookie dough bites so the freezer dessert stash is stocked for a solid month.
steps: Line an 8x8-inch pan with parchment, leaving overhang on two sides for easy lifting.
Melt the peanut butter and coconut oil together in a small saucepan over low heat, stirring until smooth.
Off the heat, whisk in the maple syrup and cocoa powder until fully combined and glossy.
Pour into the prepared pan, smooth the top, and sprinkle with flaky salt.
Freeze for at least 2 hours, or until firm, before lifting out and slicing into squares.
Store the squares in a freezer bag or airtight container -- they hold their texture straight from the freezer, so this is genuinely a 'cut one piece off, dessert's done' situation.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use peanut butter -- substitute sunflower seed butter measured 1:1; the fudge sets up the same way.

name: Freezer-Stash Banana Walnut Blondies
description: This is where the walnuts I toast in bulk for the week's oatmeal go on their day off -- one pan of blondies uses up overripe bananas and leftover toasted nuts at the same time, which is exactly the kind of double-duty I build a week around.

ingredients.name: toasted walnuts, chopped, from the week's batch

steps: Heat the oven to 350F and line a 9x9-inch pan with parchment.
Whisk the mashed banana, melted butter, and brown sugar together until smooth.
Whisk in the egg and vanilla.
Stir in the flour, baking soda, and salt just until combined.
Fold in the toasted walnuts and white chocolate chips, saving a small handful of each to scatter on top.
Spread the batter into the prepared pan, top with the reserved walnuts and chips, and bake 28-32 minutes, until a toothpick comes out mostly clean and the top is golden.

Cool completely, then cut into squares -- half the pan freezes well wrapped in parchment and foil for up to 2 months, so this doubles as a freezer dessert stash the same way the cookie dough bites do.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy butter and white chocolate chips -- substitute melted coconut oil for the butter and a dairy-free white chocolate chip brand for the chips, both measured 1:1.
Do NOT use egg -- substitute 1 flax egg (1 tablespoon ground flaxseed whisked into 3 tablespoons water, rested 5 minutes).
Do NOT use all-purpose flour -- substitute a 1:1 gluten-free baking flour blend that contains xanthan gum.
Do NOT use walnuts -- substitute toasted pepitas measured 1:1.

name: Freezer-Batch Peanut Butter Oat Energy Bites
description: I make a double batch of these every Sunday and freeze half -- they're the thing that keeps a lunchbox or an after-school ask from turning into a trip to the pantry for whatever's fastest.
steps: In a large bowl, stir together the oats, peanut butter, honey, chia seeds, vanilla, and salt until a stiff dough forms.
Fold in the mini chocolate chips.
Chill the dough for 15 minutes so it's easier to handle.
Roll into 1-inch balls (about 20-24 bites) and set on a parchment-lined tray.
Freeze half the batch in a labeled freezer bag for up to 2 months; keep the rest in the fridge for up to a week.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use peanut butter -- substitute sunflower seed butter (sunbutter) measured the same, 1 cup.
Do NOT use standard mini chocolate chips -- substitute a dairy-free chocolate chip brand measured the same, 1/3 cup.

name: Big-Batch Honey Almond Granola Bars
description: One sheet pan makes enough bars to cover breakfast grabs and after-dinner treats for the whole week -- the same toasted oats and almonds I batch here also top my roasted-fruit crisps, so nothing goes to waste.
steps: Preheat oven to 350F and line a 9x13 pan with parchment, leaving overhang on two sides.
Spread the oats and sliced almonds on a sheet pan and toast for 8-10 minutes, stirring once, until golden and fragrant.
In a saucepan, warm the almond butter, honey, butter, cinnamon, and salt over low heat until smooth, about 3 minutes.
Stir the toasted oats and almonds and the dried cranberries into the warm honey mixture until evenly coated.
Let cool 5 minutes, then fold in the mini chocolate chips so they don't fully melt.
Press firmly and evenly into the lined pan -- really lean into it, a tight pack is what keeps the bars from crumbling.
Chill at least 2 hours, then lift out by the parchment and cut into 16 bars.
Wrap bars individually and freeze half for grab-and-go weeks; keep the rest in an airtight container up to 5 days.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use sliced almonds or almond butter -- substitute toasted pepitas (3/4 cup) for the almonds and sunflower seed butter (3/4 cup) for the almond butter.
Do NOT use standard butter or mini chocolate chips -- substitute a plant-based butter stick (2 tbsp) and a dairy-free chocolate chip brand (1/3 cup), both measured the same.

name: Freezer-Stash Fudgy Cocoa Brownies
description: I always bake a double pan of these -- one goes straight into the freezer cut into squares, so a chocolate craving three weeks from now doesn't turn into an unplanned grocery run.
steps: Preheat oven to 350F and line a 9x13 pan with parchment.
Melt the butter, then whisk in sugar and cocoa powder until smooth.
Whisk in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Fold in the flour, salt, and walnuts just until no dry streaks remain -- overmixing is the only real way to ruin these.
Spread into the pan and bake 28-32 minutes, until a toothpick has a few moist crumbs, not wet batter.
Cool completely in the pan before cutting into 24 squares.
Wrap half the squares individually and freeze up to 3 months; they thaw on the counter in about 20 minutes.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy butter -- substitute a plant-based butter stick measured the same, 1 cup.
Do NOT use eggs -- substitute 4 flax eggs (4 tbsp ground flaxseed whisked with 12 tbsp water, rested 5 minutes) in place of the 4 eggs.
Do NOT use all-purpose flour -- substitute a 1:1 gluten-free baking flour blend measured the same, 1 cup.
Omit the walnuts entirely, or substitute an equal amount of nut-free mini chocolate chips, 1/2 cup.

name: Weekly Frozen Yogurt Bark, Three Ways
description: This is what I do with the back half of a big tub of yogurt before it turns -- one sheet pan splits into three flavor zones so nobody in the house has to agree on toppings.
steps: Line a sheet pan with parchment.
Whisk the yogurt, honey, and vanilla together until smooth and spread evenly across the pan, about 1/2 inch thick.
Scatter the strawberries over one third, granola over the middle third, and chocolate chips over the last third.
Freeze uncovered at least 4 hours, or until fully solid.
Break into shards and store in a freezer bag -- it keeps well for a month and never gets soggy the way whole frozen yogurt tubs do.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use Greek yogurt or standard mini chocolate chips -- substitute a plain coconut- or oat-milk yogurt (3 cups) and a dairy-free chocolate chip brand (1/4 cup), both measured the same.
Do NOT use almond granola -- substitute a nut-free granola or plain toasted oats measured the same, 1/2 cup.

name: Microwave Mug Scrambled Eggs
description: Two eggs, a mug, and about ninety seconds of microwave time -- no stovetop needed when you're rushing to an 8am.
steps: Crack the 2 eggs into a large microwave-safe mug or bowl (at least 12 oz, so the eggs don't overflow as they puff up).
Add the milk, salt, and pepper, and whisk with a fork until fully blended and slightly frothy.
Microwave uncovered on high for 45 seconds, then stir with the fork.

Microwave in 20-second bursts, stirring between each, until the eggs are fully set with no wet or runny liquid left -- usually 3-4 bursts total. Eggs are safe to eat once no liquid egg remains and they're firm throughout; you won't have a thermometer for this, so "no runny spots" is your visual check.
Stir in the shredded cheese while the eggs are still hot so it melts, and eat straight from the mug.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use milk or shredded cheese -- substitute unsweetened plain soy milk or water for the milk, and either omit the cheese or use a dairy-free shredded cheese alternative.

alternateRecipe.name: Microwave Mug Tofu Scramble
alternateRecipe.description: Same one-mug method, swapped to firm tofu and a pinch of turmeric for that scrambled-egg color and texture.
steps: Press excess water out of the tofu by squeezing it gently in a paper towel or clean cloth, then crumble it into a microwave-safe mug or bowl.
Stir in the oil, turmeric, garlic powder, and salt until the tofu is evenly coated and yellow.
Microwave uncovered on high for 2 minutes, stir, then microwave in 30-second bursts (stirring between each) until heated through and slightly firm, about 4 minutes total.
Let cool for a minute before eating -- tofu holds heat.

name: No-Cook Peanut Butter Banana Overnight Oats
description: Mix it in a jar before bed and breakfast is already done when your alarm goes off -- zero heat, zero dishes in the morning.
steps: In a jar with a lid or any container with a tight-fitting cover, combine the oats, milk, peanut butter, honey, and cinnamon.
Stir well until the peanut butter is mostly broken up and mixed in -- it won't fully dissolve, and that's fine.

Cover and refrigerate overnight (at least 6 hours). If you don't have a fridge, this only works safely for a couple hours at cool room temperature -- milk-based food left out longer than 2 hours is a food-safety risk, so plan for fridge access, or skip the milk-soak step and just eat it as dry-toasted oats with the same toppings.
In the morning, stir again, top with the sliced banana, and eat cold straight from the jar -- no heating required.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy milk -- substitute unsweetened soy milk, oat milk, or water instead, in the same amount.
Do NOT use peanut butter -- substitute sunflower seed butter (widely sold as a peanut-free alternative) in the same amount.

name: Peanut Butter Banana Toast
description: The cheapest real breakfast there is -- bread, peanut butter, a banana, and nothing that needs a stove.
steps: Toast the bread in a toaster if you have one; if not, toast it in a dry pan over medium heat for about 1 minute per side until golden, watching closely so it doesn't burn.
Spread 1 tablespoon of peanut butter on each slice while it's still warm so it softens slightly.
Layer the banana slices on top, drizzle with honey, and dust with cinnamon.
Eat immediately while the toast is still warm.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular bread -- substitute a certified gluten-free bread, toasted the same way.
Do NOT use peanut butter -- substitute sunflower seed butter in the same amount.

name: Rice Cooker Egg Congee
description: A rice cooker turns leftover rice and water into a warm, filling porridge while you shower -- no stovetop babysitting required.
steps: Add the cooked rice, water, and salt to a rice cooker (or a covered pot on the stove over low heat if you don't have one).

Run the rice cooker on the regular "cook" or "porridge" setting, or, on the stove, simmer uncovered over low heat, stirring occasionally, until the rice breaks down into a thick, creamy porridge, about 35-40 minutes.

Crack the egg directly into the hot congee and stir it in for about a minute until it's fully cooked through with no runny streaks visible -- the residual heat of the porridge is usually enough, but if you're unsure, let it sit covered another minute before checking.
Stir in the soy sauce, top with sliced green onion, and eat straight from the bowl once it's cool enough not to burn your mouth.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use egg -- substitute 1/4 cup drained canned chickpeas or extra crumbled firm tofu stirred in during the last minute of cooking for protein.
Do NOT use soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos, or a pinch of salt with a small splash of rice vinegar.

name: Microwave Breakfast Burrito
description: Eggs cook right in the mug, then get folded into a tortilla with beans and cheese -- one microwave, one pan-free breakfast that travels to class.
steps: Crack the eggs into a microwave-safe mug or bowl and whisk with a fork until blended.
Microwave uncovered on high for 45 seconds, stir, then continue in 20-second bursts until fully set with no runny liquid left, about 3 bursts total.
Stir the black beans, cheese, and bacon bits into the hot eggs so the cheese melts.
Warm the tortilla for 15-20 seconds in the microwave wrapped in a damp paper towel so it's pliable and doesn't crack when folded.
Spoon the egg mixture down the center of the tortilla, top with salsa, fold in the sides, then roll it up burrito-style.

Eat right away, or wrap it in foil to eat on the way to class. Bacon bits (whether the shelf-stable jarred kind or a refrigerated fully-cooked variety) should be kept refrigerated once opened and used within a few days -- check the label, since not all bacon bits are shelf-stable after opening.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use a flour tortilla -- substitute a certified gluten-free tortilla or two corn tortillas, warmed the same way.
Do NOT use egg -- substitute 1/2 cup firm tofu, crumbled and microwaved with a pinch of turmeric until heated through, in place of the scrambled egg.
Do NOT use shredded cheese -- substitute a dairy-free shredded cheese alternative, or omit it.
Swap the bacon bits for the same amount of diced plant-based sausage crumbles, or just omit them -- the beans already carry the protein.
Swap the bacon bits for diced turkey bacon or plant-based bacon bits, or omit them entirely.

name: Stovetop Pancakes from Mix
description: One pan, one box of mix, and enough flipping practice to feel like an actual cook -- this is the recipe that gets you off cereal for good.
steps: In a bowl or large mug, whisk together the pancake mix, egg, milk, and oil until just combined -- a few small lumps are fine, overmixing makes tough pancakes.
Heat a pan over medium heat and melt the butter, tilting the pan to coat the bottom.
Pour about 1/4 cup of batter per pancake into the hot pan, leaving space between them.
Cook for 2-3 minutes until bubbles form across the surface and the edges look dry, then flip.
Cook the second side for another 1-2 minutes until golden and cooked through -- cut one open if you're unsure; it should look dry and fluffy inside, not wet or shiny.
Repeat with the remaining batter, adding a little more butter to the pan between batches, and serve warm.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular pancake mix -- substitute a certified gluten-free pancake mix, prepared the same way.
Do NOT use egg -- substitute 1 mashed ripe banana, or 1 tablespoon ground flaxseed stirred into 3 tablespoons water and left to sit for 5 minutes before adding.
Do NOT use milk or butter -- substitute unsweetened soy or oat milk in the same amount, and use vegetable oil in the pan instead of butter.

name: Breakfast Fried Rice with Egg
description: Day-old rice, a scrambled egg, and whatever frozen vegetables you've got -- the recipe that made me stop throwing out leftover rice.
steps: Heat the oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Add the frozen vegetables straight from frozen and cook, stirring occasionally, for 3-4 minutes until thawed and starting to brown.
Push the vegetables to one side of the pan, crack the eggs into the empty space, and scramble them until fully set with no runny liquid, about 1-2 minutes.

Add the cold rice and diced ham, breaking up any rice clumps with your spatula, and stir everything together. Diced ham is a refrigerated deli-style item -- keep it refrigerated and use it within a few days of opening the package.
Cook for 4-5 minutes, stirring often, until the rice is heated through and starting to crisp slightly in spots.

Stir in the soy sauce, top with green onion, and serve hot -- if using leftover rice, make sure it was refrigerated within 2 hours of first cooking, and reheat it until steaming hot all the way through for food safety.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use egg -- substitute 1/2 cup drained canned chickpeas stirred in with the rice for protein and texture.
Do NOT use soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos, or a pinch of salt with a small splash of rice vinegar.
Swap the diced ham for diced deli turkey, or omit it and add an extra 1/4 cup frozen vegetables or chickpeas instead.
Swap the diced ham for diced deli turkey or plant-based ham, or omit it entirely.

name: One-Pan Tomato & Egg Skillet
description: A dorm-budget take on shakshuka -- one pan of canned tomatoes doing all the work while eggs poach right on top.
steps: Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat, then add the canned tomatoes (juice included), garlic powder, onion powder, and chili flakes.
Simmer, stirring occasionally, for 5-6 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Use a spoon to make 3 small wells in the sauce, then crack one egg into each well.

Cover the pan (a plate or another pan lid works if you don't have a matching lid) and cook over low heat for 6-8 minutes, until the egg whites are fully set and opaque with no clear or runny patches, and the yolks are cooked to your preference -- for food safety, the whites must be fully set with no jiggle or translucency.
Sprinkle with crumbled feta, and serve straight from the pan with toasted bread for scooping.

alternateRecipe.name: Dorm Chickpea Tomato Skillet
alternateRecipe.description: Same one-pan tomato base, but canned chickpeas do the job eggs usually do -- still warm, still scoopable with bread.
steps: Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat, then add the canned tomatoes, chickpeas, garlic powder, onion powder, and chili flakes.
Simmer, stirring occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until the sauce thickens and the chickpeas are heated through.
Sprinkle with crumbled feta and serve straight from the pan with toasted bread for scooping.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use feta cheese -- substitute a dairy-free feta-style crumble, or omit it.
Do NOT use regular bread for serving -- substitute a certified gluten-free bread, toasted the same way, or serve over rice instead.

name: Microwave Rice & Bean Burrito Bowl
description: My go-to when I've got $3 and a microwave -- canned beans and instant rice turn into a filling bowl with almost no cleanup.
steps: In a microwave-safe bowl or mug, combine instant rice and water. Cover loosely (a plate on top works if you don't have a lid) and microwave 5 minutes, or per your rice package's directions.
Before opening, check the canned beans aren't bulging, leaking, or badly dented -- skip it and use a different can if it is.
Drain the canned beans (no colander? hold the lid ajar over the sink and pour slowly) and stir them into the hot rice along with the salsa.
Microwave another 1-2 minutes until everything is steaming hot all the way through.
Top with cheese and hot sauce. Let it sit 1 minute so the cheese melts from the residual heat.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy cheddar cheese -- substitute a dairy-free shredded cheese (look for one labeled to actually melt), or just skip the cheese and add extra salsa/hot sauce for flavor.

name: Doctored Instant Ramen with Egg and Frozen Veggies
description: Instant ramen alone won't fill you up until dinner -- cracking an egg into the broth and dumping in a handful of frozen vegetables turns a 60-cent brick into an actual lunch.

ingredients.name: instant ramen noodles with seasoning packet

steps: Bring 2 cups water to a boil in your one pan on the stovetop (or in a microwave-safe bowl, 3-4 minutes on high, checking it doesn't boil over).
Add the frozen vegetables and the noodle brick (without the seasoning packet yet). Cook 3 minutes, breaking up the noodle block with a fork.
Crack the egg directly into the pan and stir gently so it cooks into ribbons in the hot broth -- keep stirring about 1 minute so it's fully cooked through, not runny.
Stir in the seasoning packet and soy sauce off heat. Taste before adding the whole seasoning packet if you're watching sodium.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use wheat ramen noodles -- substitute a certified gluten-free instant noodle or rice noodles, cooked the same way.

Do NOT use a whole egg -- substitute a quarter cup of drained canned black beans or chickpeas stirred in during the last minute just to warm through (they're shelf-stable and need zero prep, unlike tofu).
Do NOT use soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos, which pours and seasons about the same.

name: Peanut Butter Noodle Bowl
description: This is the recipe that convinced my roommate peanut butter belongs in savory food -- cheap spaghetti tossed in a five-ingredient peanut sauce you whisk right in the same pan you boiled the noodles in.
steps: Cook spaghetti in your one pan of boiling water per the package time (usually 9-11 minutes). Drain by holding the lid ajar over the pan and pouring the water off into the sink (careful, it's hot) -- no colander needed.
Return the empty hot pan to low heat. Add peanut butter, soy sauce, water, and sesame oil. Whisk with a fork until smooth, about 1 minute.
Add the frozen vegetables straight from the freezer and stir 3-4 minutes until heated through.
Add the noodles back in and toss until everything's coated.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use wheat spaghetti -- substitute a rice or corn-based gluten-free pasta, cooked per its package (usually a couple minutes less time).
Do NOT use peanut butter -- substitute sunflower seed butter, which mixes into a sauce almost identically.
Do NOT use soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos in the same amount.
Do NOT use sesame oil -- substitute a neutral oil like vegetable oil, since sesame oil here is mainly for flavor, not function.

name: Canned Tuna Salad Pita Pocket
description: No stove, no microwave, just a can opener and a fork -- this is the lunch I make when I don't even want to think about cooking.
steps: Before opening, check the tuna can isn't bulging, leaking, or badly dented -- skip it and use a different can if it is.
Drain the tuna well (press it against the can lid with a fork to squeeze out extra liquid -- no colander needed).
In a mug or bowl, flake the tuna apart with a fork and stir in mayonnaise, thawed corn, and pepper.
Warm the pita 15 seconds in the microwave if you want it soft, then split it open and stuff with the tuna salad.
Food safety note: since this is a mayo-based salad, don't leave it out more than 2 hours at room temperature, and refrigerate leftovers right away.

alternateRecipe.name: Canned Chicken Salad Pita Pocket
alternateRecipe.description: Swap the can of tuna for a can of chicken breast and you get basically the same 5-minute no-cook lunch, just without the fish.
steps: Before opening, check the chicken can isn't bulging, leaking, or badly dented -- skip it and use a different can if it is.
Drain the canned chicken well and flake it apart with a fork in a mug or bowl.
Stir in mayonnaise, thawed corn, and pepper until combined.
Warm the pita for 15 seconds in the microwave if you like it soft, then stuff with the chicken salad.
Food safety note: since this is a mayo-based salad, don't leave it out more than 2 hours at room temperature, and refrigerate leftovers right away.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular mayonnaise -- substitute an egg-free mayo alternative (many store brands are egg-free now) or plain mustard mixed with a splash of oil.
Do NOT use a wheat pita -- substitute a corn tortilla or gluten-free wrap, or just eat the tuna salad over rice instead.

name: Skillet Bean & Cheese Quesadilla
description: One pan, one flip, and you've got a crispy, cheesy lunch for under two dollars -- the trick is medium-low heat so the tortilla crisps before the cheese scorches.
steps: Before opening the can of beans, check it isn't bulging, leaking, or badly dented -- skip it and use a different can if it is.
Heat oil in your one pan over medium-low heat.
Lay one tortilla flat in the pan. Scatter cheese and beans evenly over half of it, then fold the tortilla in half (or top with the second tortilla if using two).
Cook 3-4 minutes per side, pressing down gently with a spatula (or the back of a fork), until golden and the cheese is melted through.
Slide onto a plate, cut into wedges, and serve with salsa for dipping.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use flour tortillas -- substitute corn tortillas, which crisp up in the same pan just as well (use two smaller ones stacked since they're usually smaller).
Do NOT use dairy cheddar cheese -- substitute a dairy-free shredded cheese labeled to melt (check the bag -- not all do), or skip the cheese and rely on the beans and salsa for flavor.

name: One-Pan Egg Fried Rice
description: This is the first "real" recipe I ever learned that made me feel like I could actually cook -- day-old rice, a couple eggs, and whatever frozen vegetables are in the freezer, all in one pan.
steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in your one pan over medium-high heat. Crack the eggs into the pan, scramble until just set (about 1 minute), then scoop onto a plate and set aside.
Add the remaining oil to the same pan. Add the frozen peas and carrots straight from the freezer and cook 3-4 minutes, stirring, until thawed and hot.

Add the cold rice, breaking up clumps with your spatula. Stir-fry 4-5 minutes until heated through and starting to get a little crispy in spots -- cold, day-old rice fries up better than fresh because it's drier.

Stir the eggs back in, add soy sauce, and toss together. Top with sliced green onion. Since this reheats egg and rice together, eat right away or refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours and reheat until steaming hot before eating again.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use egg -- substitute a half cup of drained canned chickpeas or black beans stirred in with the rice to warm through (they're shelf-stable and need zero prep, unlike tofu).
Do NOT use soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos in the same amount.

name: Budget Shrimp Ramen Stir-Fry
description: A bag of frozen pre-cooked shrimp is one of the few "fancy" proteins that's actually cheap and doesn't spoil before you get around to using it -- this turns a ramen brick into something that feels like takeout.
steps: Boil the ramen noodles in your one pan of water for 3 minutes (skip the seasoning packet). Drain by holding the lid ajar over the pan and pouring the water out, or scoop the noodles into a bowl with a fork.
In the same pan, heat sesame oil over medium-high heat. Add the frozen vegetables and cook 3-4 minutes until hot.

Add the thawed shrimp and garlic powder. Cook 2-3 minutes, stirring, until the shrimp is heated through and opaque (about 145 degF/63 degC) -- don't overcook or it gets rubbery, since it's already pre-cooked.
Add the noodles back in with the soy sauce and toss everything together for 1 minute.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use wheat ramen noodles -- substitute rice noodles or a certified gluten-free noodle, cooked according to its package time (usually shorter than ramen).

alternateRecipe.name: Budget Chicken Ramen Stir-Fry
alternateRecipe.description: Same one-pan stir-fry, but chicken instead of shrimp for anyone with a shellfish allergy -- just cook the chicken all the way through before adding anything else.

ingredients.name: boneless chicken thigh, cut into small pieces

steps: Heat a splash of oil in your one pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken pieces and cook, stirring, 6-7 minutes until no longer pink and it reaches 165 degF/74 degC inside (cut a piece open to check if you don't have a thermometer -- juices should run clear).
Meanwhile, boil the ramen noodles in a separate pot of water for 3 minutes, then drain by holding the lid ajar over the pan.
Add the frozen vegetables to the chicken pan and cook 3-4 minutes until hot.
Add the drained noodles, soy sauce, sesame oil, and garlic powder. Toss everything together over heat for 1-2 minutes.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos in the same amount.
Do NOT use sesame oil -- substitute a neutral cooking oil.

name: Soy-Sesame Chicken & Rice Bowl
description: This is my "I actually have $8 and want to feel like an adult" lunch -- cheap chicken thighs, instant rice, and a sauce made from three pantry bottles.
steps: Cut chicken thigh into bite-sized pieces. Heat a splash of oil in your one pan over medium-high heat and cook the chicken 6-8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until it reaches 165 degF/74 degC inside and no longer looks pink (cut into the thickest piece to check if you don't have a thermometer).
While the chicken cooks, combine instant rice and water in a microwave-safe bowl, cover loosely, and microwave 5 minutes.
Add the frozen broccoli to the chicken pan and cook 3-4 minutes until bright green and hot through.
Stir in soy sauce, sesame oil, and garlic powder. Cook 1 more minute, then serve over the rice.

adaptations.instructions: If you don't eat chicken, substitute an equal amount of drained canned chickpeas added in the last 3 minutes just to warm through, skipping the raw-cook step entirely.
Do NOT use soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos in the same amount.
Do NOT use sesame oil -- substitute a neutral cooking oil.

name: One-Pan Rice & Beans Skillet
description: Rice, canned beans, and whatever frozen veggies you've got, all in one pan -- this is the recipe I make when my wallet's tight and I don't want to wash three dishes.
steps: Check your canned beans and tomatoes for bulging, leaking, or heavy denting before opening -- skip any can showing these signs, they can mean the contents have spoiled.
Heat the oil in your one pan over medium heat.
Add the rice and stir for a minute so it gets coated -- this keeps it from clumping.
Add the water, cover (a plate works if you don't have a lid), bring to a boil, then turn heat down to low. Simmer 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
Stir in the drained black beans, diced tomatoes (with their juice), frozen corn, chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, and salt.
Cover again and cook another 5-8 minutes until the rice is fully tender and everything's heated through.
Turn off the heat, sprinkle cheese on top if using, and let it sit covered for 2 minutes to melt. Makes 3-4 servings and usually costs under $6 for the whole pan.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular shredded cheddar if avoiding dairy -- substitute a dairy-free shredded cheese, or just skip the cheese; the dish holds up fine without it.

name: Microwave Mug Chili
description: One microwave-safe bowl, no stovetop needed -- built for the nights the communal kitchen is a war zone or you just don't have one.

ingredients.name: frozen bell pepper and onion mix

steps: Check your canned beans and tomatoes for bulging, leaking, or heavy denting before opening -- skip any can showing these signs.
Combine the drained kidney beans, diced tomatoes, frozen pepper/onion mix, chili powder, cumin, and garlic powder in a large microwave-safe bowl or two mugs.

Microwave uncovered on high for 3 minutes, stir, then microwave another 3-5 minutes until bubbling and the peppers are soft. Microwaves vary a lot, so check at the 3-minute mark and add time as needed.
Let it sit for 1 minute before eating -- food straight out of the microwave can be much hotter than the bowl feels.
Top with cheese and crushed tortilla chips if you've got them. Feeds 1 hungry person or 2 modest servings, usually under $3 total.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular shredded cheddar -- substitute a dairy-free shredded cheese, or skip the topping entirely.

name: Ramen Upgrade Bowl
description: Instant ramen is basically free, so I dump in an egg and whatever frozen veggies are in the freezer to make it an actual meal instead of just salty noodles.

ingredients.name: instant ramen noodles with seasoning packet

steps: Bring the water to a boil in your pan.
Add the frozen vegetables and cook 2 minutes.
Add the ramen noodles and half the seasoning packet (save the rest for next time, or use it all if you like it salty). Cook 3 minutes, stirring so the block breaks apart.

Crack the egg directly into the pan and let it sit without stirring for about 90 seconds so it starts to set, then gently stir it through the broth for ribbons of cooked egg. If you'd rather have a whole poached egg, drop it in whole and let it sit untouched in the broth for 4-5 minutes.
Stir in the soy sauce and sesame oil off heat. The egg should look fully set with no runny, glossy, or translucent parts -- if it does, cook another 30 seconds.
Top with green onion. Costs under $2 with a decent ramen brand and a single egg.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular wheat ramen -- substitute a rice-noodle ramen or a gluten-free instant noodle brand (widely available now at most grocery stores).
Do NOT use egg -- substitute 1/2 cup drained, cubed firm tofu stirred in with the vegetables to add protein instead.

Do NOT use regular soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos or a soy-free tamari alternative. Also double-check your ramen seasoning packet's label: most brands' seasoning base includes soy sauce powder or hydrolyzed soy protein, so use only half the packet (or none) and season instead with garlic powder, a pinch of salt, and pepper, or a confirmed soy-free bouillon.
Do NOT use sesame oil -- substitute a small drizzle of vegetable oil; you'll lose some of the nutty flavor but the dish still works.

name: Microwave Baked Potato Bar
description: No oven required -- a potato in the microwave gets you the same soft, fluffy inside in 12 minutes instead of an hour, and you load it up like a cheap taco night.

ingredients.name: canned black beans, drained and warmed

steps: Check your can of black beans for bulging, leaking, or heavy denting before opening -- skip it if you see any of these.
Wash the potatoes and poke each one 6-8 times with a fork -- this lets steam escape so it doesn't build up pressure and split the potato open in the microwave.

Microwave on high for 5 minutes, flip, then microwave another 5-7 minutes until a fork slides into the center easily with no resistance. Time varies a lot by microwave wattage and potato size, so check at 5 minutes and add time in 2-minute bursts.
While the potatoes cook, microwave the frozen broccoli in a separate microwave-safe bowl with a splash of water, covered, for 3 minutes until tender.
Microwave the black beans in a mug for 1 minute until warm.
Split the potatoes open, fluff the inside with a fork, and season with salt and pepper.
Top with beans, broccoli, cheese, and sour cream. Two loaded potatoes makes a full dinner for about $3.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular cheddar and sour cream -- substitute dairy-free shredded cheese and a dairy-free sour cream alternative, or skip both and lean on the beans and broccoli for toppings.

name: Instant Mac and "Cheese" Bowl
description: Real elbow macaroni with real melted cheese, made in one pan with no strainer -- you drain it by holding the lid ajar over the sink.
steps: Bring the water to a boil in your pan and add a pinch of salt.
Add the macaroni and cook 8-9 minutes, stirring occasionally so it doesn't stick, until tender.
If using frozen peas, stir them in for the last 2 minutes of cooking.
Carry the pan to the sink, hold the lid ajar with an oven mitt or towel so there's just a gap, and pour off most of the water, leaving about 2 tablespoons in the pan -- no colander needed.
Return the pan to low heat and stir in the butter, milk, and cheese until melted and creamy, about 2 minutes. Season with salt to taste.
Serves 2-3 and costs about $3 a batch, less than the boxed stuff.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular elbow macaroni -- substitute a gluten-free elbow pasta; check the cook time on the box since gluten-free pasta often needs a minute or two less.
Do NOT use regular butter, milk, and cheddar -- substitute a plant-based butter, unsweetened plain non-dairy milk, and a dairy-free shredded cheese.

name: Dorm Fried Rice with Egg
description: The move for leftover rice that's about to go stale -- cold rice actually fries up better than fresh because it's drier and doesn't turn to mush in the pan.

ingredients.name: cooked rice, day-old and cold if possible

steps: Heat the vegetable oil in your pan over medium-high heat.
Add the frozen vegetables and cook 3-4 minutes, stirring, until thawed and starting to brown a little at the edges.
Push the vegetables to one side of the pan. Crack both eggs into the empty side and scramble with your spatula until fully set -- no runny or glossy parts left, about 90 seconds.
Add the cold rice, breaking up clumps with the spatula. Stir everything together and cook 4-5 minutes, pressing the rice into the pan occasionally so it gets a little crispy in spots.
Add the soy sauce, sesame oil, and garlic powder. Stir to coat evenly and cook 1 more minute.
Top with green onion. Makes 2 servings and is a great way to use up rice you cooked earlier in the week instead of tossing it.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use egg -- substitute 1/2 cup drained, crumbled firm tofu stirred in with the vegetables for protein.
Do NOT use regular soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos or a soy-free tamari alternative.
Do NOT use sesame oil -- substitute a small drizzle of extra vegetable oil.

name: One-Pot Tomato Pasta with White Beans
description: Pasta, a can of tomatoes, and a can of beans -- everything cooks in the same pot, so there's one pan to wash and dinner's ready in 20 minutes.
steps: Check your cans of crushed tomatoes and white beans for bulging, leaking, or heavy denting before opening -- skip any can showing these signs.
Break the spaghetti in half so it fits in the pan, then add it along with the crushed tomatoes, water, garlic powder, oregano, basil, olive oil, and salt.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring occasionally so the pasta doesn't stick together or to the bottom.
Reduce heat to a strong simmer and cook 10-12 minutes, stirring every couple minutes, until the pasta is tender and most of the liquid has thickened into a sauce.
Stir in the drained white beans and cook 2 more minutes until warmed through.
Top with parmesan if using. Makes 3-4 servings and usually costs around $5 total.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular spaghetti -- substitute a gluten-free spaghetti; it can break down a bit more in the sauce, so cook it a minute or two less than the package says and check for doneness early.
Do NOT use parmesan cheese -- substitute a dairy-free parmesan alternative or a sprinkle of nutritional yeast, or just skip it.

name: Canned Tuna Melt Skillet
description: A grilled-cheese-and-tuna mashup made entirely in a skillet, no broiler or oven needed -- flip it like a grilled cheese and the cheese still melts fine.
steps: Check your can of tuna for bulging, leaking, or heavy denting before opening -- skip it if you see any of these.

In a mug or small bowl, mix the drained tuna with the mayonnaise, celery if using, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Once mixed with mayo, this filling isn't shelf-stable anymore -- keep any leftovers refrigerated and eat within a day.
Butter one side of each bread slice. Spread the tuna mixture on the unbuttered side of two slices, top with cheese, then close with the remaining two slices, buttered side out.

Heat your pan over medium-low heat (too hot and the outside burns before the cheese melts). Place the sandwiches in the pan and cook 3-4 minutes per side, pressing down gently with the spatula, until golden brown and the cheese is fully melted.
Cut in half and serve. Makes 2 sandwiches for around $4 using a store-brand tuna can.

alternateRecipe.name: Canned Chicken Melt
alternateRecipe.description: Same grilled-cheese method, swapped to canned chicken breast for anyone steering clear of fish -- just as cheap and just as fast.
steps: Check your can of chicken for bulging, leaking, or heavy denting before opening -- skip it if you see any of these.

In a mug or small bowl, mix the drained canned chicken with the mayonnaise, celery if using, and a pinch of salt and pepper. Once mixed with mayo, keep any leftovers refrigerated and eat within a day.
Butter one side of each bread slice. Spread the chicken mixture on the unbuttered side of two slices, top with cheese, then close with the remaining two slices, buttered side out.
Heat your pan over medium-low heat. Cook the sandwiches 3-4 minutes per side, pressing down gently, until golden and the cheese is fully melted.
Cut in half and serve. Makes 2 sandwiches.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular bread -- substitute a gluten-free bread; toast it a little longer than usual since gluten-free bread tends to be denser.
Do NOT use regular cheddar and butter -- substitute a dairy-free shredded cheese and a dairy-free margarine or oil for cooking.
Do NOT use regular mayonnaise -- substitute an egg-free mayo alternative or mashed avocado.

name: Black Bean Quesadillas
description: Flour tortillas folded over beans and cheese, crisped in a dry-ish pan -- one of the fastest hot dinners you can make with a $1 can of beans.
steps: Check your can of black beans for bulging, leaking, or heavy denting before opening -- skip it if you see any of these.
In a mug or bowl, lightly mash the drained black beans with cumin and salt (doesn't need to be smooth, just broken up a bit).
Microwave the frozen corn in a separate bowl for 90 seconds to thaw, or stir it in raw -- it'll cook through in the pan.
Spread the bean mixture, corn, and cheese over one half of each tortilla, then fold the other half over.
Heat the oil in your pan over medium heat. Cook each folded quesadilla 2-3 minutes per side, pressing down with the spatula, until golden and crisp and the cheese is fully melted.
Slice into wedges. Makes 4 quesadillas (2 servings) for about $3.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use flour tortillas -- substitute corn tortillas, which are naturally gluten-free; use two stacked per quesadilla since they're smaller and tear more easily.
Do NOT use regular shredded cheddar -- substitute a dairy-free shredded cheese.

name: Lentil Soup One-Pot
description: Dried red lentils cook down soft in under 25 minutes with no soaking -- this is the cheapest hot meal in my rotation, usually under $2 for the whole pot.
steps: Check your can of diced tomatoes for bulging, leaking, or heavy denting before opening -- skip it if you see any of these.
Heat the olive oil in your pan over medium heat, then add the garlic powder and cumin and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the rinsed lentils, diced tomatoes, water, and bouillon cube. Stir to break up the bouillon cube as it dissolves.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally so nothing sticks to the bottom, for 20 minutes.
Add the frozen vegetables and simmer another 5-8 minutes until the lentils are fully soft and starting to break apart and the vegetables are tender.
Season with salt to taste. Makes about 4 servings and reheats well for lunch the next day.

name: Peanut Noodle Stir-Fry
description: A cheap peanut sauce turns plain noodles into something that actually tastes like takeout -- this one takes a bit more juggling than my usual recipes since you're managing sauce, noodles, and vegetables at once.

ingredients.name: spaghetti (or ramen noodles, seasoning packet discarded)

steps: Cook the noodles in a pot of boiling water according to the package time, usually 8-10 minutes. Drain by holding the lid ajar over the sink -- no colander needed -- and set the noodles aside.

While the noodles cook, whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, sesame oil, garlic powder, ginger, and water together in a mug until smooth. If it's too thick to stir, microwave the mug for 15 seconds to loosen the peanut butter first.
Wipe out the pot, add a splash of oil, and cook the frozen vegetables over medium-high heat 4-5 minutes until tender.
Add the drained noodles back to the pot along with the peanut sauce. Toss everything together over low heat for 1-2 minutes until evenly coated and warmed through.
Top with crushed peanuts if using. Makes 2-3 servings.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular wheat spaghetti or ramen -- substitute rice noodles or a gluten-free noodle.
Do NOT use peanut butter or crushed peanuts -- substitute sunflower seed butter (nut-free) for the sauce and skip the peanut topping entirely.
Do NOT use regular soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos or a soy-free tamari alternative.
Do NOT use sesame oil -- substitute a small drizzle of extra vegetable oil.

name: Skillet Chicken Thighs with Rice
description: Boneless chicken thighs are cheaper than breasts and harder to dry out, which matters a lot when you're still learning to judge doneness by eye.
steps: Pat the chicken thighs dry with a paper towel and season both sides with salt, pepper, garlic powder, and paprika.
Heat the oil in your pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken and cook 5-6 minutes per side until browned.

Chicken is safe to eat once it reaches 165°F/74°C internally. If you don't have a meat thermometer, cut into the thickest piece: the meat should be opaque all the way through with no pink, and the juices should run clear, not pink or red.
Remove the chicken to a plate and set aside. Add the rice to the same pan, stirring to pick up the browned bits, then add the water or broth.
Nestle the chicken back into the pan on top of the rice, cover (a plate works as a lid), and simmer on low for 15-18 minutes until the rice is tender and has absorbed the liquid.
Stir in the frozen vegetables for the last 5 minutes of cooking, covered, until heated through. Makes 3-4 servings.
