Fold the dry ingredients into the wet mixture in two additions, alternating with the oat milk.
Pour the batter into the prepared dish and bake 30-35 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Let the cake cool completely, then poke holes all over with a fork.
Whisk together the coconut milk and sweetened condensed coconut milk, and slowly pour over the cake, letting it soak in.
Chill at least 2 hours (overnight is best).
Top with whipped chilled coconut cream before serving, dusted with cinnamon.

name: Salted Caramel Coconut Flan
description: A caramel-bottomed custard built on coconut milk alongside the traditional condensed and evaporated dairy -- coconut milk is already doing half the work, so going fully dairy-free is a short trip, listed as its own version below.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and set a kettle of water to boil for the water bath.
Melt the sugar with the water in a saucepan over medium heat, swirling (don't stir) until it turns deep amber.
Immediately pour the caramel into a 9-inch round baking dish or flan mold, tilting to coat the bottom.
Whisk together the condensed milk, evaporated milk, coconut milk, eggs, and vanilla until smooth.
Strain the custard through a fine-mesh sieve into the caramel-lined dish.
Set the dish inside a larger roasting pan and pour the boiling water halfway up the sides.
Bake 50-60 minutes, until the center is just set but still slightly jiggly.
Cool to room temperature, then chill at least 4 hours or overnight.
Run a knife around the edge, invert onto a serving plate, and finish with flaky sea salt.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use eggs -- substitute a slurry of 1/4 cup cornstarch whisked into the milk mixture plus 1 teaspoon agar-agar powder, brought to a brief simmer to activate, for an eggless set; the texture will be a touch firmer than classic flan.

alternateRecipe.name: All-Coconut Flan (Dairy-Free)
alternateRecipe.description: Same caramel-bottomed custard technique, built entirely on coconut milk in place of the condensed and evaporated dairy milks.

ingredients.name: sweetened condensed coconut milk (store-bought vegan condensed milk)

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C) and set a kettle of water to boil for the water bath.
Melt the sugar with the water in a saucepan over medium heat, swirling (don't stir) until it turns deep amber.
Immediately pour the caramel into a 9-inch round baking dish or flan mold, tilting to coat the bottom.
Whisk together the coconut milk, sweetened condensed coconut milk, eggs, and vanilla until smooth.
Strain the custard through a fine-mesh sieve into the caramel-lined dish.
Set the dish inside a larger roasting pan and pour the boiling water halfway up the sides.
Bake 50-60 minutes, until the center is just set but still slightly jiggly.
Cool to room temperature, then chill at least 4 hours or overnight.
Run a knife around the edge, invert onto a serving plate, and finish with flaky sea salt.

name: Toasted Coconut Rice Krispie Treats
description: My abuela's rice krispie treats got a beach-vacation upgrade -- toasted coconut folded right into the marshmallow and pressed on top, so every bite has that little bit of crunch and coconut smell.
steps: Toast the shredded coconut in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirring often, until golden, 3-4 minutes; set aside.
Melt the butter in a large pot over low heat.
Add the marshmallows and stir until fully melted and smooth.
Remove from heat, stir in vanilla and half the toasted coconut.
Fold in the rice cereal until evenly coated.
Press the mixture into a greased 9x13 pan, sprinkle with remaining coconut and sea salt, and press gently to set.
Let cool 20 minutes before cutting into bars.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy butter -- substitute a plant-based butter or coconut oil in the same amount.

Do NOT use standard marshmallows -- substitute a vegetarian marshmallow made with agar-agar instead of gelatin (widely available at natural grocers); the gelatin in ordinary marshmallows is usually beef- or pork-derived.
Do NOT use standard crisped rice cereal -- substitute a certified gluten-free crisped rice cereal in the same measurement.

name: Skillet S'mores Dip
description: One skillet, four ingredients, ten minutes -- this is the treat I hand a kid who wants to 'help cook' without actually needing supervision on a stove full of hot oil.
steps: Preheat oven to 450F.
Grease a 10-inch cast iron skillet with the butter.
Spread the chocolate chips evenly across the bottom of the skillet.
Cover the chocolate completely with a layer of mini marshmallows.
Bake 8-10 minutes, until the marshmallows are puffed and golden on top.
Sprinkle with flaky sea salt and serve immediately with graham crackers for dipping.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use standard chocolate chips (most contain soy lecithin) -- substitute a soy-free dark chocolate bar, chopped, confirmed soy-free on the label.
Do NOT use standard marshmallows -- substitute a vegetarian, agar-agar-set marshmallow; ordinary gelatin marshmallows are usually beef- or pork-derived.
Do NOT use butter to grease the skillet -- substitute a neutral oil or vegan butter.
Do NOT use standard graham crackers -- substitute a certified gluten-free graham-style cracker for dipping.

name: Key Lime Pie Bars
description: All the tang of a Florida key lime pie, cut into bars so nobody's fighting over pie-slice geometry -- I make these every time the limes at the store actually look good.
steps: Preheat oven to 350F. Line an 8x8 pan with parchment.
Mix graham crumbs, melted butter, and sugar; press firmly into the pan.
Bake crust 8 minutes, then let cool slightly.
Whisk condensed milk, egg yolks, lime juice, and zest until smooth.
Pour filling over the crust.
Bake 15 minutes, until the center is just set with a slight jiggle.
Cool to room temperature, then chill at least 3 hours before slicing.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use standard graham cracker crumbs -- substitute a certified gluten-free graham-style crumb in the same measurement.
Do NOT use dairy butter and condensed milk -- substitute vegan butter and a canned coconut condensed milk (widely available) in equal amounts.
Do NOT use egg yolks -- substitute 3 tablespoons cornstarch whisked into the condensed milk to thicken the filling before baking; chill until fully set.

name: Mango Sticky Rice with Toasted Sesame
description: This is the dessert I order every time I see it on a menu, so I finally learned to make it at home -- the sesame on top isn't traditional everywhere, but I like the extra crunch against the soft rice.
steps: Soak the sticky rice in water at least 4 hours or overnight; drain well.
Steam the rice over simmering water, covered, for about 25 minutes, until tender and translucent.
Warm the coconut milk with sugar and salt over low heat until dissolved; reserve a few tablespoons for drizzling.
Fold most of the warm coconut milk into the hot cooked rice; let it sit and absorb for 10 minutes.
Plate the rice with sliced mango, drizzle with the reserved coconut milk, and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use sesame seeds -- simply omit the garnish (the dish works fine without it); if a crunchy topping is wanted, use toasted crushed peanuts instead, but check for a nut allergy first since that introduces a different allergen.

name: Churro Bites with Chocolate-Sea Salt Dip
description: Real choux dough, fried in small pieces so you skip the piping-bag stress of full-size churros -- I started making these bite-sized after one too many kitchen mishaps with hot oil and a pastry bag at the same time.
steps: Bring water, butter, 1 tablespoon sugar, and salt to a boil in a saucepan.
Remove from heat and stir in the flour vigorously until a smooth dough ball forms.
Cool the dough 5 minutes, then beat in the eggs one at a time until glossy and smooth (this is choux dough).
Heat oil to 350F in a deep pot.
Pipe or spoon small dough pieces into the hot oil, frying in batches until golden, 3-4 minutes, turning as needed.
Drain on paper towels, then toss warm in cinnamon-sugar.
Warm the heavy cream, pour over chocolate chips, and stir until smooth; sprinkle with flaky sea salt for the dip.
Serve churro bites warm alongside the chocolate dip.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy butter and heavy cream -- substitute vegan butter for the dough and full-fat coconut cream for the dip in equal amounts.
Do NOT use all-purpose flour -- substitute a measure-for-measure gluten-free baking blend; choux dough can be trickier gluten-free, so pipe smaller pieces and fry a touch longer.

alternateRecipe.name: Cinnamon-Sugar Fried Dough Bites (Egg-Free)
alternateRecipe.description: Choux dough leans on eggs for structure and lift, so an egg-free version needs a different dough entirely rather than a one-for-one swap -- this yeasted-biscuit-style dough fries up light and puffy without any eggs, then gets the same cinnamon-sugar toss and chocolate dip.
steps: Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt together.
Stir in the melted butter and milk until a soft, slightly sticky dough forms; do not overmix.
Heat oil to 350F in a deep pot.
Using two spoons, drop small pieces of dough into the hot oil, frying in batches until deep golden and cooked through, 3-4 minutes, turning as needed.
Drain on paper towels, then toss warm in cinnamon-sugar.
Warm the heavy cream, pour over chocolate chips, and stir until smooth; sprinkle with flaky sea salt for the dip.
Serve the bites warm alongside the chocolate dip.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use standard chocolate chips (most contain soy lecithin) -- substitute a confirmed soy-free dark chocolate bar, chopped.

name: Peanut Butter Miso Blondies
description: White miso in the batter sounds like a savory-kitchen accident but it deepens the caramel-peanut flavor into something closer to butterscotch -- worth the extra ingredient hunt at an Asian grocery if your regular store doesn't stock miso.
steps: Preheat oven to 350F. Line a 9x9 pan with parchment.
Whisk peanut butter, melted butter, brown sugar, and miso paste together until smooth and glossy.
Beat in eggs and vanilla until fully incorporated.
Fold in flour, baking powder, and salt just until no streaks remain.
Fold in the chocolate chunks, reserving a few for the top.
Spread batter into the pan and scatter reserved chocolate on top.
Bake 25-30 minutes, until the edges are set and the center has a slight give.
Cool completely in the pan before cutting -- the miso deepens the caramel-nutty flavor as it sits.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use peanut butter -- substitute sunflower seed butter (such as SunButter) in the same amount for a nut-free blondie with similar richness.
Do NOT use dairy butter -- substitute a plant-based butter in equal amount.
Do NOT use soy miso paste or standard chocolate chunks (usually soy lecithin) -- substitute a chickpea miso (soy-free, same umami depth) and a confirmed soy-free dark chocolate.
Do NOT use eggs -- substitute 2 flax eggs (2 tablespoons ground flaxseed plus 6 tablespoons water, rested 5 minutes); blondies will be slightly denser but still fudgy.
Do NOT use all-purpose flour -- substitute a measure-for-measure gluten-free baking blend.

name: Overnight Peanut Butter Banana Oats
description: The lunchbox-that-doubles-as-breakfast move -- stir it together the night before and grab jars on the way out the door, no stove required.
steps: In a jar or container, stir together oats, milk, peanut butter, chia seeds, honey, and cinnamon until the peanut butter is mostly incorporated.
Top with sliced banana, cover, and refrigerate overnight (at least 4 hours).
In the morning, stir well, add a splash more milk if it's too thick, and eat cold or microwave 60-90 seconds if you want it warm.
Batch note: double or triple the base mix (skip the banana until serving) and portion into jars for the whole week -- it holds fine for 4-5 days.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy milk -- substitute unsweetened oat milk or another plant milk of your choice.
Do NOT use peanut butter -- substitute sunflower seed butter to keep it peanut- and tree-nut-free.

name: Freezer Breakfast Burritos
description: This is the recipe that actually saves a weekday morning -- cook the whole batch once on a Sunday and every burrito after that is a 90-second microwave job.
steps: Whisk eggs with milk and a pinch of salt.
Brown the sausage in a large skillet over medium heat, breaking it up, about 6 minutes; add bell pepper and cook 2 more minutes; remove to a bowl.
In the same skillet, scramble the eggs until just set, about 3 minutes.
Lay out tortillas and divide sausage mixture, scrambled eggs, black beans, cheese, and a spoonful of salsa evenly across each.
Roll into burritos, wrap each individually in foil or parchment, and freeze flat.
To reheat: unwrap, microwave 90 seconds to 2 minutes from frozen (or 45 seconds from thawed), flipping halfway.
Batch note: this whole batch is the batch-cook -- one Sunday session buys the whole family breakfast through Friday.

alternateRecipe.name: Tofu Scramble Freezer Burritos
alternateRecipe.description: Same freezer-burrito system, egg-free -- crumbled tofu takes on the sausage seasoning just as well as scrambled eggs did.
steps: Press tofu for 10 minutes, then crumble it into bite-size pieces.
Brown sausage in a large skillet, about 6 minutes; add bell pepper, cook 2 minutes; remove to a bowl.
In the same skillet, add crumbled tofu, turmeric, and nutritional yeast; cook 4-5 minutes until lightly golden (the turmeric gives it an egg-like color).
Combine the tofu scramble with the sausage mixture.
Assemble burritos with tortillas, filling, beans, cheese, and salsa; roll and wrap individually.
Freeze flat; reheat from frozen 90 seconds to 2 minutes in the microwave.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use shredded cheddar and milk -- substitute a dairy-free shredded cheese and unsweetened oat milk.
Do NOT use wheat tortillas -- substitute certified gluten-free tortillas.
Swap the pork breakfast sausage for turkey breakfast sausage or a plant-based sausage crumble.

name: Sheet-Pan Baked Oatmeal Bars
description: One pan, cut into squares, and breakfast is portable for the whole week -- my kids eat these plain and I eat mine with extra peanut butter on top.
steps: Preheat oven to 375F and line a 9x13 pan with parchment.
Mash banana in a large bowl, then whisk in eggs, milk, and maple syrup.
Stir in oats, baking powder, and cinnamon until combined; fold in walnuts.
Pour into the pan, spread evenly, and bake 25-30 minutes until set and golden at the edges.
Cool 10 minutes, then cut into 12 bars.
Batch note: bars freeze well individually wrapped -- pull one out the night before and it's thawed by breakfast.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use egg -- substitute a flax egg (1 tbsp ground flaxseed whisked with 3 tbsp water, rested 5 minutes) per egg.
Do NOT use dairy milk -- substitute oat milk or another unsweetened plant milk.
Do NOT use walnuts -- substitute pepitas (pumpkin seeds) or omit entirely.

name: Greek Yogurt Parfait Jars
description: Zero cooking, five minutes of layering, and it looks fancy enough that nobody complains it's 'just yogurt' -- my go-to when mornings are a disaster.
steps: In four jars or containers, spoon a layer of yogurt, then berries, then a sprinkle of granola and almonds.
Repeat the layers once more, drizzle with honey, and seal.
Refrigerate up to 2 days, or grab and go same-morning.
Batch note: assemble all 4 jars at once on Sunday for grab-and-go breakfasts through midweek -- just keep the granola layer on top so it stays crunchy.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy yogurt -- substitute a plain coconut- or soy-based yogurt.
Do NOT use regular granola -- substitute a certified gluten-free granola.
Do NOT use sliced almonds -- substitute toasted sunflower seeds.

name: Whole Wheat Banana Pancakes with Make-Ahead Dry Mix
description: I keep a jar of the dry mix pre-measured in the pantry so pancake morning is just 'add wet ingredients and go' -- no more measuring flour at 7am.
steps: Whisk flour, baking powder, and cinnamon together (this is the make-ahead dry mix -- can be jarred and stored up to a month).
In a separate bowl, whisk eggs, milk, mashed banana, melted butter, and maple syrup.
Pour wet into dry and stir just until combined (a few lumps are fine).
Heat a griddle over medium heat; pour 1/4-cup portions and cook 2-3 minutes per side until golden and bubbles form.
Serve immediately, or cool and freeze between parchment sheets for weekday toaster reheats.
Batch note: double the dry mix now, portion into two jars, and next pancake morning is a 10-minute job.

alternateRecipe.name: Gluten-Free Banana Oat Pancakes
alternateRecipe.description: Certified gluten-free oat flour swaps in one-for-one here -- same fluffy banana pancake, no wheat.
steps: Whisk gluten-free oat flour, baking powder, and cinnamon together.
In a separate bowl, whisk eggs, milk, mashed banana, melted butter, and maple syrup.
Pour wet into dry and stir just until combined; let batter rest 5 minutes so the oat flour hydrates.
Heat a griddle over medium heat; pour 1/4-cup portions and cook 2-3 minutes per side until golden.
Serve immediately or freeze between parchment sheets for weekday toaster reheats.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use egg -- substitute a flax egg (1 tbsp ground flaxseed whisked with 3 tbsp water, rested 5 minutes) per egg.
Do NOT use dairy milk and butter -- substitute oat milk and a neutral oil or dairy-free butter.

name: Breakfast Fried Rice with Egg and Sausage
description: The answer to 'what do we do with last night's rice' -- a genuinely fast, one-pan breakfast that uses up a fridge staple instead of wasting it.
steps: Heat a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat; cook sausage/ham until browned, about 4 minutes, then push to one side.
Push protein aside, crack eggs into the empty space, and scramble until just set, about 1 minute.
Add cold rice, peas and carrots, and garlic; stir-fry, breaking up rice clumps, about 4 minutes.
Add soy sauce and sesame oil, tossing to coat evenly; cook 1-2 more minutes.
Top with scallions and serve hot.
Batch note: the leftover-rice base is the batch component -- cook a double batch of rice earlier in the week specifically to have this ready any morning.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use egg -- substitute extra-firm tofu crumbled and scrambled the same way for the protein and moisture.
Swap the pork sausage or ham for diced cooked chicken sausage, or omit and add extra vegetables.
Do NOT use soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos to keep the dish soy-free.
Do NOT use regular soy sauce -- substitute tamari labeled gluten-free or coconut aminos.
Do NOT use sesame oil -- substitute a neutral oil such as avocado or vegetable oil.

name: Turkey Hummus Ranch Wrap
description: Zero cooking, five minutes of assembly -- I roll a stack of these on Sunday and the kids grab one on the way out the door all week.
steps: Lay each tortilla flat and spread with hummus, leaving a half-inch border.
Layer turkey, a cheese slice, lettuce, and carrot down the center.
Drizzle with ranch, fold in the sides, and roll tightly.
Slice in half on the diagonal and pack, or wrap whole in foil for lunch boxes.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use a wheat tortilla -- substitute a certified gluten-free tortilla, or skip the wrap and layer everything in large butter lettuce leaves instead.
Do NOT use regular hummus (made with tahini) -- substitute a tahini-free hummus, such as one made with white beans or avocado, or plain mashed avocado.
Do NOT use dairy ranch dressing or cheese -- substitute a dairy-free ranch and a dairy-free cheese slice, or skip the cheese and add extra veggies.
Swap the turkey for canned chickpeas mashed with a little olive oil and lemon, or sliced roasted chicken if that's what's on hand.

name: Mediterranean Chickpea Mason Jar Salad
description: Dressing on the bottom, chickpeas on top so nothing goes soggy by Wednesday -- I make four jars at once Sunday night and lunch is a non-decision for the rest of the week.
steps: Whisk olive oil, vinegar, and oregano; spoon 1 tablespoon of dressing into the bottom of each of 4 mason jars.
Layer chickpeas, then onion, tomatoes, cucumber, olives, and feta on top, keeping the layers separate from the dressing until serving.
Seal and refrigerate up to 5 days.
To eat, shake the jar to distribute the dressing and pour into a bowl.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy feta -- substitute a dairy-free feta-style crumble, or leave it out and add extra olives for the same salty hit.

name: Egg Salad Sandwiches
description: Boil a full dozen eggs Sunday and this lunch is five minutes of chopping and stirring any day that week -- my go-to when the fridge otherwise looks bare.
steps: Place eggs in a pot, cover with water, bring to a boil, then cover and remove from heat for 12 minutes.
Cool eggs in ice water, then peel and chop.
Mix chopped eggs with mayonnaise, celery, mustard, salt, and pepper.
Spread on bread and serve, or chill the filling separately for up to 4 days.

alternateRecipe.name: Mashed Chickpea "Egg-Free" Salad Sandwiches
alternateRecipe.description: All the creamy, tangy egg-salad flavor without a single egg -- mashed chickpeas give the same forkable texture and a pinch of turmeric brings back that familiar yellow color.
steps: Drain and rinse chickpeas, then mash coarsely with a fork, leaving some texture.
Stir in vegan mayonnaise, celery, onion, mustard, turmeric, salt, and pepper.
Spread on bread and serve, or chill up to 4 days.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use wheat bread -- substitute a certified gluten-free bread or serve the egg salad over greens instead.

name: Next-Day Fajita Chicken Lunch Bowls
description: Built entirely from Tuesday's leftover roasted chicken and peppers reheated over fresh rice -- this is the exact reason I always roast double on fajita night.
steps: Reheat chicken and peppers in a skillet with cumin and chili powder until warmed through, about 6 minutes.
Warm the rice in the microwave or a second pan.
Divide rice among bowls, top with the chicken and pepper mixture and cheese.
Finish with a dollop of sour cream and a squeeze of lime.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the chicken for black beans or extra roasted vegetables to make it a vegetarian bowl.
Do NOT use dairy cheese or sour cream -- substitute a dairy-free cheese and dairy-free sour cream, or skip both and add extra avocado.

name: Weeknight Leftover Fried Rice
description: This is where a big batch-cooked pot of rice goes to get a second life -- one skillet, whatever protein and frozen veg are in the freezer, done before the kids finish setting the table.
steps: Heat a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat, scramble the eggs, and set aside.
Add a splash of oil, then stir-fry the peas and carrots for 2 minutes.
Add the rice, breaking up clumps, and stir-fry 4-5 minutes until heated through.
Stir in the chicken or ham, soy sauce, and sesame oil, then fold in the scrambled egg and scallions.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use egg -- substitute crumbled, pan-seared extra-firm tofu scrambled in at the same step.
Do NOT use regular soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos.
Do NOT use regular soy sauce (it contains wheat) -- substitute tamari or coconut aminos, both labeled gluten-free.
Do NOT use sesame oil -- substitute a neutral oil such as avocado oil to finish.
Swap the chicken or ham for extra scrambled egg or edamame for a vegetarian version.
Do NOT use ham -- substitute cooked diced chicken, extra scrambled egg, or edamame instead.

name: Skillet Tuna Melt Sandwiches
description: Pantry tuna plus whatever cheese is in the fridge, broiled into a melt in under ten minutes -- my backup lunch when nothing got prepped over the weekend.
steps: Mix tuna, mayonnaise, celery, onion, and lemon juice in a bowl.
Spread the tuna mixture on 4 slices of bread and top each with a cheese slice, then the remaining bread.
Toast in a skillet over medium heat, 2-3 minutes per side, pressing gently, until golden and the cheese melts.
Slice and serve warm.

alternateRecipe.name: Chickpea "Tuna" Melt Sandwiches
alternateRecipe.description: Mashed chickpeas with a squeeze of lemon stand in for tuna's flake and brine, then it's melted under cheese exactly the same way.
steps: Mix mashed chickpeas, vegan mayonnaise, celery, onion, and lemon juice in a bowl.
Spread the mixture on 4 slices of bread and top each with a cheese slice, then the remaining bread.
Toast in a skillet over medium heat, 2-3 minutes per side, pressing gently, until golden and the cheese melts.
Slice and serve warm.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular mayonnaise -- substitute an egg-free (vegan) mayonnaise.
Do NOT use wheat bread -- substitute a certified gluten-free bread.
Do NOT use dairy cheddar -- substitute a dairy-free cheese slice, or skip the cheese and finish with a squeeze of extra lemon.

name: Saturday Baked Ziti (Freeze Half for Wednesday Lunch)
description: This clears 30 minutes so it's a weekend project, not a weeknight one -- I bake the full pan on Saturday, freeze it in individual lunch containers, and Wednesday's lunch is just a microwave away.
steps: Preheat oven to 375F. Cook ziti until just shy of al dente, then drain.
Brown ground beef with garlic, then stir in marinara sauce and simmer 5 minutes.
Mix ricotta, egg, half the parmesan, and half the basil in a separate bowl.
Combine pasta with the meat sauce, fold in the ricotta mixture, and spread in a baking dish.
Top with mozzarella and remaining parmesan, then bake uncovered 25 minutes until bubbling.
Cool, portion half into freezer-safe containers, and refrigerate or freeze the rest for later in the week.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular ziti -- substitute a certified gluten-free pasta shape.
Swap the ground beef for an Italian-style plant-based crumble, or omit it for a vegetarian version.
Do NOT use dairy ricotta, mozzarella, or parmesan -- substitute dairy-free ricotta-style and mozzarella-style alternatives, and skip the parmesan or use a dairy-free hard-cheese alternative.
Do NOT use egg in the ricotta mixture -- substitute 2 tablespoons of dairy-free cream cheese, or simply omit it; the filling will be slightly looser but still holds together.

name: Sheet-Pan Chicken Fajitas
description: One sheet pan, one shower's worth of cleanup -- chicken and peppers roast together while I set the table, and the leftover filling makes a killer next-day quesadilla.
steps: Heat oven to 425F.
Toss chicken, peppers, and onion with olive oil and fajita seasoning on a sheet pan.
Roast 18-20 minutes, stirring once, until chicken is cooked through.
Warm tortillas.
Squeeze lime over the pan and top with cheese to serve.
Fridge the extra filling flat in a shallow container so it reheats fast for lunch.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use flour tortillas -- substitute corn tortillas, or skip the tortilla entirely and serve the filling over rice.
Do NOT use dairy cheddar -- substitute a dairy-free shredded cheese, or simply skip the cheese and add extra lime and cilantro.
Swap the chicken for sliced steak or extra-firm tofu cubes (cut tofu roast time down by about 5 minutes).

name: 30-Minute Chicken Stir-Fry with Peanut Sauce
description: The peanut sauce is the real batch MVP here -- I double it every time and keep half in the fridge for noodle bowls later in the week.
steps: Cook rice according to package directions.
Whisk soy sauce, peanut butter, sesame oil, and garlic with 2 tbsp warm water into a sauce; double it and fridge half if you want a head start on next week.
Stir-fry chicken over high heat until nearly cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Add broccoli and carrots, cook 4-5 minutes until crisp-tender.
Pour in sauce and toss to coat, 1-2 minutes.
Serve over rice.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos (tamari is still a soybean product and is not soy-free).
Do NOT use peanut butter -- substitute sunflower seed butter for the same texture with no tree nut or peanut cross-contact risk.
Do NOT use sesame oil -- substitute a neutral oil like avocado or vegetable oil.
Swap the chicken for peeled shrimp or extra-firm tofu cubes.

name: Weeknight Beef and Broccoli
description: Takeout-speed beef and broccoli that actually beats delivery once the rice is going -- the sauce reduces fast, so this one wants your full attention for ten minutes straight.
steps: Cook rice according to package directions.
Whisk soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, and cornstarch with 0.5 cup water into a sauce.
Sear steak in a very hot skillet in batches, 1-2 minutes per side; set aside.
Steam or stir-fry broccoli until crisp-tender, about 4 minutes.
Return steak to the pan, pour in sauce, and simmer until glossy and thick, about 2 minutes.
Finish with sesame oil and serve over rice.
Sauce keeps well -- double the batch and refrigerate extra, or portion cooked beef and broccoli separately for a fast reheat lunch.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos (tamari is still a soybean product and is not soy-free).
Do NOT use sesame oil -- substitute a neutral oil for finishing.
Swap the flank steak for chicken thighs or extra-firm tofu.

name: Sheet-Pan Salmon with Roasted Veg
description: This is a cook-what-you-eat-tonight dinner, not a leftovers plan -- salmon turns rubbery reheated, so I only make what the family will actually finish at the table.
steps: Heat oven to 425F.
Arrange salmon, asparagus, and tomatoes on a sheet pan; drizzle with olive oil, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Roast 15-18 minutes until salmon flakes easily.
Squeeze lemon over everything before serving.
Serve immediately -- this one really doesn't hold well overnight.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the salmon for a firm white fish like cod, or use boneless chicken thighs if fish isn't for you (add about 10 minutes roast time for chicken).

name: Slow-Cooker Pulled Pork
description: This is a Sunday-load, Wednesday-eat move, not a weeknight cook -- ten minutes of prep, then the slow cooker does the rest while I'm nowhere near the kitchen; freeze half for a fast future dinner.
steps: Place onion in the bottom of the slow cooker, then the pork shoulder on top.
Whisk bbq sauce, vinegar, and brown sugar; pour over the pork.
Cook on low 8 hours or high 6 hours until the pork shreds easily with a fork.
Shred pork in the pot and stir back through the sauce.
Serve on buns; freeze half the shredded pork flat in a bag for a fast weeknight later this month.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular hamburger buns -- substitute a certified gluten-free bun or serve the pork over rice.
Swap the pork shoulder for boneless chicken thighs (reduce cook time to about 4 hours on low).

name: Baked Ziti
description: Baked ziti blows the 30-minute rule wide open, so I only make it as a weekend project -- one pan goes in the oven for tonight, one goes straight into the freezer for a Wednesday I already know is going to be rough.
steps: Heat oven to 375F. Boil ziti 2 minutes short of package directions; drain.
Brown ground beef and stir in marinara sauce.
Mix ricotta, egg, and half the parmesan in a bowl.
Combine pasta with the meat sauce, then layer half into a baking dish, dollop with ricotta mixture, top with remaining pasta, mozzarella, and remaining parmesan.
Bake covered 20 minutes, uncover, and bake 10-15 more minutes until bubbly.
Assemble a second unbaked pan in a freezer-safe dish, cover tightly, and freeze for up to 3 months -- thaw overnight before baking.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular ziti -- substitute a gluten-free pasta shape (cook it slightly under to avoid mush after baking).
Do NOT use dairy ricotta, mozzarella, or parmesan -- substitute dairy-free ricotta-style and shredded mozzarella-style alternatives; nutritional yeast can stand in for the parmesan.
Do NOT use egg -- substitute 3 tbsp of the reserved marinara or a flax egg (1 tbsp ground flaxseed plus 3 tbsp water, rested 5 minutes) to bind the ricotta layer.
Swap the ground beef for ground turkey, Italian sausage, or a can of drained lentils for a vegetarian version.

name: 20-Minute Garlic Butter Shrimp Pasta
description: Shrimp cooks in the time it takes the pasta water to boil, which makes this my fastest dinner -- but like all my fish nights, it's a cook-and-eat-tonight dish, not a make-ahead one.
steps: Boil spaghetti in salted water until al dente; reserve 0.5 cup pasta water before draining.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat and saute garlic 1 minute.
Add shrimp and cook 2-3 minutes per side until pink and opaque.
Toss in drained pasta with a splash of reserved pasta water, lemon juice, and parsley.
Serve immediately -- shrimp toughens fast on reheat, so this one is a cook-what-you-eat night.

alternateRecipe.name: 20-Minute Garlic Butter Chicken Pasta
alternateRecipe.description: Same fast garlic-butter move, but built around diced chicken so it's shellfish-free from the ground up, not just a swapped topping.
steps: Boil spaghetti in salted water until al dente; reserve 0.5 cup pasta water before draining.
Melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat and saute garlic 1 minute.
Add diced chicken, season with salt and pepper, and cook 6-7 minutes until cooked through.
Toss in drained pasta with a splash of reserved pasta water, lemon juice, and parsley.
Serve right away; this reheats fine the next day since it's chicken, not shellfish.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular spaghetti -- substitute a gluten-free pasta.
Do NOT use dairy butter -- substitute a dairy-free butter alternative or olive oil.

name: Sheet-Pan Sausage and Peppers
description: Four ingredients, one pan, and it looks fancier than the effort it took -- this is my go-to when I forgot to plan dinner until 5:30.
steps: Heat oven to 425F.
Toss sausage links, peppers, and onion with olive oil on a sheet pan.
Roast 25 minutes, flipping the sausages halfway, until cooked through and vegetables are tender.
Slice sausages and serve as-is or piled onto rolls.
Double the pan if your oven fits two -- the extra sausage and peppers reheat well sliced into a wrap or over rice for lunch.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the Italian sausage for a chicken or plant-based sausage.

name: Chicken and Black Bean Quesadillas
description: Quesadillas are the ultimate one-dish-whole-family meal -- I leave the beans out of the littlest one's half instead of cooking a separate kids' dinner.
steps: Mix shredded chicken and drained black beans in a bowl.
Lay a tortilla in a dry skillet, sprinkle with cheese, spoon on chicken-bean mix, and top with more cheese and a second tortilla.
Cook 2-3 minutes per side over medium heat until golden and cheese is melted.
Slice into wedges and serve with salsa.
Leave beans off one half of the pan for picky eaters instead of making a separate dinner.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use flour tortillas -- substitute corn tortillas.
Do NOT use dairy cheddar -- substitute a dairy-free shredded cheese.
Swap the chicken for extra black beans and roasted veg for a vegetarian version.

name: Egg Fried Rice with Veggies
description: This is my leftover-rice rescue mission -- day-old rice, whatever veg is wilting in the drawer, and it's on the table faster than delivery would even arrive.
steps: Heat a large skillet or wok over high heat with a little oil.
Scramble eggs quickly and set aside.
Add frozen peas and carrots, cook 2 minutes.
Add rice, breaking up clumps, and stir-fry 3-4 minutes.
Stir in soy sauce, scrambled eggs, and sesame oil; toss to combine.
Top with green onion and serve.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use eggs -- substitute crumbled firm tofu, scrambled in the pan first, for the same texture and protein.
Do NOT use regular soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos (tamari is still a soybean product and is not soy-free).
Do NOT use sesame oil -- substitute a neutral oil.

name: Chicken Pot Pie with Biscuit Topping
description: This is my advanced weekend project, not a Tuesday ask -- a real roux and homemade biscuit dough, made in a batch big enough to freeze a second pie for the week I already know is going to eat me alive.
steps: Cook diced chicken in 2 tbsp butter until browned; set aside.
In the same pot, melt remaining butter, whisk in flour, and cook 1-2 minutes to form a roux.
Gradually whisk in broth and milk, simmer until thickened, about 5 minutes.
Stir chicken and frozen vegetables into the sauce; season and pour into a baking dish.
Mix biscuit baking mix per package directions, drop spoonfuls over the filling, and brush with egg wash.
Bake at 400F for 25-30 minutes until biscuits are golden and filling is bubbling.
Assemble a second unbaked pie in a freezer-safe dish (skip the egg wash until baking day) and freeze for up to 3 months.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy butter and milk -- substitute a dairy-free butter alternative and unsweetened plain oat milk.
Do NOT use regular flour and biscuit baking mix -- substitute a 1:1 gluten-free flour blend for the roux and a gluten-free biscuit mix for the topping.
Do NOT use an egg wash -- substitute a brush of milk-alternative, or skip the wash entirely (biscuits will be a touch less golden).
Swap the chicken for shredded rotisserie turkey, or canned chickpeas and vegetable broth in place of the chicken broth, for a vegetarian version.

name: Peanut Noodles with Chicken
description: Cold or warm, this one survives the fridge better than almost anything else I make -- the peanut sauce actually gets better by day two.
steps: Cook noodles according to package directions; drain and rinse briefly with cold water.
Whisk peanut butter, soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and 3 tbsp warm water into a smooth sauce.
Toss noodles with sauce, chicken, and shredded carrots.
Serve warm or chilled -- this one is genuinely good cold straight from the fridge.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use wheat noodles -- substitute rice noodles.
Do NOT use peanut butter -- substitute sunflower seed butter.
Do NOT use regular soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos (tamari is still a soybean product and is not soy-free).
Do NOT use sesame oil -- substitute a neutral oil.
Swap the chicken for cubed tofu or shelled edamame.

name: Slow-Cooker Beef Chili
description: This is the freezer stash I always regret not doubling -- fifteen minutes of browning on a Sunday buys me two zero-effort dinners this month.
steps: Brown ground beef with onion in a skillet; drain excess fat.
Transfer to the slow cooker with kidney beans, diced tomatoes, and chili powder.
Cook on low 6-8 hours or high 3-4 hours.
Top individual bowls with cheese.
Freeze a full batch in portioned containers -- this reheats perfectly for a zero-effort future dinner.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy cheddar for topping -- substitute a dairy-free shredded cheese, or skip the topping and add sliced avocado.
Swap the ground beef for ground turkey or a double batch of beans and lentils for a vegetarian version.

name: No-Bake Peanut Butter Energy Bites
description: Five minutes of stirring turns into a week and a half of grab-and-go snacks -- I make a double batch on Sunday and freeze half so nobody has an excuse to raid the pantry chips instead.
steps: In a large bowl, stir together oats, peanut butter, honey, and vanilla until fully combined.
Fold in chocolate chips and chia seeds.
Chill the dough in the fridge for 15 minutes so it's easier to handle.
Roll into 1-inch balls (makes about 20). Store in an airtight container in the fridge for up to a week, or freeze half in a zip-top bag for instant after-school snacks straight from the freezer.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular rolled oats -- substitute certified gluten-free rolled oats.
Do NOT use peanut butter -- substitute sunflower seed butter (check the label for a nut-free facility if the allergy is severe).
Do NOT use regular mini chocolate chips -- substitute a dairy-free chocolate chip (e.g., Enjoy Life brand).

name: Sheet-Pan Snack Tray: Roasted Chickpeas, Cheese & Apple
description: One sheet pan of crispy roasted chickpeas gets divided into a week of grab-and-go trays alongside cheese, apple, and crackers -- the closest thing I have to a Lunchable that isn't secretly more work than dinner.
steps: Preheat oven to 400F. Drain and pat chickpeas dry, then toss with olive oil and smoked paprika on a sheet pan.
Roast 20-25 minutes, shaking the pan halfway, until crispy. Double this batch on a weekend and keep extra roasted chickpeas in a pantry jar for grab-and-go snacking all week.
While the chickpeas roast, cube the cheese and slice the apples.
Divide roasted chickpeas, cheese cubes, apple slices, and crackers into snack containers for the week ahead.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use cheddar cheese -- substitute a dairy-free cheese alternative or extra apple slices.
Do NOT use whole grain crackers -- substitute gluten-free crackers or rice cakes.

name: Freezer Yogurt Bark with Berries and Granola
description: Spread, scatter, freeze, snap into pieces -- this is the snack I actually keep stocked because it takes ten minutes of effort and then hands-off freezer time does the rest.
steps: Line a sheet pan with parchment paper.
Stir honey into the yogurt, then spread it in an even layer, about 1/4 inch thick, over the pan.
Scatter berries and granola over the top, pressing gently so they stick.
Freeze at least 3 hours, then break into pieces. This is a genuine batch move -- make a double batch on Sunday and keep a bag of broken pieces in the freezer for two weeks of instant snacks.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy yogurt -- substitute a thick coconut- or oat-based yogurt alternative.
Do NOT use standard granola -- substitute a certified gluten-free granola.
Do NOT use almond granola -- substitute a nut-free granola, or crushed pretzels or seeds.

name: Homemade Soft Pretzel Bites
description: This is not a weeknight recipe and I won't pretend it is -- it's a Sunday-afternoon project where the payoff is a freezer bag of bakery-quality pretzel bites that reheat from frozen in eight minutes for the rest of the week.
steps: Combine warm water, yeast, and brown sugar; let sit 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix in flour and melted butter and knead about 5 minutes until smooth (stand mixer or by hand), then let rise, covered, for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 450F. Divide the risen dough into ropes and cut into 1-inch bites.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil with the baking soda dissolved in; boil bites in batches for 30 seconds each, then transfer to a parchment-lined sheet pan.
Brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with coarse salt, and bake 10-12 minutes until deep golden brown.
Freeze extra baked bites in a zip-top bag; reheat straight from frozen in a 350F oven for about 8 minutes for a fast snack later in the week.

alternateRecipe.name: Gluten-Free Soft Pretzel Bites
alternateRecipe.description: A yeasted dough this structural doesn't survive a one-line flour swap -- this version uses a 1:1 gluten-free flour blend with xanthan gum and a slightly wetter, stickier dough handled with oiled hands instead of a floured board.
steps: Combine warm water, yeast, and brown sugar; let sit 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix in the gluten-free flour blend and melted butter. The dough will be stickier than a wheat dough -- mix just until smooth, then let rise, covered, for 30 minutes.
Preheat oven to 450F. With well-oiled hands (not a floured board), divide the dough into ropes and cut into 1-inch bites.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil with the baking soda dissolved in; boil bites in batches for 30 seconds each, then transfer to a parchment-lined sheet pan.
Brush with beaten egg, sprinkle with coarse salt, and bake 12-14 minutes (a minute or two longer than the wheat version) until deep golden brown.
Freeze extra baked bites in a zip-top bag; reheat straight from frozen in a 350F oven for about 8 minutes.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use butter -- substitute a dairy-free butter or margarine.
Do NOT use an egg wash -- substitute a dairy-free milk wash or a light brush of melted butter alternative for shine.

name: Turkey, Cheese & Hummus Roll-Ups
description: No stove, no timer, no cleanup beyond a cutting board -- these pinwheels are what I make when someone's hungry in the ninety seconds before we need to leave the house.
steps: Lay tortillas flat and spread each with a thin layer of hummus.
Layer turkey, cheese, and spinach evenly across each tortilla.
Roll tightly, slice into 1-inch pinwheels, and secure with toothpicks if needed.
Pack extras in an airtight container for up to 3 days -- great for lunchboxes, not just after-school snacking.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use wheat tortillas -- substitute gluten-free tortillas or use large lettuce leaves as wraps.
Swap the turkey for ham, rotisserie chicken, or a plant-based deli slice depending on what's on hand.
Do NOT use cheddar cheese -- substitute a dairy-free cheese slice, or omit.
Do NOT use tahini-based hummus -- substitute a sunflower-seed-based hummus or mashed avocado.

name: Baked Zucchini Tots
description: Squeezing every bit of water out of the zucchini is the one step you can't skip -- skip it and you get zucchini mush instead of tots -- but once you've got the technique down these freeze beautifully for a snack that's basically a vegetable in disguise.
steps: Preheat oven to 400F and line a sheet pan with parchment.
Grate the zucchini, wrap in a clean kitchen towel, and squeeze out as much liquid as possible -- this step is non-negotiable or the tots turn soggy.
Mix the squeezed zucchini with egg, breadcrumbs, parmesan, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Shape into small tot shapes, place on the pan, and bake 20 minutes, flipping halfway, until golden.
Double the batch and freeze the unbaked tots on a tray, then bag them once solid -- bake straight from frozen (add about 5 minutes) on a night you need a fast side or snack.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use egg -- substitute 1 tbsp ground flaxseed mixed with 3 tbsp water, rested 5 minutes until gel-like, as a flax egg.
Do NOT use panko breadcrumbs -- substitute gluten-free panko or crushed gluten-free crackers.
Do NOT use parmesan cheese -- substitute a dairy-free parmesan alternative or nutritional yeast.

name: 5-Minute No-Bake Peanut Butter Oat Bites
description: No oven, no timer, no reason not to make these on a school night -- stir, roll, fridge, done, and they hold up in a lunchbox for days.
steps: In a large bowl, stir together oats, peanut butter, honey, vanilla, and salt until fully combined and slightly sticky.
Fold in the mini chocolate chips.
Chill the bowl 10 minutes if the mix feels too soft to shape.
Roll into 1-inch balls (a cookie scoop makes this a one-minute job) and set on a lined tray.
Chill 20 minutes, then transfer to an airtight container. Keeps in the fridge 1 week or the freezer 2 months -- eat straight from frozen, they thaw in a lunchbox by mid-morning.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular rolled oats -- substitute certified gluten-free rolled oats (cross-contamination during processing is the real risk with standard oats).
Do NOT use regular mini chocolate chips -- substitute dairy-free/vegan mini chocolate chips.

alternateRecipe.name: No-Bake Sunflower Seed Oat Bites
alternateRecipe.description: Same one-bowl, no-bake bite, swapped nut-free for school lunchboxes with a peanut ban -- nobody at the table will notice the difference.
steps: In a large bowl, stir together oats, sunflower seed butter, honey, vanilla, and salt until fully combined and slightly sticky.
Fold in the mini chocolate chips.
Chill the bowl 10 minutes if the mix feels too soft to shape.
Roll into 1-inch balls and set on a lined tray.

Chill 20 minutes, then store airtight in the fridge 1 week or freezer 2 months. Note: sunflower seed butter can turn baked goods slightly green from a natural chlorophyll reaction -- harmless, just a heads-up before a kid asks.

name: One-Bowl Freezer Banana Bread
description: This is a weekend-batch move, not a weeknight ask -- the hour in the oven is the tradeoff for a loaf that slices, freezes, and turns overripe bananas into three separate lunchbox wins.
steps: Preheat oven to 350F and grease a loaf pan.
In a large bowl, mash the bananas well, then whisk in the eggs, melted butter, brown sugar, and vanilla.
Sprinkle the baking soda over the wet mix and stir in, then fold in the flour just until no dry streaks remain -- don't overmix.
Fold in the walnuts.
Pour into the pan and bake 50-60 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool completely, then slice and freeze individual slices flat on a tray before bagging -- grab one straight into a lunchbox and it thaws by mid-morning.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use eggs -- substitute 2 flax eggs (2 tbsp ground flaxseed whisked with 5 tbsp water, rested 5 minutes until gel-like).
Do NOT use butter -- substitute an equal amount of melted coconut oil or dairy-free margarine.
Do NOT use all-purpose flour -- substitute a 1:1 gluten-free baking blend.
Do NOT use walnuts -- substitute mini chocolate chips or omit entirely; the loaf still slices and freezes the same.

name: Double-Batch Chocolate Chip Cookie Dough, Freeze Half
description: Make the full double batch, bake half tonight, and freeze the rest as scoop-ready dough balls -- future-Tuesday you gets warm cookies in 14 minutes flat with zero fresh mixing.
steps: Cream the butter with brown and granulated sugar until fluffy, then beat in the egg and vanilla.
Stir the baking soda into the flour, then mix into the wet ingredients just until combined.
Fold in the chocolate chips.
Scoop the whole batch into tablespoon-size balls on trays. Bake half at 375F for 10-12 minutes until edges are golden.
Freeze the remaining dough balls solid on a tray, then bag them -- bake straight from frozen, adding 1-2 extra minutes.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy butter or regular chocolate chips -- substitute dairy-free butter/margarine and dairy-free chocolate chips.
Do NOT use egg -- substitute 1 flax egg (1 tbsp ground flaxseed whisked with 3 tbsp water, rested 5 minutes) or a store-bought egg replacer.
Do NOT use all-purpose flour -- substitute a 1:1 gluten-free baking blend.

name: Mug Brownie for Two, Doubled for Tomorrow
description: When there's ten minutes and a chocolate craving between homework and bedtime, this is the answer -- mix double, microwave one mug now and stash the second batter in the fridge for tomorrow's ten minutes.
steps: In a microwave-safe mug, whisk together flour, sugar, cocoa powder, and salt.
Stir in the milk and oil until smooth.
Fold in the chocolate chips.
Microwave on high 60-90 seconds, until the top just sets -- it should still look slightly underdone in the center.
Let sit 1 minute before eating with a spoon straight from the mug. To save the second portion, mix it in a separate bowl and refrigerate covered up to 2 days; microwave fresh when ready.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use all-purpose flour -- substitute a 1:1 gluten-free baking blend.
Do NOT use milk and regular chocolate chips -- substitute an unsweetened dairy-free milk (oat or soy work well here) and dairy-free chocolate chips.

name: Weekend Batch Rice Pudding, Grab-and-Go Fridge Cups
description: A stovetop stir-and-watch project for a weekend afternoon, portioned into jars so weeknight dessert is just opening the fridge -- I'm calling this fridge-batch, not freezer-batch, because dairy custards like this one turn grainy after a freeze-thaw and I'd rather be honest about that than oversell it.
steps: In a saucepan over medium heat, combine the cooked rice, milk, and sugar. Bring to a gentle simmer, stirring occasionally.
Simmer 20-25 minutes, stirring often, until thickened and the rice is very soft.
Whisk the egg yolks in a small bowl with a splash of the hot milk mixture to temper them, then stir the yolks back into the pot.
Cook 2-3 more minutes over low heat, stirring constantly, until slightly thickened (it will thicken more as it cools). Do not let it boil after adding the yolks.
Stir in vanilla, cinnamon, and raisins.
Portion into individual jars or containers while warm. Cool, then refrigerate up to 5 days -- do not freeze, the texture will turn grainy on thaw.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use whole milk -- substitute canned full-fat coconut milk or another unsweetened dairy-free milk.
Do NOT use egg yolks -- substitute 2 tbsp cornstarch whisked into 1/4 cup cold milk, stirred in during the last few minutes of simmering to thicken instead.

name: No-Bake Peanut Butter Oat Bites
description: My freezer-stash answer to the 3pm 'I'm starving' ambush -- ten minutes of stirring, no oven, and they hold up in a lunchbox or a backpack for days.
steps: In a large bowl, stir the peanut butter and honey together until smooth (microwave 20 seconds if the peanut butter is stiff).
Add the oats, flaxseed, vanilla, and salt; mix until everything is evenly coated and the mixture holds together when pressed.
Fold in the mini chocolate chips.
Chill the mixture 10 minutes so it firms up enough to roll.
Roll into 1-inch balls (makes about 20). Store in the fridge for the week, or freeze half in a labeled bag for next week's snack drawer.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use peanut butter -- substitute sunbutter (sunflower seed butter) at a 1:1 ratio; the binding and texture stay the same.
Do NOT use regular rolled oats -- substitute certified gluten-free rolled oats.
Do NOT use milk chocolate chips -- substitute a dairy-free chocolate chip made with cocoa butter or coconut oil.

name: One-Bowl Fudgy Brownie Squares
description: One bowl, one pan, done before the 'ten more minutes of screen time' timer runs out -- this is the brownie I make when the whole family votes for dessert on a school night.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and line an 8x8 pan with parchment.
Melt the butter, then whisk in both sugars until smooth.
Whisk in the eggs and vanilla until glossy.
Fold in cocoa powder, flour, and salt just until no dry streaks remain -- don't overmix.
Stir in the chocolate chips, spread into the pan, and bake 20-22 minutes until a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs.
Cool 10 minutes before cutting into 16 squares. Extras freeze well for up to 2 months.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy butter -- substitute melted coconut oil or a stick plant-based butter 1:1. Do NOT use milk chocolate chips -- substitute dairy-free chocolate chips.
Do NOT use eggs -- substitute 2 tablespoons ground flaxseed whisked with 5 tablespoons water per egg, rested 5 minutes until gel-like, then use as normal.
Do NOT use all-purpose flour -- substitute a 1:1 gluten-free baking flour blend.

name: Frozen Yogurt Bark with Berries and Granola
description: This is the treat I make on a Sunday so it's already broken into shards in the freezer the first time someone asks for ice cream on a random Tuesday.
steps: Line a baking sheet with parchment paper.
Whisk the yogurt, honey, and vanilla together until smooth, then spread evenly onto the parchment in a rectangle about 1/4-inch thick.
Scatter the berries, granola, and almonds evenly over the top, pressing gently so they stick.
Freeze uncovered at least 3 hours, or until solid.
Break into shards and store in a freezer bag -- grab a piece straight from the freezer any night of the week.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy yogurt -- substitute a plain, unsweetened coconut-milk yogurt 1:1.
Do NOT use regular granola -- substitute a certified gluten-free granola or crushed gluten-free crackers.
Do NOT use sliced almonds -- substitute toasted pepitas (pumpkin seeds) or omit the topping entirely.

name: Sheet-Pan Chocolate Chip Cookie Bars
description: One pan, no scooping forty individual cookies -- this is what 'homemade cookies on a Wednesday' actually looks like at my house.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and line a 9x13 pan with parchment.
Cream the softened butter with both sugars until light, then beat in the eggs and vanilla.
Stir in flour, baking soda, and salt until just combined, then fold in the chocolate chips.
Press the dough evenly into the pan.
Bake 18-20 minutes until the edges are golden and the center still looks slightly underbaked.
Cool fully before cutting into 20 bars. They freeze well, unfrosted, for up to 2 months.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy butter -- substitute a stick plant-based butter 1:1. Do NOT use regular chocolate chips -- substitute dairy-free chocolate chips.
Do NOT use eggs -- substitute 2 tablespoons ground flaxseed whisked with 5 tablespoons water per egg, rested 5 minutes until gel-like.
Do NOT use all-purpose flour -- substitute a 1:1 gluten-free baking flour blend.

name: Banana Oat Freezer Muffins
description: I bake a double batch of these on a Sunday specifically so a lunchbox treat or a breakfast-on-the-run is already done for the whole week -- this is my go-to batch-and-freeze move.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and line a 12-cup muffin tin.
Mash the bananas in a large bowl, then whisk in the eggs, brown sugar, melted butter, and vanilla.
In a separate bowl, combine flour, oats, baking soda, and salt.
Fold the dry ingredients into the wet just until combined, then stir in the walnuts.
Divide batter evenly among the muffin cups and bake 18-20 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean.
Cool completely, then freeze half the batch in a labeled bag -- they reheat from frozen in about 30 seconds in the microwave, so a 'fresh baked' treat is always one button-press away.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use eggs -- substitute 2 tablespoons ground flaxseed whisked with 5 tablespoons water per egg, rested 5 minutes.
Do NOT use dairy butter -- substitute melted coconut oil or a plant-based butter 1:1.
Do NOT use all-purpose flour or regular rolled oats -- substitute a 1:1 gluten-free baking flour blend and certified gluten-free rolled oats.
Do NOT use walnuts -- substitute sunflower seeds or omit them entirely.

name: Classic Diner Scrambled Eggs & Crispy Bacon
description: This is what a diner breakfast is supposed to taste like -- soft curds of egg, a little butterfat, bacon with real snap. I watch the salt on the bacon side and let black pepper and fresh chives do some of the work the shaker used to.
steps: Lay bacon in a cold skillet, turn heat to medium, and render slowly, turning once, until crisp, about 8 minutes. Drain on paper towels -- this is where most of a scrambled-egg breakfast's sodium already lives, so I don't add more later.
Whisk eggs with milk and a light pinch of salt and pepper until just combined -- don't overbeat, you want tenderness, not air.
Wipe most of the bacon fat from the pan, add butter over low heat, and pour in the eggs.
Push the eggs gently with a spatula in slow folds, pulling from the edges to the center, taking the pan off heat for the last few passes -- they keep cooking.
Fold in chives at the very end, plate alongside the bacon while both are hot.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use whole milk or butter -- substitute unsweetened plant milk and olive oil; the eggs stay tender, just cook them a touch gentler since oil browns faster than butter.

alternateRecipe.name: Diner-Style Tofu Scramble & Bacon
alternateRecipe.description: Same diner plate, minus the eggs -- turmeric and nutritional yeast get the color and savoriness close enough that it still reads as a scramble, not a science project.
steps: Render bacon in a cold skillet over medium heat until crisp, about 8 minutes; drain and set aside.
Crumble pressed tofu into a bowl and toss with turmeric, nutritional yeast, plant milk, salt, and pepper.
Warm olive oil in a skillet over medium heat, add the tofu mixture, and cook, stirring occasionally, until heated through and lightly golden at the edges, 6-8 minutes.
Fold in chives, plate alongside the bacon.

adaptations.instructions: Use turkey bacon or a plant-based bacon in the same quantity -- render it the same slow, low way so it still crisps instead of just browning.

name: Real Buttermilk Pancakes
description: Griddle-crisp at the edges, soft in the middle -- I cut the added salt in the batter and let the buttermilk's tang and a properly hot griddle carry the flavor instead.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter, melted (plus more for the griddle)

steps: Whisk flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
In another bowl, whisk buttermilk, egg, melted butter, and vanilla.
Pour wet into dry and stir just until combined -- lumps are fine, overmixing is what makes pancakes tough.
Let the batter rest 5 minutes while the griddle heats to medium.
Butter the griddle and ladle batter into rounds; flip once bubbles cover the surface and the edges look set, 2-3 minutes per side.
Serve hot with real maple syrup -- that's where the sweetness should live, not the batter.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use all-purpose flour -- substitute a 1:1 measure-for-measure gluten-free flour blend; the batter looks slightly thicker, so thin with an extra tablespoon of buttermilk if needed.
Do NOT use buttermilk or butter -- substitute 1 1/4 cups unsweetened plant milk mixed with 1 tablespoon lemon juice, rested 5 minutes to sour, and a neutral oil in place of the butter.
Do NOT use egg -- substitute 1 tablespoon ground flaxseed whisked with 3 tablespoons water, rested 5 minutes until gel-like, then stirred in where the egg would go.

name: Corned Beef Hash with Fried Eggs
description: Hash the way it ought to be -- crisp-edged potato, real corned beef, a fried egg to break over the top. I rinse the corned beef and lean on cider vinegar and black pepper so cutting the salt doesn't leave it flat.
steps: If using canned or deli corned beef, rinse it quickly under cold water and pat dry -- that alone cuts a good chunk of the sodium without losing the beef flavor.
Parboil diced potatoes in salted water 5 minutes; drain well.
Melt butter in a heavy skillet over medium-high heat, add potatoes in a single layer, and let them sit undisturbed several minutes to develop a real crust before stirring.
Add onion and bell pepper; cook until softened and the potatoes are browned, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the corned beef, paprika, and black pepper; cook until the beef has crisped edges, then splash in the cider vinegar and scrape up the browned bits.
Fry the eggs separately to your liking, plate over the hash, and finish with parsley.

adaptations.instructions: Swap in diced smoked turkey or a well-seasoned sautéed mushroom-and-lentil mix for the corned beef, and add an extra pinch of smoked paprika to make up the depth beef would have carried.
Do NOT use butter -- substitute olive oil; the potatoes crisp just as well.
Skip the fried egg or top the hash with sliced avocado instead -- it holds up fine on its own without egg.

name: Old-Fashioned Sausage Gravy and Biscuits
description: This is a Sunday-morning dish and I won't apologize for it -- flaky butter biscuits under a black-pepper-heavy sausage gravy. I hold back on salting the gravy directly and let the pepper and the sausage's own fat do the heavy lifting.
steps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Cut cold butter into flour, baking powder, and salt until pea-sized crumbs form.
Stir in buttermilk just until a shaggy dough comes together, pat out on a floured board to 3/4-inch thick, cut rounds, and bake 12-14 minutes until golden.
While the biscuits bake, brown the sausage in a skillet over medium heat, breaking it up, about 8 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over the sausage and its fat, stir, and cook 1 minute to lose the raw-flour taste.
Slowly whisk in the milk, bring to a gentle simmer, and stir often until thickened, 5-7 minutes.
Season with black pepper and sage -- taste before you reach for salt, the sausage usually carries enough.
Split warm biscuits, ladle gravy over, and serve right away.

alternateRecipe.name: Gluten-Free Sausage Gravy and Biscuits
alternateRecipe.description: The same Sunday plate built on a 1:1 gluten-free flour blend for the biscuits and a cornstarch slurry in place of a roux -- it still comes out flaky and thick, not gummy.

ingredients.name: cornstarch, mixed with 3 tablespoons cold water (gravy)

steps: Preheat oven to 425°F. Cut cold butter into the gluten-free flour blend, baking powder, and salt until pea-sized crumbs form.

Stir in buttermilk just until a shaggy dough comes together, pat out to 3/4-inch thick, cut rounds, and bake 12-15 minutes until golden -- gluten-free biscuits brown a bit faster, watch them near the end.
While the biscuits bake, brown the sausage in a skillet over medium heat, breaking it up, about 8 minutes.
Pour in the milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Whisk in the cornstarch slurry and simmer, stirring, until thickened, 3-4 minutes.
Season with black pepper and sage; taste before adding salt.
Split warm biscuits, ladle gravy over, and serve.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use butter, buttermilk, or whole milk -- substitute cold vegan butter and plant milk soured with a little lemon juice for the biscuits, and unsweetened plant milk for the gravy; whisk the gravy a bit longer, it thickens slower without dairy's proteins.
Use a turkey breakfast sausage or a plant-based sausage crumble in the same amount, and add a touch more sage since turkey and plant sausage run milder.

name: Denver Omelet
description: A proper diner Denver -- ham, peppers, onion, melted cheddar folded into eggs. I go easy on the cheese and let a hot pan and a hard sear on the vegetables do the flavor work salt usually gets credit for.
steps: Sauté onion and bell pepper in a splash of butter over medium-high heat until they pick up real color, about 5 minutes -- that browning is doing a lot of the seasoning work.
Stir in ham and warm through, 1-2 minutes, then remove the filling to a bowl.
Wipe the pan, melt the remaining butter over medium-low heat, and pour in the whisked eggs.
As the eggs set at the edges, tilt the pan and let uncooked egg run underneath.
When mostly set, scatter the filling and cheese over half, fold the other half over, and let the cheese finish melting, about 1 minute.

alternateRecipe.name: Denver-Style Tofu Scramble
alternateRecipe.description: All the Denver flavors -- ham, peppers, onion, melted cheddar -- folded into a turmeric tofu scramble instead of egg; it still eats like a hearty diner plate.
steps: Sauté onion and bell pepper in olive oil over medium-high heat until browned, about 5 minutes.
Stir in ham and warm through, 1-2 minutes.
Add crumbled tofu, turmeric, nutritional yeast, and black pepper; cook, stirring, until heated through and lightly golden, 6-7 minutes.
Scatter cheddar over the top, cover briefly to melt, then serve.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use cheddar or butter -- substitute a dairy-free cheddar-style shred and olive oil; melt the shreds under a lid for the last minute since they don't melt as freely as real cheddar.
Use diced turkey ham, or leave the meat out entirely and add extra peppers and onion for a vegetarian Denver.

name: Classic French Toast
description: French toast should taste like custard and butter, not cereal milk -- thick bread, a real soak, a hot buttered pan. I keep the salt to a pinch in the custard and let cinnamon and good maple syrup carry the rest.
steps: Whisk eggs, milk, cinnamon, vanilla, and salt in a wide shallow dish.
Soak each bread slice 20-30 seconds per side -- long enough to soften through, not so long it falls apart.
Melt butter over medium heat in a skillet or on a griddle.
Cook slices until deep golden and set, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve hot with real maple syrup, not the corn-syrup kind -- that's not where I'm looking to save money.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular bread -- substitute a sturdy certified gluten-free sandwich loaf, day-old or lightly toasted first so it holds the custard without falling apart.
Do NOT use whole milk or butter -- substitute a full-fat plant milk (oat works best for richness) and a neutral oil for the pan.

alternateRecipe.name: Custard-Style Batter French Toast (No Egg)
alternateRecipe.description: A chickpea-flour batter stands in for the egg custard here -- it browns and crisps at the edges close enough to the real thing that it still feels like a diner plate, not a substitute.
steps: Whisk chickpea flour, plant milk, cinnamon, vanilla, mashed banana, and salt into a smooth batter.
Soak each bread slice 20-30 seconds per side.
Heat oil in a skillet or on a griddle over medium heat.
Cook slices until deep golden and set, about 3-4 minutes per side.
Serve hot with maple syrup.

name: Old-Fashioned Oatmeal with Brown Sugar and Walnuts
description: Nothing fussy here -- oats cooked low and slow in milk, a spoon of brown sugar, toasted walnuts for crunch. I cut the pinch of salt in half and toast the walnuts hard enough that they still carry the bowl.
steps: Toast walnuts in a dry skillet over medium heat, stirring, until fragrant, 3-4 minutes -- this step is doing the flavor work, don't skip it.
Bring milk to a gentle simmer with the pinch of salt, stir in oats.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until thick and creamy, about 5-6 minutes.
Stir in butter and cinnamon off heat.
Spoon into bowls, top with brown sugar and toasted walnuts.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use whole milk or butter -- substitute unsweetened oat milk and a small pat of a plant-based butter; cook it a minute or two longer since plant milk simmers thinner.
Do NOT use walnuts -- substitute toasted pepitas or sunflower seeds, or leave them out and add a touch more cinnamon in their place.

name: Eggs Benedict with Canadian Bacon and Hollandaise
description: Eggs Benedict done right is worth the fuss -- a properly poached egg, real hollandaise, Canadian bacon with some char on it. I lean on fresh lemon and cracked pepper in the hollandaise so it doesn't need a heavy hand with the salt cellar.
steps: Make the hollandaise: whisk egg yolks and lemon juice in a heatproof bowl over barely simmering water until pale and thickened, about 3 minutes.

Off heat, drizzle in melted butter very slowly, whisking constantly, until thick and glossy; season with cayenne and black pepper. Keep warm off direct heat, whisking occasionally so it doesn't split.
Bring a wide pot of water to a bare simmer with the vinegar. Crack each egg into a small cup, swirl the water gently, and slide the egg in; poach 3 minutes for a runny yolk.
Meanwhile, sear Canadian bacon in a dry skillet until it picks up color at the edges, about 2 minutes per side. Toast the English muffins.
Build each plate: muffin half, Canadian bacon, poached egg, a generous spoon of hollandaise, a crack of black pepper and chives.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular English muffins -- substitute a certified gluten-free English muffin, toasted a shade darker since they can be more delicate once soaked with hollandaise.
Do NOT use butter in the hollandaise -- substitute a melted vegan butter alternative; whisk a bit more vigorously, it can be slower to emulsify.

alternateRecipe.name: Yolk-Free Benedict with Tofu 'Poach' and Cashew Hollandaise
alternateRecipe.description: No eggs anywhere on the plate, but between black salt for a faint sulfur note and a cashew hollandaise, it still lands as a Benedict, not a bowl of tofu.
steps: Slice tofu into rounds, sprinkle with black salt and turmeric, and warm gently in a skillet over medium-low heat, about 5 minutes per side.
Blend soaked cashews, lemon juice, nutritional yeast, water, and black pepper until smooth, then warm gently in a small saucepan, stirring, until slightly thickened.
Sear Canadian bacon until it picks up color, about 2 minutes per side. Toast the English muffins.
Build each plate: muffin half, Canadian bacon, warm tofu round, a spoon of cashew hollandaise, black pepper and chives on top.

adaptations.instructions: Use turkey Canadian bacon or a grilled portobello cap in place of the Canadian bacon, seared the same way for char.

name: Old-Fashioned Grilled Cheese and Tomato Soup, Lightened
description: This is the lunch I grew up on, just with low-sodium tomatoes and a splash of vinegar doing the work salt used to do -- you still get a crackling, buttery grilled cheese to dunk in it.
steps: Warm olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat; add onion and cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
Add garlic and cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in crushed tomatoes, dried basil, and 1 cup water; bring to a simmer and cook 10 minutes.
Stir in vinegar and pepper -- taste it; that vinegar and basil should make you forget there's less salt in the pot.
Butter one side of each bread slice; build sandwiches with the cheddar between the unbuttered sides.
Griddle over medium heat, 3-4 minutes per side, until golden and the cheese is fully melted.
Ladle soup into bowls, garnish with fresh basil, and serve alongside the sandwiches for dunking.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular wheat bread -- substitute a sturdy gluten-free sandwich bread; it griddles the same way, maybe a minute less per side since it toasts faster.
Do NOT use dairy butter or cheddar -- substitute a plant-based butter and a melty dairy-free cheddar-style slice; the tomato soup carries plenty of flavor on its own so you won't miss much.

name: Reuben Sandwich, Rebuilt Lower Sodium
description: A real Reuben, not a diet Reuben -- rinsing the kraut and using low-sodium corned beef cuts a real amount of salt, and horseradish in the dressing makes sure you never notice.
steps: Rinse the sauerkraut under cold water and press it dry -- this alone cuts a real amount of sodium without losing the tang.
Stir together mayonnaise, ketchup, and horseradish for the dressing.
Warm the corned beef in a dry skillet just until heated through, 2-3 minutes.
Spread dressing on one side of each bread slice; layer corned beef, sauerkraut, and Swiss cheese between two slices.
Butter the outside of each sandwich.
Griddle over medium-low heat, pressing gently, 4-5 minutes per side, until the cheese melts and the bread is deep golden.
Slice on the diagonal and serve hot.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use rye bread -- substitute a sturdy gluten-free rye-style loaf; it griddles the same way.
Do NOT use Swiss cheese or dairy butter -- substitute a dairy-free Swiss-style slice and a plant-based butter.
Do NOT use regular mayonnaise -- substitute an egg-free mayonnaise for the dressing; it whisks up the same.
Sliced roasted turkey works in place of the corned beef for a lighter Reuben -- still warm it in the dressing and kraut so it doesn't taste like a diet sandwich.

name: Classic Chicken Salad Sandwich
description: No grapes, no curry powder -- just chicken, mayo, celery, and enough lemon and tarragon that you don't think about the fact the mayo's been cut back a touch.
steps: In a bowl, combine mayonnaise, lemon juice, tarragon, and pepper.
Fold in shredded chicken, celery, and red onion until evenly coated.
Taste and adjust the lemon and pepper -- the acid and tarragon do the job salt usually does here.
Let the salad sit 15 minutes in the fridge so the flavors settle.
Toast the bread lightly if you like a little bite to it.
Layer lettuce and chicken salad between slices and serve.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular mayonnaise -- substitute an egg-free mayonnaise; the lemon and tarragon carry the flavor either way.
Do NOT use wheat bread -- substitute a hearty gluten-free sandwich bread.
Canned chickpeas, mashed lightly, make a fine stand-in for the chicken if you want to go meatless -- season the same way.

name: Turkey Club, Right-Sized
description: A proper triple-decker club, just built with lower-sodium turkey and a light hand on the bacon count so it's a real portion, not a doorstop.
steps: Cook bacon in a skillet until crisp; drain on paper towels.
Toast the bread.
Mix mayonnaise and Dijon; spread on the toast.
Layer turkey, bacon, lettuce, and tomato between three stacked slices of toast, club-style.
Secure with toothpicks, slice into quarters, and serve.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use wheat bread -- substitute gluten-free sandwich bread, toasted the same way.
Do NOT use regular mayonnaise -- substitute an egg-free mayonnaise for the spread.
Turkey bacon works fine if you're skipping pork -- it won't crisp up quite as much, so watch the pan a minute less.

Do NOT use sliced roast chicken here -- chicken carries the same meat restriction as turkey. Instead, layer in a marinated grilled portobello or a plant-based deli slice in place of the turkey (and skip or swap the bacon too, per the pork adaptation, if meat is fully off the table); build the club the same way so the stack and crunch stay intact.

name: Classic Beef Chili, Lower Sodium
description: This is chili the way it's supposed to taste -- I get there without dumping in salt by toasting the spices hard and finishing with a splash of vinegar instead of leaving it flat.

ingredients.name: low-sodium kidney beans, drained and rinsed

steps: Brown ground beef in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat, breaking it up; drain excess fat.
Add onion and garlic, cook until softened, about 5 minutes.
Stir in chili powder, cumin, and cocoa powder; toast 1 minute until fragrant.
Add crushed tomatoes, beans, and beef broth; bring to a simmer.
Cover partially and simmer 45 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened.
Stir in vinegar and pepper at the end -- that splash of acid is what makes it taste seasoned instead of just less salty.
Ladle into bowls and serve with your usual fixings.

adaptations.instructions: Ground turkey or a plant-based crumble both work in this chili -- brown it the same way and lean a little harder on the cumin and chili powder since they carry less fat flavor. Also swap the beef broth for a low-sodium vegetable or mushroom broth, since that's beef too -- it still gives the chili body.

name: Classic Tuna Salad Melt
description: A diner-counter tuna melt, dill and lemon doing the seasoning work so I can use no-salt-added tuna and still get something worth broiling.

ingredients.name: canned tuna in water, no-salt-added, drained

steps: Combine tuna, mayonnaise, celery, onion, lemon juice, dill, and pepper in a bowl; mix well.
Split and toast the English muffins.
Mound tuna salad on each muffin half, top with a slice of cheddar.
Broil 2-3 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and just starting to brown.
Serve open-faced, hot from the broiler.

alternateRecipe.name: Chickpea Salad Melt
alternateRecipe.description: Same mustardy, dilled deli-salad idea as the tuna melt, built on smashed chickpeas instead -- still gets broiled with cheddar so it comes out hot and melty, not like a sad plain salad.

ingredients.name: canned chickpeas, no-salt-added, drained and coarsely mashed

steps: Drain chickpeas and mash coarsely with a fork, leaving some texture.
Combine mashed chickpeas, mayonnaise, celery, onion, lemon juice, dill, and pepper in a bowl; mix well.
Split and toast the English muffins.
Mound the chickpea salad on each muffin half, top with a slice of cheddar.
Broil 2-3 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and just starting to brown.
Serve open-faced, hot from the broiler.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular mayonnaise -- substitute an egg-free mayonnaise; it binds the salad the same way.
Do NOT use regular English muffins -- substitute a gluten-free English muffin or gluten-free bread, toasted well so it holds up to broiling.
Do NOT use cheddar cheese -- substitute a dairy-free cheddar-style slice that melts under the broiler.

name: Split Pea Soup with Smoked Ham, Rebuilt Lower Sodium
