description: This is my signature move applied to the soup I grew up on -- searing the ham for a real base, then smoked paprika and a last splash of vinegar make up for using half the ham I used to.
steps: Rinse split peas and pick over for debris.
In a Dutch oven, sear the diced ham over medium heat until lightly browned, 3-4 minutes -- this builds a real base of flavor before anything else goes in.
Add onion, carrot, celery, and garlic; cook until softened, 6-7 minutes.
Stir in smoked paprika and toast 30 seconds.
Add split peas, broth, bay leaf, and thyme; bring to a boil, then reduce to a low simmer.
Cover partially and simmer 60-75 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the peas break down and the soup is thick.
Remove bay leaf and thyme stems; stir in vinegar and pepper.
Taste -- the smoked paprika and vinegar should make up for the ham being lighter on salt than you're used to. Adjust pepper, not salt, if it needs more.
Let rest 10 minutes before serving; it thickens further as it sits.

adaptations.instructions: A smoked turkey leg or drumstick makes a good stand-in for the ham -- sear it the same way to render some fat and get that browned base, then pull the meat off the bone before serving.
Vegetable broth works instead of chicken broth if you want this meatless outside of the ham; the smoked paprika still carries the smokiness.

name: Classic Cobb Salad
description: Rows, not a tossed mess -- chicken, bacon, egg, avocado, tomato, and blue cheese laid out the way it's supposed to be, with a sharp vinaigrette so nobody misses a heavy hand of salt.
steps: Whisk together vinegar, olive oil, Dijon, and pepper for the dressing.
Arrange romaine on a platter.
Line up rows of chicken, bacon, egg, avocado, tomato, and blue cheese across the lettuce, Cobb-style, so everybody can see what's in it.
Drizzle with dressing right before serving so the avocado doesn't sit around getting soggy underneath it.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use hard-boiled eggs -- substitute marinated white beans or simply omit and add extra avocado; the row still holds its place on the platter.
Do NOT use blue cheese -- substitute a dairy-free blue-cheese-style crumble, or skip it and add a few more olives for that same salty bite.
Turkey bacon crisps up fine in place of regular bacon.
Chickpeas make a fine substitute for the chicken row if you want to skip meat entirely.

name: Classic Patty Melt
description: Caramelized onions, griddled rye, and a beef patty under melted Swiss -- take the time on the onions and you won't reach for the salt shaker.
steps: In a skillet, melt 1 tbsp butter over medium-low heat; add onions and cook slowly, stirring occasionally, 20 minutes, until deeply caramelized.
Meanwhile, form ground beef into 4 thin oval patties; season with pepper and a light brush of Worcestershire.
Sear patties in a hot skillet, 3 minutes per side, until well browned; set aside.
Butter one side of each bread slice.
Build sandwiches: bread (butter-side out), Swiss cheese, a beef patty, caramelized onions, more Swiss, second slice of bread.
Griddle over medium-low heat, pressing gently, 3-4 minutes per side, until the cheese is fully melted and the bread is deep golden.
Cut in half and serve hot, while the cheese is still pulling.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use rye bread -- substitute a hearty gluten-free rye-style loaf, buttered and griddled the same way.
Do NOT use Swiss cheese or dairy butter -- substitute a dairy-free Swiss-style slice and a plant-based butter.
Do NOT use traditional Worcestershire sauce -- substitute a fish-free Worcestershire-style sauce or coconut aminos for that same savory depth.
A well-seasoned mushroom or turkey patty stands in fine here, though press it a little firmer since it won't render fat the way beef does.

name: Classic Lower-Sodium Meatloaf
description: The meatloaf I grew up with, just with half the salt swapped for a hit of vinegar and mustard so nobody at the table notices the difference.
steps: Preheat oven to 350F and line a baking sheet with parchment.

In a large bowl, combine ground beef, breadcrumbs, egg, milk, onion, garlic, half the ketchup, mustard, paprika, pepper, and parsley. Mix gently with your hands just until combined -- overworking makes it tough.
Shape into a firm free-form loaf on the baking sheet; it browns better than a loaf pan.
Whisk remaining ketchup with the vinegar and brush over the top.
Bake 55-60 minutes until internal temp hits 160F, then rest 10 minutes before slicing.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the ground beef 1:1 for ground turkey or ground chicken thigh; brown it a little longer since it releases more moisture.
Do NOT use regular panko breadcrumbs -- substitute certified gluten-free breadcrumbs or gluten-free rolled oats, pulsed fine.
Do NOT use egg -- substitute 1 tbsp ground flaxseed whisked with 3 tbsp water, rested 5 minutes, as the binder.
Do NOT use milk -- substitute unsweetened plain oat milk or unsweetened almond milk.

name: Chicken Pot Pie
description: Real pot pie: a flaky top crust, a gravy that actually coats the spoon, and enough black pepper that you forget I cut the salt in the broth.
steps: Preheat oven to 400F.
Melt 2 tbsp butter in a Dutch oven, sear chicken until just cooked through, remove and set aside.
Add remaining butter and sauté onion, carrot, celery until softened, then add garlic and thyme.
Stir in flour, cook 1 minute, then whisk in broth and milk until smooth and thickened.
Return chicken to the pot, stir in peas and pepper, and transfer to a baking dish.
Top with pie crust, cut a few vents, and bake 25-30 minutes until crust is golden and filling bubbles.

alternateRecipe.name: Hearty Vegetable Pot Pie
alternateRecipe.description: Built around mushrooms and root vegetables instead of chicken, with a splash of soy sauce standing in for the savory depth the meat used to carry.
steps: Preheat oven to 400F.
Melt 2 tbsp butter in a Dutch oven and sear mushrooms hard, without stirring too often, until deeply browned; remove and set aside.
Add remaining butter and sauté onion, carrot, celery, and potato until softened, then add garlic and thyme.
Stir in flour, cook 1 minute, then whisk in broth, milk, and soy sauce until smooth and thickened.
Return mushrooms to the pot, stir in peas and pepper, and transfer to a baking dish.
Top with pie crust, cut a few vents, and bake 25-30 minutes until crust is golden and filling bubbles.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use butter or whole milk -- substitute a dairy-free butter alternative and unsweetened plain oat milk.
Do NOT use regular flour or the standard pie crust -- substitute a 1:1 gluten-free flour blend for the gravy and a certified gluten-free pie crust.

name: Beef Pot Roast with Root Vegetables
description: A Sunday roast that falls apart with a fork -- red wine and a long slow braise do the seasoning work that salt used to.
steps: Preheat oven to 300F. Pat roast dry, season with pepper, and dust with flour.
Sear roast on all sides in a Dutch oven in a little oil until deeply browned; remove.
Sauté onion and garlic in the same pot, stir in tomato paste, then deglaze with wine, scraping up the browned bits.
Return roast to the pot, add broth, bay leaves, thyme, and rosemary. Cover and braise in the oven 2.5 hours.
Add carrots and potatoes, cover, and cook another 45-60 minutes until everything is fork-tender.
Discard herb stems and bay leaves, skim fat, and serve roast with vegetables and pan juices.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the chuck roast for boneless short ribs or a venison roast, adjusting braise time down slightly for a smaller cut, and swap the beef broth for a low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth so no beef remains in the dish.
Do NOT dust the roast with regular flour -- season and sear it plain, then thicken the pan juices at the end with a cornstarch slurry instead.

name: Herb Roast Chicken with Pan Gravy
description: A whole roasted bird with crisp skin and a gravy built from the drippings -- the kind of centerpiece that doesn't need much salt when the herbs and pan juices are doing real work.
steps: Preheat oven to 425F. Pat chicken very dry.
Rub softened butter under and over the skin, and season generously with pepper.
Stuff cavity with lemon, garlic, rosemary, and thyme, then tie the legs together.
Roast 60-75 minutes until a thigh reads 165F, basting once with pan juices halfway through.
Rest chicken 15 minutes; pour pan drippings into a saucepan.
Whisk flour into the drippings over medium heat, then slowly whisk in broth until the gravy thickens, about 5 minutes.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use butter -- substitute a dairy-free butter alternative or olive oil rubbed under and over the skin.
Do NOT use regular flour for the gravy -- substitute a cornstarch slurry (1 tbsp cornstarch whisked with 2 tbsp cold water) whisked into the drippings instead.

name: Baked Ziti
description: Weeknight red-sauce comfort -- I lean on a good no-salt-added marinara and extra garlic and basil so the lower sodium never shows.
steps: Preheat oven to 375F. Boil ziti in unsalted water until just shy of al dente; drain.
Brown ground beef with garlic, drain excess fat, stir in marinara, and simmer 10 minutes.
In a bowl, mix ricotta, egg, half the parmesan, basil, and red pepper flakes.
In a baking dish, layer pasta, meat sauce, and ricotta mixture, repeating, finishing with mozzarella and remaining parmesan on top.
Cover with foil, bake 20 minutes, then uncover and bake 10-15 more minutes until bubbly and golden.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular ziti -- substitute a certified gluten-free penne or ziti-style pasta, watching it closely as it can overcook faster.
Swap the ground beef for Italian-style plant-based crumbles, or omit it for a vegetarian version -- simmer the sauce a few extra minutes to concentrate flavor either way.
Do NOT use ricotta, mozzarella, or parmesan -- substitute dairy-free ricotta-style and mozzarella-style alternatives, and skip the parmesan or use a dairy-free hard-cheese alternative.
Do NOT use egg in the ricotta mixture -- simply omit it; the ricotta layer will be slightly looser but still sets fine when baked.

name: Shepherd's Pie
description: Ground beef and gravy under a blanket of buttery mashed potatoes -- I browned the meat harder than usual this time, since that char does a lot of the flavor lifting salt used to.
steps: Boil potatoes in unsalted water until tender, about 15 minutes; drain.
Mash potatoes with butter and milk until smooth; season with pepper. Set aside.
Preheat oven to 400F. Brown beef with onion and carrots until deeply caramelized; drain fat.
Stir in garlic and tomato paste, then flour, cooking 1 minute, then whisk in broth until thickened.
Stir in peas, spread the meat mixture in a baking dish, and top with mashed potatoes, fluffing with a fork.
Bake 20-25 minutes until the top is golden in spots.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the ground beef for ground lamb -- the traditional version of this dish -- and swap the beef broth for a low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth so no beef remains in the gravy.
Do NOT use butter or milk in the mash -- substitute a dairy-free butter alternative and unsweetened plain oat milk.
Do NOT use regular flour -- substitute cornstarch (1 tbsp) whisked into a little cold broth before adding to the pan.

name: Chicken and Dumplings
description: This is the one my wife still asks for by name -- the broth has to reduce down enough to taste rich on its own, because dumplings this fluffy will show you exactly where the flavor is thin.
steps: Simmer chicken thighs in broth with bay leaf, half the onion, and half the carrots and celery until cooked through, about 30 minutes. Remove chicken, shred the meat, discard bones and skin, then strain and reserve the broth.
Melt butter in the same pot and sauté the remaining onion, carrots, celery, and garlic until softened.
Sprinkle in the roux flour, cook 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the reserved broth until smooth. Simmer 10 minutes until slightly thickened; return the shredded chicken, and add thyme and pepper.
Make the dumpling dough by whisking dumpling flour, baking powder, and a pinch of pepper, then stirring in milk just until a soft dough forms -- don't overmix.
Drop spoonfuls of dough onto the simmering stew, cover, and cook without lifting the lid for 15-18 minutes until the dumplings are puffed and cooked through.
Stir in parsley just before serving.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use butter or milk -- substitute a dairy-free butter alternative for the roux and unsweetened plain oat milk in the dumpling dough.
Do NOT use regular flour for the roux or dumplings -- substitute a 1:1 gluten-free flour blend in both, and expect the dumplings to hold together a little more delicately.

name: Swiss Steak
description: A cheap cut of round steak braised down with tomatoes and peppers until it's fork-tender -- this was a regular in my mother's kitchen and it still holds up.
steps: Pound steak to tenderize, cut into portions, season with pepper, and dredge in flour.
Sear in olive oil in a Dutch oven until browned on both sides; remove.
Sauté onion, bell pepper, and garlic until softened.
Return the steak to the pot, and add tomatoes, broth, paprika, and thyme.
Cover and simmer on low (or braise at 325F) for about 90 minutes until the steak is fork-tender.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the round steak for a pork round cut or venison steak of similar thickness, keeping the same braise time, and swap the beef broth for a low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth so no beef remains in the dish.
Do NOT use regular flour for dredging -- substitute cornstarch or a 1:1 gluten-free flour blend.

name: Salisbury Steak with Mushroom Gravy
description: Ground beef patties in a dark mushroom gravy -- a little Dijon and balsamic in the gravy stands in for the salt without turning it into something my mother wouldn't recognize.
steps: Mix ground beef, breadcrumbs, egg, half the onion, half the garlic, mustard, and pepper. Shape into 4-6 oval patties.
Sear patties in olive oil in a skillet until browned on both sides; remove.
In the same skillet, sauté the remaining onion, garlic, and mushrooms until golden.
Sprinkle flour over the mushrooms, cook 1 minute, then whisk in broth and balsamic vinegar until the gravy thickens.
Return patties to the skillet, spoon gravy over them, cover, and simmer 10-12 minutes until cooked through.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the ground beef for ground bison or ground turkey, checking for doneness a few minutes earlier if using turkey, and swap the beef broth for a low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth in the gravy so no beef remains in the dish.
Do NOT use regular breadcrumbs or flour -- substitute certified gluten-free breadcrumbs in the patties and cornstarch to thicken the gravy.
Do NOT use egg -- substitute 1 tbsp ground flaxseed whisked with 3 tbsp water, rested 5 minutes, as the binder.

name: Pork Chops with Apples and Onions
description: Bone-in chops, sweet apples, and a mustardy pan sauce -- an old standby that doesn't need much salt when the apples and cider are doing the work.
steps: Season pork chops with pepper. Sear in butter and oil over medium-high heat, 3-4 minutes per side; remove.
Add onion to the skillet, sauté until softened, then add apples and cook 3-4 minutes.
Stir in apple cider, broth, thyme, and mustard, scraping up browned bits, and simmer 5 minutes to reduce slightly.
Return chops to the skillet, spoon sauce over top, cover, and simmer 8-10 minutes until chops reach 145F.
Rest 5 minutes before serving with the apples and pan sauce.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the pork chops for bone-in chicken thighs, adjusting cook time until they reach 165F.
Do NOT use butter -- substitute a dairy-free butter alternative or an extra tablespoon of olive oil.

name: Beef Stroganoff
description: Tender beef and mushrooms in a sour cream gravy over egg noodles -- I hold back on the beef bouillon and let the browned meat and mushrooms carry the flavor instead.
steps: Boil egg noodles in unsalted water until al dente; drain and set aside.
Sear beef in butter over high heat in batches until browned but not cooked through; remove.
In the same pan, sauté mushrooms and onion until golden, then add garlic.
Sprinkle in flour, cook 1 minute, then whisk in broth until thickened, about 5 minutes.
Reduce heat to low, stir in sour cream, mustard, and pepper, then return beef to the pan just to warm through (don't let it boil).
Serve over egg noodles, topped with parsley.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the beef sirloin for venison or bison, sliced the same way and cooked the same amount of time, and swap the beef broth for a low-sodium chicken or vegetable broth so no beef remains in the dish.
Do NOT use butter or sour cream -- substitute a dairy-free butter alternative and a dairy-free sour cream alternative, stirred in off the heat.
Do NOT use regular flour or the egg noodles -- substitute cornstarch to thicken the gravy and serve over a gluten-free noodle or rice instead.
Do NOT use egg noodles -- substitute an egg-free wide pasta (gluten-free or wheat, depending on other needs).

name: Turkey Meatballs in Marinara
description: Lighter than my old beef version but I wouldn't call it diet food -- extra garlic, basil, and a long simmer in a no-salt-added marinara keep it tasting like Sunday gravy.
steps: Combine turkey, breadcrumbs, egg, parmesan, garlic, basil, oregano, and pepper in a bowl. Mix gently and roll into 1.5-inch meatballs.
Brown meatballs in a large skillet with a little oil until golden on all sides (they don't need to be cooked through yet).
Pour marinara over meatballs, cover, and simmer 20 minutes until meatballs are cooked through and the sauce has thickened slightly.
Meanwhile, boil spaghetti in unsalted water until al dente; drain.
Serve meatballs and sauce over spaghetti.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the ground turkey for ground beef or ground pork, keeping the same amounts and cook time.
Do NOT use regular breadcrumbs or spaghetti -- substitute certified gluten-free breadcrumbs in the meatballs and gluten-free spaghetti.
Do NOT use egg -- substitute 1 tbsp ground flaxseed whisked with 3 tbsp water, rested 5 minutes, as the binder.
Do NOT use parmesan -- omit it or substitute a dairy-free parmesan-style alternative.

name: Chicken Parmesan
description: Pounded thin, breaded properly, and finished under the broiler with real mozzarella -- the trick to keeping it from tasting bland without extra salt is a hot pan and a marinara that's simmered down enough to taste like something.
steps: Pound chicken breasts to an even 1/2-inch thickness and slice in half if large.
Set up a dredging station: flour, beaten egg, and panko mixed with parmesan, oregano, and pepper.
Dredge each cutlet in flour, then egg, then the breadcrumb mixture, pressing to adhere.
Pan-fry in olive oil over medium-high heat, 3-4 minutes per side, until golden; transfer to a baking dish.
Spoon marinara over each cutlet, top with mozzarella, and broil 3-5 minutes until bubbly and browned.
Serve over spaghetti tossed with the remaining marinara, garnished with basil.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular flour, panko, or spaghetti -- substitute a 1:1 gluten-free flour blend, gluten-free panko, and gluten-free spaghetti.
Do NOT use egg for the dredge -- substitute unsweetened plain dairy-free milk mixed with a spoonful of Dijon mustard to help the breadcrumbs adhere.
Do NOT use parmesan or mozzarella -- substitute dairy-free parmesan-style and mozzarella-style alternatives.

name: Split Pea Soup with Ham
description: Ham bone, split peas, and a long simmer -- this one was always salty from the ham alone, so I use less ham and finish it with a splash of vinegar to bring the flavor back up front.
steps: Rinse split peas and pick over for debris.
In a large pot, sauté onion, carrots, celery, and garlic until softened, about 5 minutes.
Add split peas, ham, broth, and bay leaves. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a simmer.
Cover partially and simmer 60-75 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the peas break down and the soup thickens.
Discard bay leaves, stir in pepper and vinegar, and adjust consistency with extra broth if needed.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the diced ham for a smoked turkey leg or smoked turkey wing, simmered whole and shredded off the bone before serving.

name: Lower-Sodium Deviled Eggs
description: These are still deviled eggs, not a science experiment -- I pulled back the salt in the filling and let vinegar, mustard, and smoked paprika do the work of making up for it. Nobody at the card table has ever noticed the difference.
steps: Place eggs in a single layer in a saucepan, cover with cold water by an inch, bring to a boil, then cover and remove from heat. Let sit 11 minutes.
Drain and transfer eggs to an ice bath for 5 minutes, then peel.
Halve eggs lengthwise and scoop yolks into a bowl. Mash yolks with mayonnaise, mustard, relish, and vinegar until smooth -- the vinegar is doing the job the extra salt used to do, so don't skip it.
Season with a small pinch of pepper (go light on added salt -- the relish and mustard already carry some).
Pipe or spoon filling back into egg whites. Dust with smoked paprika and scatter chives over top.
Chill at least 30 minutes before serving so the flavors settle.

alternateRecipe.name: Smoky Deviled Potato Bites
alternateRecipe.description: You lose the egg white as the vessel, so this isn't a swap so much as a cousin recipe -- but it hits the same smoked paprika and tang notes and disappears off the tray just as fast.
steps: Preheat oven to 400F. Toss halved baby potatoes with olive oil, spread cut-side down on a sheet pan, and roast 20-25 minutes until tender and lightly browned.
Let cool slightly, then scoop out a small well in the cut side of each half with a spoon and set the scooped potato aside.
Mash the scooped potato with vegan mayonnaise, mustard, relish, and vinegar until smooth.
Spoon or pipe the filling back into the potato wells.
Dust with smoked paprika, top with chives, and serve warm or at room temperature.

name: Classic Pigs in a Blanket
description: Every football Sunday of my life has had a tray of these on it. Golden dough, a good snap on the sausage, and a mustard for dipping -- there's no improving on it, just doing it right.
steps: Preheat oven to 375F and line a sheet pan with parchment.
Unroll crescent dough and separate into triangles. Cut each triangle lengthwise into 2-3 narrow strips depending on how many sausages you have.
Pat sausages dry, then wrap a strip of dough around each one, tucking the ends underneath so they don't unroll in the oven.
Arrange seam-side down on the sheet pan, brush with melted butter, and sprinkle with everything seasoning.
Bake 12-15 minutes until the dough is deep golden brown.
Let cool 5 minutes -- they hold their filling better once they've rested a bit -- and serve with grainy mustard.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular crescent roll dough -- substitute a certified gluten-free crescent or biscuit dough (several brands make one now) and confirm the everything seasoning blend is labeled gluten-free.
Do NOT use a standard everything bagel seasoning blend -- most contain sesame seeds. Substitute a sesame-free version, or simply use poppy seeds, dried minced garlic, and dried minced onion.
Swap in mini smoked chicken or turkey sausage links for the pork smokies -- same size, same snap, no loss of flavor.
Swap in a plant-based smoked sausage link (a vegan andouille-style link works well) cut into 2-inch pieces before wrapping, for a vegetarian version.
Do NOT use dairy butter for brushing -- substitute a plant-based butter or margarine; olive oil works in a pinch though it browns a little less evenly.

name: Real Pimento Cheese with Crackers
description: This is not a spread you fuss over -- sharp cheddar, real mayonnaise, diced pimentos, a little cayenne for backbone. Anything fancier than that and it stops being pimento cheese.
steps: In a bowl, beat the cream cheese until smooth, then fold in the shredded cheddar and mayonnaise until evenly combined -- don't overmix or it turns gluey.
Stir in the drained pimentos, cayenne, and black pepper.
Taste before adding any salt -- the cheddar and pimentos usually carry enough on their own.
Cover and chill at least an hour so the flavors come together.
Serve with whole grain crackers.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy cheddar and cream cheese -- substitute a good melting dairy-free cheddar-style shred and a dairy-free cream cheese. The pimentos and cayenne carry enough flavor on their own that the swap doesn't read as fake.
Do NOT use regular egg-based mayonnaise -- substitute an egg-free mayonnaise (most vegan mayos work fine in this recipe).
Do NOT serve with standard wheat crackers -- substitute a gluten-free cracker, or sliced cucumber and celery for scooping.

name: Sausage-Stuffed Mushroom Caps
description: A church-potluck standby done properly -- browned sausage, real cream cheese, a little parmesan, packed into a good-sized mushroom cap and baked until the tops just start to brown.

ingredients.name: large cremini or white mushrooms, stems removed

steps: Preheat oven to 375F. Brush mushroom caps lightly with olive oil and arrange stem-side up on a sheet pan.
In a skillet over medium heat, brown the sausage, breaking it up as it cooks, until fully cooked through. Drain any excess fat.
In a bowl, mix the cooked sausage with cream cheese, parmesan, breadcrumbs, garlic, and parsley until well combined.
Spoon the filling into the mushroom caps, mounding slightly.
Bake 18-20 minutes until the mushrooms release their liquid and the tops are lightly golden.
Let sit 5 minutes before serving -- they hold heat and the filling firms up a touch.

adaptations.instructions: Use Italian-style turkey or chicken breakfast sausage in place of pork sausage -- season it up with a little extra fennel and black pepper if the brand runs mild.
Swap the sausage for a finely chopped mix of sauteed mushroom stems, shallot, and a plant-based sausage crumble for a vegetarian filling with the same savory depth.
Do NOT use dairy cream cheese and parmesan -- substitute a dairy-free cream cheese and a dairy-free parmesan alternative (or nutritional yeast for the salty, savory note).
Do NOT use regular breadcrumbs -- substitute a gluten-free breadcrumb or crushed gluten-free crackers.

name: Lower-Sodium Homemade Chex-Style Snack Mix
description: This is my signature move applied to a snack bowl instead of a pot roast: half the salt of the box recipe, made up for with more garlic and onion powder, smoked paprika, and a splash of low-sodium tamari for the savory backbone. Tastes like the mix you grew up on, not a diet version of it.
steps: Preheat oven to 250F. In a very large bowl, combine the cereals, pretzel sticks, and mixed nuts.
Whisk the melted butter with the tamari, garlic powder, onion powder, smoked paprika, and cayenne -- this seasoned butter is doing the flavor work the extra salt used to do.
Pour the butter mixture over the cereal mix and toss thoroughly, using two spatulas or your hands, until every piece is coated.
Spread in a thin layer across two sheet pans.
Bake 45 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes, until everything is crisp and lightly toasted.
Cool completely on the pans before storing -- it crisps up more as it cools.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use wheat Chex or regular pretzel sticks -- substitute corn and rice Chex only, plus a certified gluten-free pretzel stick, and confirm the tamari is labeled gluten-free (most are, but check the bottle).
Do NOT include mixed nuts -- substitute roasted pepitas or sunflower seeds for the same crunch without the tree nut risk.
Do NOT use dairy butter -- substitute melted plant-based butter or a neutral oil like avocado oil.
Do NOT use tamari or soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos for the same umami, savory note without soy.

name: Homemade Soft Pretzel Bites with Beer Cheese Dip
description: This is the one I actually enjoy standing at the counter for -- proofing the dough, the baking-soda bath that gives real pretzels their crust, and a beer cheese dip that isn't shy about the cheddar. Worth the extra steps for a Saturday.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the bowl

steps: Stir warm water, yeast, and sugar together and let sit 5-10 minutes until foamy.

In a large bowl or stand mixer, combine flour and salt, add the yeast mixture and melted butter, and knead 6-8 minutes until smooth and elastic. Place in a greased bowl, cover, and let rise 1 hour until doubled.
Preheat oven to 425F and line two sheet pans with parchment. Bring 8 cups water and the baking soda to a boil in a wide pot.
Punch down dough, divide into 6 pieces, and roll each into a long rope. Cut ropes into 1 1/2-inch bites.
Boil bites in batches for 20-30 seconds each, then lift out with a slotted spoon onto the sheet pans.
Brush bites with beaten egg, sprinkle with pretzel salt, and bake 12-15 minutes until deep golden brown.

For the dip: combine cheddar, cream cheese, beer, and garlic in a small saucepan over low heat, stirring until melted and smooth. Whisk in mustard and a cornstarch slurry (cornstarch dissolved in a splash of water), and cook 2-3 minutes until thickened.
Serve pretzel bites warm with the beer cheese dip alongside.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use all-purpose flour or regular beer -- substitute a 1:1 gluten-free flour blend with 1/2 teaspoon xanthan gum added for the dough, and use a certified gluten-free beer (or a gluten-free chicken broth) in the dip. The dough will be a touch stickier; flour your hands, not the counter.

Do NOT use dairy butter, cheddar, and cream cheese -- substitute a plant-based butter in the dough, and a good melting dairy-free cheddar plus dairy-free cream cheese in the dip. Add an extra pinch of smoked paprika to the dip since dairy-free cheese needs a little help carrying flavor.
Do NOT use an egg wash -- substitute a wash of melted plant-based butter, or plain water with a small pinch of sugar, brushed on before salting for the same shine.

name: Classic Double-Crust Apple Pie
description: This is the pie you grew up with, not a reinvention of it -- flaky all-butter crust, apples that hold their shape, and just enough spice that you can still taste the fruit. I cut the sugar back a touch and lean on lemon and cinnamon so nobody notices.

ingredients.name: apples (mix of Granny Smith and Honeycrisp), peeled and sliced

steps: Cut cold butter into flour and salt with a pastry cutter or your fingers until pea-sized crumbs form.
Add ice water a tablespoon at a time until the dough just comes together. Divide in two, flatten into discs, wrap and chill at least 1 hour.
Toss sliced apples with sugar, lemon juice, cinnamon, nutmeg, and cornstarch. Let sit 15 minutes so the juices release.
Preheat oven to 425F. Roll out one disc and line a 9-inch pie plate.
Fill with the apple mixture, mounding slightly in the center.
Roll out the second disc, lay over the top, and crimp the edges. Cut a few vents in the top crust.
Brush with egg wash. Bake 20 minutes at 425F, then reduce to 375F and bake another 30-35 minutes until the crust is deep golden and juices bubble through the vents.
Cool at least 2 hours before slicing so it sets -- I know it's hard to wait.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular all-purpose flour -- substitute a 1:1 gluten-free baking flour blend that includes xanthan gum, measured cup for cup, for both the flour in the crust.
Do NOT use dairy butter -- substitute a cold, stick-style plant-based butter alternative in the same amount; it cuts into the flour the same way.
Do NOT use an egg wash -- substitute a brush of unsweetened plant milk or melted plant butter for the same golden-brown finish.

name: Old-Fashioned Bread Pudding with Vanilla Sauce
description: The kind of bread pudding that uses up the heel of the loaf instead of the trash can -- custardy in the middle, a little crisp on top, warm vanilla sauce poured over. No novelty toppings, just the classic.

ingredients.name: unsalted butter, for pan and sauce

steps: Preheat oven to 350F. Butter a 9x13 baking dish and scatter the bread cubes evenly.
Whisk milk, cream, eggs, sugar, vanilla, and cinnamon together until smooth.
Pour the custard over the bread, pressing cubes down so they soak. Scatter raisins over the top. Let sit 15 minutes.
Bake 40-45 minutes until the top is golden and the center is just set (a knife should come out mostly clean).
Melt the remaining butter with a splash of cream and a spoonful of sugar in a small saucepan for a simple vanilla sauce; drizzle over each serving.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular bread -- substitute a day-old gluten-free sandwich loaf, cubed the same way; it soaks up custard just as well once it's a bit stale.
Do NOT use whole milk, heavy cream, or dairy butter -- substitute full-fat oat milk for the milk and cream, and a plant-based butter for the pan and sauce.
Do NOT use whole eggs -- substitute a commercial egg replacer whisked to the package's custard ratio, or 4 tablespoons cornstarch whisked into the milk to help the custard set instead.

name: Portion-Right Chocolate Chip Cookies
description: Same cookie you remember, just baked as a smaller batch you won't eat six of standing at the counter. I dropped some of the white sugar without touching the brown sugar, so the chew is still there. Note: commercial chocolate chip brands vary in whether they contain soy lecithin or trace milk fat -- if soy or dairy is a strict allergy in your house, check the specific bag's label rather than assuming.
steps: Preheat oven to 375F and line two baking sheets with parchment.
Whisk flour, baking soda, and salt together in a bowl.
Cream butter with both sugars until light and fluffy, about 2 minutes.
Beat in eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Mix in the dry ingredients just until combined, then fold in the chocolate chips.
Drop rounded tablespoons of dough onto the sheets, spaced 2 inches apart.
Bake 9-11 minutes until the edges are golden but the centers still look slightly underdone.
Cool on the sheet 5 minutes before moving to a rack.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular all-purpose flour -- substitute a 1:1 gluten-free baking flour blend measured cup for cup; the dough will be a touch stickier, which is normal.
Do NOT use dairy butter -- substitute a stick-style plant-based butter in the same amount; cream it the same way.
Do NOT use whole eggs -- substitute 2 flax eggs (2 tablespoons ground flaxseed plus 6 tablespoons water, rested 5 minutes until gelled).

name: Classic Peanut Butter Cookies
description: Crosshatch on top, salty-sweet all the way through -- the real thing, not a peanut-adjacent shortcut. If peanuts are off the table in your house, see the sunflower seed butter version below; it holds up just as well.
steps: Preheat oven to 350F and line two baking sheets with parchment.
Cream peanut butter, butter, and both sugars together until smooth.
Beat in the egg and vanilla.
Whisk flour, baking soda, and salt together, then mix into the wet ingredients until a soft dough forms.
Roll into 1-inch balls, place on the sheets, and press a crosshatch pattern into each with a fork.
Bake 9-10 minutes until just set at the edges -- they'll firm up as they cool, so don't overbake.
Cool on the sheet 5 minutes before moving to a rack.

alternateRecipe.name: Sunflower Seed Butter Cookies
alternateRecipe.description: Built the same way as the classic, just with sunflower seed butter standing in for peanut butter -- same crosshatch, same salty-sweet chew, nobody misses the peanuts.
steps: Preheat oven to 350F and line two baking sheets with parchment.
Cream sunflower seed butter, butter, and both sugars together until smooth.
Beat in the egg and vanilla.
Whisk flour, baking soda, and salt together, then mix into the wet ingredients until a soft dough forms.
Roll into 1-inch balls, place on the sheets, and press a crosshatch pattern into each with a fork.
Bake 9-10 minutes until just set at the edges.
Cool on the sheet 5 minutes before moving to a rack. Note: dough may turn slightly green around the edges from a natural reaction between the seed butter and baking soda -- harmless, just cosmetic.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy butter -- substitute a stick-style plant-based butter in the same amount.
Do NOT use a whole egg -- substitute 1 flax egg (1 tablespoon ground flaxseed plus 3 tablespoons water, rested 5 minutes until gelled).
Do NOT use regular all-purpose flour -- substitute a 1:1 gluten-free baking flour blend measured cup for cup.

name: Banana Cream Pie
description: A real banana cream pie: blind-baked crust, cooked pastry cream, sliced bananas layered in, and softly whipped cream on top -- not a pudding-mix shortcut. Worth the extra steps and the chill time.
steps: Make the crust: cut cold butter into flour and salt until pea-sized crumbs form, add ice water until dough comes together, chill 1 hour.
Roll out and fit into a 9-inch pie plate, crimp edges, dock with a fork, and chill another 20 minutes.
Blind bake at 400F with pie weights for 15 minutes, remove weights, bake 8-10 more minutes until golden. Cool completely.
Make the pastry cream: whisk milk, sugar, and cornstarch in a saucepan over medium heat until it just starts to thicken.
Whisk egg yolks in a bowl, then temper with a ladle of the hot milk mixture before whisking back into the pan.
Cook, stirring constantly, until thick enough to hold a ribbon, about 3-4 minutes. Remove from heat and stir in butter and vanilla.
Press plastic wrap directly onto the surface of the pastry cream and chill at least 1 hour.
Layer sliced bananas over the cooled crust, spread the pastry cream over top, then add another layer of bananas if you like it extra banana-forward.
Whip heavy cream with powdered sugar to soft peaks and spread or pipe over the pie. Chill at least 2 hours before slicing.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular all-purpose flour -- substitute a 1:1 gluten-free baking flour blend measured cup for cup for the crust.

Do NOT use whole milk, heavy cream, or dairy butter -- substitute full-fat coconut milk for the milk, chilled coconut cream for the whipped topping, and plant-based butter throughout, in the same amounts.
Do NOT use egg yolks -- substitute an extra 3 tablespoons cornstarch whisked into the milk in place of the yolks; the pastry cream will set slightly firmer, which is fine here.

name: Old-Fashioned Stovetop Rice Pudding
description: The rice pudding my mother made on a Sunday afternoon -- simmered slow on the stove until it's thick and creamy, no shortcuts, no instant rice.
steps: In a heavy-bottomed saucepan, combine milk, rice, sugar, and salt. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring often so it doesn't scorch on the bottom.
Reduce heat to low and let it simmer uncovered 25-30 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until the rice is tender and the mixture has thickened to a loose custard consistency.
Whisk the egg yolks in a small bowl with a ladleful of the hot milk mixture to temper them, then stir the tempered yolks back into the pot.
Cook another 3-4 minutes over low heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens further -- don't let it boil or the yolks will curdle.
Stir in the raisins, cinnamon, and vanilla. Remove from heat.
Serve warm, or chill covered for a couple of hours -- it thickens more as it cools.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy milk -- substitute a full-fat unsweetened oat milk or canned coconut milk; the pudding will be slightly less rich but still sets up creamy.
Do NOT use egg yolks -- substitute a slurry of 2 tablespoons cornstarch whisked into 3 tablespoons cold water, stirred in during the last 5 minutes of simmering until thickened.

name: Classic Apple Crisp
description: Done the way it's supposed to be done -- tart apples, a buttery oat topping, nothing fancy layered on top. I cut the sugar back some but made up for it with more cinnamon and a squeeze of lemon so it still tastes like the real thing.

ingredients.name: Granny Smith apples, peeled and sliced

steps: Preheat oven to 375°F. Butter a 9x9-inch baking dish.
Toss the sliced apples with lemon juice, the first measure of brown sugar, 1/2 teaspoon of the cinnamon, and the nutmeg. Spread in the baking dish.
In a bowl, combine flour, oats, the remaining brown sugar, remaining cinnamon, and salt.
Cut the cold butter into the dry mixture with your fingers or a pastry cutter until it looks like coarse, pea-sized crumbs.
Scatter the topping evenly over the apples.
Bake 40-45 minutes, until the topping is golden and the apples are bubbling at the edges.
Let it rest 10 minutes before serving -- it's better warm than piping hot, and the juices set up a little.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use all-purpose flour -- substitute a 1:1 gluten-free baking flour blend, and confirm the oats are labeled certified gluten-free (regular oats are often cross-contaminated with wheat).
Do NOT use dairy butter -- substitute a plant-based butter stick, cold and cubed the same way.

name: Bread Pudding with Bourbon Caramel Sauce
description: This is a diner-style bread pudding done properly -- day-old bread soaked overnight in a real custard, baked until the top is crisp, and finished with a bourbon caramel that isn't shy about it.
steps: Spread the bread cubes in a buttered 9x13-inch baking dish.
Whisk together milk, cream, eggs, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, and salt.
Pour the custard over the bread, pressing down gently so every cube soaks. Cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Preheat oven to 350°F. Bake uncovered 40-45 minutes, until puffed, golden, and just set in the center.
While it bakes, melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, whisk in the brown sugar, and cook 2 minutes until it dissolves.
Slowly whisk in the cream, then simmer 3-4 minutes until slightly thickened. Off heat, stir in the bourbon.
Serve the bread pudding warm with the sauce poured over.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular French bread -- substitute a sturdy certified gluten-free bread, cubed and left out an extra day so it's dry enough to soak without turning mushy.

Do NOT use dairy milk, cream, or butter -- substitute full-fat canned coconut milk for the milk and both creams, and a plant-based butter stick for the butter; the caramel sauce will taste faintly of coconut but still sets up glossy.

alternateRecipe.name: Custard-Free Bread Pudding with Bourbon Caramel Sauce
alternateRecipe.description: Same soaked-bread base, but I thicken the custard with cornstarch instead of eggs so it still sets up sliceable, not soupy.
steps: Spread the bread cubes in a buttered 9x13-inch baking dish.
Whisk the cornstarch into 1/2 cup of the milk until smooth, then whisk in the rest of the milk, the cream, sugar, vanilla, cinnamon, and salt.
Pour over the bread, pressing down so every cube soaks. Cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours, or overnight.
Preheat oven to 350°F. Bake uncovered 40-45 minutes, until golden and set in the center -- it will look slightly less puffed than an egg version, that's normal.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat, whisk in the brown sugar, and cook 2 minutes until dissolved.
Slowly whisk in the cream, then simmer 3-4 minutes until slightly thickened. Off heat, stir in the bourbon.
Serve warm with the sauce poured over.

name: Classic Pecan Pie
description: A proper Southern pecan pie, homemade crust and all -- the kind that sets up glossy and sliceable, not the gloopy version you get from a box mix.
steps: Make the crust: pulse flour and salt, cut in cold butter until pea-sized crumbs form, drizzle in ice water a tablespoon at a time until dough just comes together. Wrap and chill 1 hour.
Roll the dough out and fit into a 9-inch pie plate, crimping the edges. Chill while you make the filling.
Preheat oven to 350°F.
Whisk eggs, corn syrup, brown sugar, melted butter, vanilla, and salt together until smooth.
Scatter the pecans in the crust, then pour the filling over them -- they'll float and settle into an even layer as it bakes.
Bake 50-55 minutes, until the edges are set and the center has a slight jiggle, like set gelatin. Tent with foil if the crust browns too fast.
Cool completely, at least 3 hours, before slicing -- it needs that time to fully set.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use all-purpose flour in the crust -- substitute a 1:1 gluten-free pie crust blend, or use a store-bought certified gluten-free pie shell.
Do NOT use dairy butter -- substitute a plant-based butter stick in both the crust and filling.

alternateRecipe.name: Egg-Free Chess-Style Pecan Pie
alternateRecipe.description: Sets up with a cornstarch custard instead of eggs -- still sliceable, still glossy, just leans a little more toward chess pie in texture.
steps: Make and blind-chill the crust as in the classic recipe.
Preheat oven to 350°F.
Whisk cornstarch into the milk until smooth, then whisk in corn syrup, brown sugar, melted butter, vanilla, and salt.
Scatter pecans in the crust, pour the filling over them.
Bake 50-55 minutes, until set with just a slight jiggle in the center; tent with foil if the crust browns too fast.
Cool completely, at least 3 hours, before slicing.

alternateRecipe.name: Classic Oatmeal Pie
alternateRecipe.description: An old Southern classic that predates the modern pecan pie boom -- same glossy, gooey filling, but oats stand in for nuts, so it's every bit as much a real recipe as its more famous cousin.
steps: Make the crust as in the classic recipe and chill.
Preheat oven to 350°F.
Whisk eggs, corn syrup, brown sugar, melted butter, vanilla, and salt until smooth. Stir in the oats.
Pour the filling into the crust.
Bake 45-50 minutes, until the edges are set and the center has a slight jiggle.
Cool completely, at least 3 hours, before slicing.

name: Fluffy Rice-Flour Buttermilk Pancakes
description: My go-to starting point for a gluten-free household -- a xanthan-gum-inclusive 1:1 flour blend gives these real fluffy structure instead of the gummy centers plain rice flour leaves you with.
steps: Whisk together the GF flour blend, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk the buttermilk, eggs, and melted butter until smooth.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and stir just until combined -- a few lumps are fine; overmixing makes GF batter gummy.
Let the batter rest 5 minutes so the xanthan gum fully hydrates -- this is the step that gives these their fluffy structure instead of a gummy center.
Heat a griddle over medium with a light coating of oil. Pour 1/4-cup portions and cook until bubbles form on the surface and the edges look dry, about 3 minutes, then flip and cook 2 more minutes.
Serve warm with maple syrup.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use the dairy buttermilk or butter -- substitute 1 3/4 cups unsweetened plant milk mixed with 1 3/4 tbsp lemon juice (rested 5 minutes to curdle) for the buttermilk, and a dairy-free butter or neutral oil for the melted butter.
Do NOT use the eggs -- substitute 2 flax eggs (2 tbsp ground flaxseed whisked with 6 tbsp water, rested 5 minutes until gel-like) for the 2 eggs.

name: Cheesy Polenta Breakfast Bowl with Fried Egg & Crispy Prosciutto
description: Stone-ground polenta is a naturally gluten-free, texture-appropriate base -- soft and spoonable with zero flour-blend workaround -- topped with a runny fried egg and shattering-crisp prosciutto.
steps: Bring the water or broth to a boil in a heavy saucepan, then whisk in the polenta in a steady stream.
Reduce heat to low and simmer, stirring often, 20-25 minutes until thick and creamy, adding more liquid if it tightens up too fast.
Stir in the butter and parmesan until melted; season with salt and pepper.
While the polenta finishes, crisp the prosciutto in a dry skillet over medium-high, about 2 minutes per side, then set aside.
In the same skillet, fry the eggs to your liking.
Divide the polenta among bowls, top each with a fried egg, crispy prosciutto, and chives.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use the parmesan and butter -- substitute a dairy-free hard-cheese alternative and olive oil or dairy-free butter; the cornmeal itself does the thickening work, so the polenta's texture holds up fine without dairy.
Do NOT use the fried egg topping -- substitute pan-seared marinated tofu triangles or a spoonful of warmed white beans for a protein topping that still plays well against the creamy polenta.
Skip the prosciutto and substitute crispy turkey bacon or a plant-based bacon for the same salty crunch.
For a meat-free bowl, skip the prosciutto entirely and top with sauteed mushrooms for a similar savory, umami note.

name: Corn Tortilla Breakfast Tacos with Chorizo & Egg
description: Corn tortillas -- confirmed corn, not a corn/wheat blend -- are the correct wrap swap here, folding and lightly charring exactly like a flour tortilla without any gluten structure behind it.
steps: Heat a large skillet over medium-high and cook the chorizo, breaking it up, until browned and crisp, about 6-8 minutes. Remove and set aside, leaving the rendered fat in the pan.
Add the onion and bell pepper to the skillet and saute 3-4 minutes until softened.
Whisk the eggs and pour into the skillet with the vegetables; scramble gently until just set.
Return the chorizo to the pan and stir to combine.
Warm the corn tortillas directly over a burner flame or in a dry skillet until pliable and lightly charred, about 20 seconds per side.
Fill the tortillas with the chorizo-egg mixture, top with cheddar, cilantro, and salsa, and serve with lime wedges.

adaptations.instructions: Skip the pork chorizo and substitute a soy-based or turkey chorizo for the same smoky, spiced flavor.
For a meat-free taco, substitute a can of drained black beans seasoned with smoked paprika and cumin for the chorizo.
Do NOT use the scrambled eggs -- substitute crumbled firm tofu sauteed with turmeric and cumin for a similar scramble texture and color.
Do NOT use the cheddar cheese -- substitute a dairy-free shredded cheese or add extra avocado for richness instead.

name: Certified GF Oat & Cornmeal Baked Breakfast Casserole
description: Built on certified gluten-free rolled oats specifically -- oats are naturally gluten-free by ingredient but the highest cross-contact-risk grain there is, so this only works as written with a bag labeled certified gluten-free.
steps: Preheat oven to 350F and butter (or oil) a 9x13-inch baking dish.
In a large bowl, whisk together the certified gluten-free oats, cornmeal, baking powder, and cinnamon.
In a separate bowl, whisk the milk, eggs, maple syrup, melted butter, and vanilla.
Pour the wet mixture over the dry and stir to combine; fold in the walnuts and blueberries.
Pour into the prepared dish and bake 35-40 minutes until set in the center and lightly golden on top.
Cool 5 minutes before slicing into squares.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use the milk and butter -- substitute unsweetened plant milk and a dairy-free butter or coconut oil in equal amounts.
Do NOT use the eggs -- substitute 3 flax eggs (3 tbsp ground flaxseed whisked with 9 tbsp water, rested 5 minutes).
Do NOT use the walnuts -- substitute toasted pepitas (pumpkin seeds) or sunflower seeds for the same crunch with zero tree-nut risk.

name: Xanthan-Gum Blend Belgian Waffles with Toasted Pecans
description: A proper waffle needs a chewy, structured crumb to hold up in the iron, so this leans on a xanthan-gum-inclusive 1:1 GF flour blend plus whipped egg whites for lift -- plain rice flour alone would crumble apart.
steps: In a large bowl, whisk together the GF flour blend, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
In another bowl, whisk the egg yolks, milk, melted butter, and vanilla; pour into the dry ingredients and whisk until smooth.
In a clean bowl, whip the egg whites to soft peaks, then gently fold into the batter -- this is what gives a GF waffle its lift, since the flour blend alone won't do it.
Preheat a waffle iron and lightly grease. Pour batter in and cook until deeply golden and crisp, about 4-5 minutes.
Sprinkle toasted pecans over each waffle as it comes off the iron so they stay crunchy.
Serve immediately with maple syrup.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use the whole milk and butter -- substitute unsweetened plant milk and dairy-free butter in equal amounts.

Do NOT use the eggs -- note that the whipped egg whites are structural here, so a flax-egg swap won't whip; use a commercial GF vegan waffle mix's egg-replacer blend for the best rise, or accept a denser, less crisp waffle with 3 flax eggs.
Do NOT use the pecans -- substitute toasted sunflower seeds or omit entirely for a nut-free waffle.

name: Shakshuka with GF Crusty Bread for Dipping
description: The tomato-pepper base cooks once for the whole table; the only real branch point is what's on the side, which makes this a genuine parallel-track breakfast, not a compromise plate.
steps: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium. Add onion and bell pepper and cook 5-6 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic, cumin, and smoked paprika and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes, season with salt, and simmer 10 minutes until slightly thickened -- this is the shared base that feeds the whole table.
Use a spoon to make 6 wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook 6-8 minutes until whites are set and yolks are still soft.
Scatter feta and parsley over the top.
Serve straight from the skillet with warm gluten-free crusty bread for dipping.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use the feta cheese -- substitute a dairy-free feta-style crumble or simply omit and finish with a drizzle of olive oil.

alternateRecipe.name: Silken Tofu Shakshuka
alternateRecipe.description: The same simmered tomato-pepper base as the egg version, poached with soft tofu rounds instead -- built so an egg-free eater still eats from the same pan as everyone else.

ingredients.name: soft silken tofu, cut into 6 rounds

steps: Heat olive oil in a large skillet over medium. Add onion and bell pepper and cook 5-6 minutes until softened.
Stir in garlic, cumin, and smoked paprika and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the crushed tomatoes, season with salt, and simmer 10 minutes until slightly thickened.
Nestle the tofu rounds into the sauce in a single layer and spoon a little sauce over each. Cover and simmer 8-10 minutes to warm through and let the tofu take on the sauce's flavor.
Scatter feta and parsley over the top.
Serve straight from the skillet with warm gluten-free crusty bread for dipping.

name: Delicate GF Crepes with Almond-Hazelnut Spread
description: Crepe batter has almost no margin for error gluten-free -- too little xanthan gum and the crepe tears the moment you flip it -- so this ratio and rest time are tuned specifically to fold without cracking.
steps: In a blender, combine the GF flour blend, eggs, milk, melted butter, and salt. Blend until completely smooth, about 30 seconds.
Let the batter rest in the refrigerator 30 minutes -- this fully hydrates the xanthan gum, which is what keeps a gluten-free crepe from tearing when you flip it.
Heat a nonstick crepe pan or skillet over medium and lightly butter it. Pour in a thin layer of batter, swirling to coat the pan evenly.
Cook 1-2 minutes until the edges lift and the underside is lightly golden, then flip carefully with a thin spatula and cook 30 seconds more.
Spread each warm crepe with chocolate-hazelnut spread, fold into quarters, and top with toasted almonds and sliced strawberries.
Serve immediately while still warm.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use the milk and butter -- substitute unsweetened plant milk and dairy-free butter; also swap in a dairy-free chocolate-hazelnut spread, since most mainstream brands contain milk.

Do NOT use the eggs -- note that GF crepe batter depends heavily on egg protein for pliability, so a flax-egg substitute will be more fragile and prone to tearing when folded; use a commercial GF vegan crepe mix for the most reliable result.
Do NOT use the chocolate-hazelnut spread or almonds -- substitute a sunflower-seed butter spread and top with toasted pepitas instead.

name: Gluten-Free Breakfast Fried Rice with Tamari-Glazed Bacon
description: My signature stir-fry move applied to breakfast: the fried-rice base browns in the pan the same way either way, and it's verified gluten-free tamari standing in for soy sauce that keeps the whole skillet safe.
steps: Cook the bacon in a large skillet or wok over medium heat until crisp, about 6 minutes. Remove, chop, and set aside, reserving 1 tbsp of the fat in the pan.
Add the onion and garlic and stir-fry 2 minutes, then push to one side. Pour the beaten eggs into the empty side and scramble until just set, then mix through.
Add the rice, breaking up clumps, and stir-fry 3-4 minutes until heated through and starting to crisp in spots.

Stir in the peas and carrots, then drizzle the gluten-free tamari and sesame oil over the rice and toss to coat evenly -- this is the branch point: the shared fried-rice base cooks identically, and swapping in verified GF tamari here is what makes the whole skillet gluten-free.
Fold the crispy bacon back in, top with sliced green onions, and serve hot.

adaptations.instructions: Skip the pork bacon and substitute turkey bacon or a plant-based bacon for the same smoky, crisp topping.
For a meat-free version, omit the bacon and add pan-seared mushrooms for a savory, umami substitute.
Do NOT use the eggs -- substitute crumbled firm tofu sauteed with a pinch of turmeric for a similar scrambled texture and color.
Do NOT use the gluten-free tamari -- substitute coconut aminos in equal amount for a similar savory-sweet glaze.
Do NOT use the toasted sesame oil -- substitute avocado oil or olive oil; you'll lose the nutty aroma but the dish stays safe.

name: Parallel-Track Chicken Pad See Ew
description: My take on the takeout classic, split at the sauce step: certified gluten-free tamari and wide rice noodles mean the whole wok stays gluten-free without a second pan — no compromise pad see ew for anyone at the table.
steps: Soak wide rice noodles in warm water 20-30 minutes until pliable but not soft; drain.
Slice chicken thighs thin against the grain; season lightly.
Whisk tamari, brown sugar, and rice vinegar together for the sauce.
Heat oil in a wok over high heat; sear chicken until just cooked through, 3-4 minutes, then push to one side.
Crack eggs into the cleared space and scramble briefly, then fold together with the chicken.
Add garlic and broccolini, stir 1 minute, then add drained noodles and sauce; toss over high heat until noodles are glossy and slightly charred in spots, about 3 minutes.
Serve immediately.

adaptations.instructions: Swap the chicken thighs for extra-firm tofu, pressed and cubed, or thinly sliced flank steak — sear the same way before adding the eggs.
Do NOT use egg — substitute 4 oz of crumbled extra-firm tofu, pan-fried until lightly golden, folded in at the same step for texture and protein.
Do NOT use tamari — substitute an equal amount of coconut aminos, and confirm any additional soy-based condiments at the table are soy-free.

name: Cornmeal-Crusted Chicken Tenders with Polenta Fries
description: A genuinely crunchy tender without a flour dredge — buttermilk-brined chicken in a straight cornmeal crust, plated with polenta fries so nobody's fries came out of a wheat-dusted fryer basket.
steps: Marinate chicken tenders in buttermilk at least 1 hour (or overnight) in the fridge.
Slice polenta tube into fry-shaped batons, toss with 1 tbsp olive oil and salt, and roast at 425°F for 25-30 minutes, flipping once, until crisp-edged.
Whisk eggs in one shallow bowl; combine cornmeal, parmesan, smoked paprika, and salt in a second.
Remove chicken from buttermilk, dip in egg, then press firmly into the cornmeal mixture to coat.
Pan-fry in remaining olive oil over medium heat, 4-5 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through (165°F internal).
Rest 2 minutes, then serve tenders alongside the polenta fries.

adaptations.instructions: Swap chicken tenders for thick-cut zucchini planks or firm white fish fillets, using the same buttermilk soak and cornmeal crust.

Do NOT use dairy buttermilk or parmesan — substitute a cup of unsweetened plant milk with 1 tbsp lemon juice stirred in (a quick dairy-free buttermilk) and swap the parmesan for a dairy-free hard cheese alternative or omit it and add extra smoked paprika.
Do NOT use egg — substitute a second round of the dairy-free buttermilk (or a flax egg: 1 tbsp ground flax + 3 tbsp water, rested 5 minutes) as the binder before pressing into the cornmeal.

name: Turkey & Jasmine Rice Bowl with Sesame-Tamari Glaze
description: A fast weekday bowl built the way I build every grain bowl — rice as the neutral base, then a glossy tamari-sesame glaze that stays gluten-free because it never went near a bottle of soy sauce.
steps: Cook jasmine rice according to package directions; keep warm.
Steam shelled edamame 3-4 minutes; set aside.
Brown ground turkey in a skillet with garlic and ginger, breaking it up, until cooked through, about 6-8 minutes.
Stir in tamari and sesame oil, coating the turkey; simmer 1 minute to glaze.
Divide rice into bowls, top with glazed turkey, shredded carrots, and edamame.
Finish with sesame seeds and green onion.

adaptations.instructions: Swap ground turkey for ground chicken or a plant-based ground crumble, browning the same way.
Do NOT use tamari or edamame — substitute coconut aminos for the tamari and swap the edamame for steamed green beans or extra shredded carrot.
Do NOT use sesame oil or sesame seeds — substitute avocado oil for the glaze and finish with toasted sunflower seeds instead of sesame seeds.

name: Quinoa Tabbouleh with Grilled Chicken, Feta, and Toasted Pine Nuts
description: Traditional tabbouleh is a bulgur salad, which puts it off-limits before you even start — quinoa gives the same fluffy, herb-flecked texture without a substitution conversation, so this one is naturally gluten-free, not adapted.
steps: Rinse quinoa, then cook in 2 cups water until fluffy, about 15 minutes; cool.
Season chicken breast, grill or pan-sear 6-7 minutes per side until 165°F internal, then rest and slice.
Toss cooled quinoa with parsley, mint, cucumber, and cherry tomatoes.
Whisk lemon juice and olive oil, season with salt, and dress the salad.
Divide onto plates, top with sliced chicken, crumbled feta, and toasted pine nuts.

adaptations.instructions: Swap grilled chicken for grilled shrimp or chickpeas for a vegetarian version.
Do NOT use feta — substitute a dairy-free feta-style crumble or simply omit and add an extra pinch of salt and lemon zest for brightness.
Do NOT use pine nuts — substitute toasted pepitas or sunflower seeds for the same crunch, and double-check any nearby bulk-bin nut cross-contact if buying seeds loose.

name: Cauliflower Rice Teriyaki Chicken Bowl
description: Cauliflower rice earns its spot here specifically as a light, absorbing base for a glossy teriyaki glaze — the same job jasmine rice does, just lower-carb — built on a tamari sauce that was never at risk of hidden gluten to begin with.
steps: Whisk tamari, honey, garlic, and ginger for the teriyaki sauce.
Cut chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces; sear in a hot skillet 5-6 minutes until browned.
Pour in the teriyaki sauce and simmer until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce thickens and coats, about 6-8 minutes.
Meanwhile, sauté riced cauliflower in sesame oil over medium heat 5-6 minutes until tender but not mushy.
Divide cauliflower rice into bowls, top with teriyaki chicken and sauce.
Finish with sesame seeds and green onion.

adaptations.instructions: Swap chicken thighs for salmon chunks or extra-firm tofu, adjusting cook time down for either.
Do NOT use tamari — substitute coconut aminos in the same amount for the teriyaki sauce.
Do NOT use sesame oil or sesame seeds — substitute avocado oil for sautéing the cauliflower rice and finish with extra sliced green onion instead of sesame seeds.

name: Corn Tortilla Chicken Tacos with Cotija and Cabbage Slaw
description: Corn tortillas are the correct swap here, not a compromise one — just confirm the bag says corn only, since a corn-and-wheat blend shows up on some store shelves and would quietly undo the whole dish.
steps: Season chicken thighs with chili powder, cumin, and salt; pan-sear or grill 6-7 minutes per side until cooked through, then rest and slice.
Toss shredded cabbage with lime juice and a pinch of salt for a quick slaw.
Warm corn tortillas in a dry skillet, 20-30 seconds per side, until pliable.
Fill tortillas with sliced chicken and slaw.
Top with cotija, a dollop of sour cream, and chopped cilantro.

adaptations.instructions: Swap chicken thighs for grilled steak, shrimp, or seasoned black beans for a vegetarian version.
Do NOT use cotija cheese or sour cream — substitute a dairy-free crumbled cheese alternative and a dairy-free sour cream, or skip both and add extra lime and avocado for richness.

name: Gluten-Free Chicken Pot Pie with Xanthan-Gum Biscuit Topping
description: The dish that finally convinced me plain rice flour was never going to work here — the biscuit topping needs a proper 1:1 gluten-free flour blend with xanthan gum in it to hold a chewy, structural crust instead of crumbling off the filling.

ingredients.name: gluten-free 1:1 flour blend with xanthan gum

steps: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Sauté onion, carrots, and celery in 2 tbsp butter until softened, about 6 minutes; add chicken and cook until no longer pink.

Whisk cornstarch into a splash of cold broth to make a slurry, then stir the slurry and remaining broth into the pot; simmer until the filling thickens into a glossy (not cloudy) sauce, about 5 minutes.
Stir in peas, season with salt, and pour the filling into a baking dish.
For the biscuit topping, cut remaining 4 tbsp cold butter into the GF flour blend, baking powder, and salt until pea-sized crumbs form; stir in milk just until a soft dough comes together.
Drop spoonfuls of biscuit dough over the filling, brush with beaten egg, and bake 25-30 minutes until the topping is golden and cooked through and the filling bubbles at the edges.
Rest 5 minutes before serving.

adaptations.instructions: Swap diced chicken breast for diced turkey, or a mix of mushrooms and white beans for a vegetarian filling.
Do NOT use butter or whole milk — substitute a solid dairy-free butter (chilled, cubed the same way) and an unsweetened plant milk in equal amounts; the biscuit texture holds fine with either.
Do NOT use egg for the wash — substitute a brush of plant milk instead, which still gives a golden top without the egg.

name: Rice Pasta Salad with Tuna, White Beans, Olives, and Feta
description: A pasta salad that holds its shape in the fridge overnight — short rice pasta shapes like fusilli grip the dressing and beans the same way wheat fusilli would, so nothing here reads as a substitution.
steps: Cook rice fusilli in salted boiling water according to package directions until al dente; drain and rinse briefly under cool water.
Whisk olive oil, red wine vinegar, and oregano for the dressing.
In a large bowl, combine cooled pasta, tuna, cannellini beans, olives, red onion, and cherry tomatoes.
Pour dressing over and toss gently.
Top with crumbled feta and chill at least 20 minutes before serving.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use tuna — substitute a second can of cannellini beans or chickpeas plus a diced hard-boiled egg for protein, keeping the same dressing.
Do NOT use feta — substitute a dairy-free feta-style crumble or omit and add extra kalamata olives and a pinch of extra salt.

name: Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry
description: My go-to example of a parallel-track stir-fry: sear the beef and broccoli once, then branch the sauce so the whole pot becomes gluten-free with a single ingredient swap instead of two separate pans.
steps: Toss the sliced steak with 1 tbsp cornstarch; set aside.
Whisk soy sauce, brown sugar, remaining cornstarch, and 1/4 cup water into a sauce; set aside.
Heat vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat. Sear the beef in batches until browned, about 2 minutes per side; remove.
Add broccoli, garlic, and ginger to the same pan; stir-fry 3-4 minutes until crisp-tender.
Return the beef to the pan, pour in the sauce, and toss until it thickens and coats everything glossy, about 1 minute.
Drizzle with sesame oil off heat and serve over rice.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular soy sauce -- substitute certified gluten-free tamari 1:1. This is the exact branch point for the whole pot: sear the meat and broccoli as written, then split the sauce here so a gluten-free eater gets the identical dish instead of a separate stir-fry.
Do NOT use soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos 1:1, and use plain avocado oil in place of the vegetable oil if your brand is soy-based.
Do NOT use sesame oil -- substitute plain toasted avocado oil for the same rounded, nutty finish without the sesame allergen.
Swap the flank steak for pressed, cubed extra-firm tofu (tag: soy) or thinly sliced chicken thigh for a beef-free version -- sear it the same way before adding the sauce.
For a meat-free version, use pressed extra-firm tofu (tag: soy) or a mix of mushrooms and extra broccoli added straight to the hot pan in place of the steak.

name: Chicken Parmesan with Spaghetti
description: A three-part breading (flour, egg, crumb) makes this the textbook case for why a GF swap has to happen at every layer, not just the visible one -- and a tubular or flat pasta shape under the marinara matters as much as the crust does.
steps: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil for the pasta.
Set up a dredging line: flour, then beaten egg, then panko mixed with half the parmesan.
Season chicken, then dredge each piece through flour, egg, and crumb, pressing the crumb on firmly.
Pan-fry in olive oil over medium heat, 3-4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through.
Cook spaghetti to al dente; drain.
Top each cutlet with marinara and mozzarella, then broil 2-3 minutes until bubbly.
Serve the cutlets over the spaghetti with remaining marinara and parmesan.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use the all-purpose flour, panko breadcrumbs, or wheat spaghetti -- dredge in a 1:1 xanthan-gum gluten-free flour blend, coat with a certified gluten-free panko-style breadcrumb for the same shattering crust, and boil brown rice spaghetti instead of wheat pasta (a sturdier rice pasta shape holds the marinara's cling far better than thin gluten-free spaghetti strands, which tend to snap).
Do NOT use whole egg for the dredge -- substitute a slurry of 3 tbsp aquafaba (chickpea can liquid) whisked with 1 tsp water, which binds the breading just as well.

Do NOT use parmesan or mozzarella -- substitute a dairy-free parmesan-style shred in the crumb mix and a meltable dairy-free mozzarella alternative on top; brush lightly with olive oil before broiling so it browns instead of staying pale.
Substitute thick-cut breaded eggplant slices for the chicken breast for a meat-free chicken parm.

name: Chicken Teriyaki Rice Bowl
description: A rice bowl is the easiest parallel-track dinner there is: rice is naturally gluten-free, so the entire dish branches at one sauce swap.
steps: Whisk soy sauce, brown sugar, rice vinegar, garlic, and ginger in a bowl.
Sear chicken thighs in a hot skillet 5-6 minutes per side until cooked through; slice.
Pour the sauce into the same skillet and simmer 2 minutes.
Whisk cornstarch with 2 tbsp cold water and stir into the simmering sauce until glossy and thickened.
Return chicken to the pan and toss to coat.
Serve over rice with broccoli, sprinkled with sesame seeds.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular soy sauce in the teriyaki glaze -- substitute certified gluten-free tamari 1:1. The cornstarch thickener already used here is the correct clear, glossy choice for this sauce (not a flour-based roux), so no other change is needed once the tamari is in.
Do NOT use soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos 1:1, reducing the added brown sugar slightly since coconut aminos run sweeter.
Do NOT use sesame seeds as a garnish -- substitute crushed certified gluten-free crisp rice cereal or chopped scallion greens for the same finishing crunch.
Substitute pressed, pan-fried extra-firm tofu (tag: soy) for the chicken thighs for a meat-free bowl.

name: Baked Salmon with Panko Crust
description: The crumb topping is doing all the textural work here, so matching it -- a crisp, shattering GF panko, not a soft substitute -- is the whole game.
steps: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C) and line a baking sheet.
Mix panko, melted butter, garlic, and parsley in a bowl.
Pat salmon dry, place on the sheet, and brush the tops with dijon mustard.
Press the panko mixture onto each fillet.
Bake 12-15 minutes until the crumb is golden and the salmon flakes easily.
Serve with lemon wedges.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular panko -- substitute certified gluten-free panko-style breadcrumbs (or crushed certified gluten-free rice crackers) pressed on in the same layer for the same shattering crust.
Do NOT use butter to bind the crust -- substitute melted dairy-free butter or olive oil in the same amount.
Substitute a firm white fish like halibut, or a thick portobello mushroom cap, for a fish-free version, adjusting the bake time down for the mushroom.

name: Chicken Pot Pie
description: The filling is easy to branch, but a flaky pot-pie crust is structurally built around wheat's gluten network -- that's the one case where I write it as a full second recipe instead of a swap note.
steps: Make the pie dough with 1 cup flour, 3/4 cup of the butter, and ice water; chill.
Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Sauté onion and celery in remaining butter, then stir in 3 tbsp flour to make a roux.
Whisk in broth and milk; simmer until thickened.
Stir in chicken, peas, and carrots; season and pour into a pie dish.
Roll out the dough, cover the filling, crimp the edges, and cut vents.
Brush with egg wash and bake 35-40 minutes until deeply golden.

alternateRecipe.name: Gluten-Free Chicken Pot Pie with Xanthan-Gum Crust
alternateRecipe.description: The same chicken-and-vegetable filling, forked at the crust: a 1:1 xanthan-gum gluten-free flour blend gives the biscuit-like structure this dish needs -- plain rice flour alone crumbles apart.

ingredients.name: gluten-free 1:1 flour blend with xanthan gum (crust and roux)

steps: Make the pie dough with the GF flour blend, 3/4 cup of the butter, and ice water; chill (handle gently -- GF dough tears more easily than wheat dough).
Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Sauté onion and celery in remaining butter, then whisk in 3 tbsp of the GF flour blend to make a roux.
Whisk in broth and milk; simmer until thickened.
Stir in chicken, peas, and carrots; season and pour into a pie dish.
Roll the dough between two sheets of parchment, cover the filling, crimp the edges, and cut vents.
Brush with egg wash and bake 35-40 minutes until golden; tent with foil if it browns too fast.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use butter or milk in the filling and crust -- substitute dairy-free butter and unsweetened plain oat milk (certified gluten-free) in equal amounts; the roux ratio doesn't change, so the filling still thickens the same.
Do NOT use egg wash on the crust -- substitute a brush of dairy-free milk for a similar golden sheen.
Substitute sautéed mushrooms and cubed extra-firm tofu (tag: soy) for the chicken for a meat-free pot pie.

name: Pork Fried Rice
description: Day-old rice is already the exact dry, separate-grain texture fried rice needs, so once again the only real branch point is the sauce, not the starch itself.
steps: Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a wok; scramble the eggs and set aside.
Add remaining oil and sear the pork until cooked through; remove.
Stir-fry garlic and peas and carrots 2 minutes.
Add rice, breaking up clumps, and stir-fry until heated through.
Return pork and egg to the wok, add soy sauce, and toss to coat evenly.
Finish with sesame oil and green onion.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular soy sauce -- substitute certified gluten-free tamari 1:1; the rice and technique don't need to change at all, so the sauce is the entire branch point.
Do NOT use soy sauce -- substitute coconut aminos 1:1.
Do NOT use sesame oil -- substitute avocado oil for the finishing drizzle.
Do NOT use whole egg scrambled into the rice -- omit it or substitute a scrambled soft tofu crumble (tag: soy) for similar texture flecks.
Substitute diced chicken thigh or pressed extra-firm tofu (tag: soy) for the pork.
Substitute pressed extra-firm tofu (tag: soy) and extra vegetables for the pork for a meat-free fried rice.

name: Fettuccine Alfredo with Grilled Chicken
description: A cream sauce needs a wide, ribbon-shaped noodle underneath it to hold on -- this is a case where the pasta shape matters as much as picking a GF starch at all.
steps: Cook fettuccine to al dente; reserve 1/2 cup pasta water and drain.
Melt butter in a large skillet, add garlic, and cook 1 minute.
Pour in cream and simmer 3-4 minutes.
Whisk in parmesan until smooth, thinning with pasta water as needed.
Toss the pasta and sliced chicken through the sauce.
Finish with black pepper and parsley.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use wheat fettuccine -- substitute a corn-and-rice-blend fettuccine, which holds the cream sauce's cling far better than thin rice-spaghetti strands (those tend to snap and shed the sauce).
Do NOT use heavy cream, butter, or parmesan -- substitute full-fat canned coconut cream, dairy-free butter, and a dairy-free parmesan-style shred; whisk over low heat so it emulsifies the same way.
Substitute pan-seared king oyster mushroom slices for the grilled chicken for a meat-free alfredo.

name: Chicken and Dumplings
description: Dumplings live or die on structure -- they need to hold together while poaching in broth, which is exactly the job a xanthan-gum GF blend is built for and plain rice flour is not.
steps: Simmer chicken thighs in broth with onion, carrots, celery, and thyme until cooked through, about 20 minutes; shred the chicken and return to the pot.
Whisk 2 cups flour with baking powder and a pinch of salt; cut in butter, then stir in milk to form a soft dough.
Drop spoonfuls of dough onto the simmering broth.
Cover and simmer 15 minutes, without lifting the lid, until dumplings are puffed and cooked through.
Whisk remaining flour with a little cold broth and stir in to thicken the soup to a stew-like consistency.

alternateRecipe.name: Gluten-Free Chicken and Dumplings with Xanthan-Gum Drop Biscuits
alternateRecipe.description: Same simmered chicken-and-vegetable base, forked at the dumpling step -- a xanthan-gum-inclusive 1:1 GF flour blend is what actually holds a dumpling's chewy structure while it poaches; plain rice flour falls apart in the broth.

ingredients.name: gluten-free 1:1 flour blend with xanthan gum (dumplings and thickening)

steps: Simmer chicken thighs in broth with onion, carrots, celery, and thyme until cooked through, about 20 minutes; shred the chicken and return to the pot.
Whisk 2 cups of the GF flour blend with baking powder and a pinch of salt; cut in butter, then stir in milk to form a soft, slightly stickier-than-usual dough.
Drop spoonfuls of dough onto the simmering broth -- do not stir once dropped, or GF dumplings can break apart.
