Top standard chicken with mozzarella in its own baking dish; top the allergen-free chicken with dairy-free shreds in its own dish.
Bake both at 425F for 10-12 minutes until the cheese melts, on separate trays.
Ladle the shared marinara over each portion at serving, and serve over gluten-free pasta for the gluten-free diner instead of wheat spaghetti.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use wheat flour, regular breadcrumbs, or wheat spaghetti for a gluten allergy -- use the gluten-free breading station with its own plates and utensils, and serve over gluten-free pasta instead of wheat spaghetti. Note: this station also carries the flax-meal egg wash for the egg-free branch -- if a diner needs gluten-free only (not egg-free), confirm the flax wash isn't a problem for them, or bread that portion with gluten-free breadcrumbs and a plain egg wash in its own dedicated bowl instead. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Do NOT dip in whisked egg for an egg allergy -- use the flax-meal-and-water wash from the allergen-free breading station instead. Note: that station's breadcrumbs are also gluten-free -- if a diner needs egg-free only (not gluten-free), that's not a problem, but don't assume the reverse. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Do NOT use parmesan or mozzarella for a dairy allergy -- omit the cheese in the breading and topping, or use a dairy-free mozzarella-style shred in its own baking dish. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

For a vegetarian portion, bread and pan-fry thick slices of eggplant the same way instead of chicken. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

name: Potstickers, Split at the First Fold
description: One batch of cabbage-and-scallion filling splits before the pork, soy sauce, and sesame oil come in, so a fully vegetarian, soy-free, gluten-free branch exists in its own bowl from the very first fold.
steps: Make the shared aromatic base: finely chop cabbage, scallions, ginger, and garlic.

Split into two bowls before adding pork, soy sauce, or sesame oil -- this is the branch point: bowl one gets ground pork, soy sauce, and sesame oil; bowl two gets chopped mushrooms and a soy-free, sesame-free seasoning of rice vinegar, salt, and extra ginger.
Fold bowl two's filling into gluten-free rice wrappers first, using clean hands and a clean surface, before touching any wheat wrapper.
Fold bowl one's filling into wheat wrappers separately, on a different surface.
Pan-fry each batch in its own pan, gluten-free/vegetarian batch first, then the wheat/pork batch, using separate spatulas.
Make two dipping sauces: a standard soy-sesame sauce, and a soy-free, sesame-free version using coconut aminos and a drop of toasted pumpkin seed oil.

adaptations.instructions: Use bowl two's mushroom filling instead of pork for a pork-free portion; it's built in its own bowl from the first step. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Use bowl two's mushroom filling instead of pork for a vegetarian portion; it's built in its own bowl from the first step. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Do NOT use soy sauce in the filling or dipping sauce for a soy allergy -- use bowl two's soy-free seasoning and the coconut-aminos dipping sauce instead. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Do NOT use sesame oil in the filling or dipping sauce for a sesame allergy -- use bowl two's sesame-free seasoning and the pumpkin-seed-oil dipping sauce instead. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Do NOT use wheat dumpling wrappers for a gluten allergy -- use the gluten-free rice wrappers, folded on a clean surface before any wheat wrapper is touched. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

name: Shepherd's Pie, Split at the Mash
description: One pot of beef-and-vegetable filling gets topped with two separate bowls of mashed potatoes -- one finished with butter and milk, one finished with olive oil and oat milk -- baked side by side in the same dish. Note: this dish is NOT adaptable for a fish allergy -- worcestershire sauce (fish) is stirred into the single shared filling before the only branch point (the mash), so no fish-free portion exists; serve a different dish entirely for a fish-allergic diner rather than attempting to omit it from part of the pot.
steps: Boil potatoes until fork-tender; drain.

Brown beef with onion, carrot, celery, and garlic; stir in tomato paste, broth, worcestershire, thyme, and peas; simmer until thickened. Spread evenly across the baking dish -- this is the fully shared base, and it is NOT fish-free (worcestershire sauce contains fish) -- do not serve this filling to a fish-allergic diner.
Split the mashed potatoes at the very last step: mash two-thirds with butter and milk for the standard topping.
Mash the remaining third separately, in a clean bowl with a clean masher, using olive oil and oat milk for the dairy-free branch.
Spoon the dairy-free mash over one clearly marked section of the filling; spoon the standard mash over the rest.
Bake at 400F for 20-25 minutes until the tops are golden. Mark the dairy-free section with a small flag or foil marker before serving.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use butter or whole milk on the dairy-allergic diner's portion -- mash their potatoes separately with olive oil and unsweetened oat milk, using a clean bowl and clean masher with no butter contact, and mark that section of the dish clearly.
For a vegetarian portion, replace the ground beef with a lentil-and-mushroom filling cooked in the same aromatics, kept in its own separate pot from the start (not split off from the beef filling).
Replace the ground beef with a lentil-and-mushroom filling cooked in the same aromatics, kept in its own separate pot from the start (not split off from the beef filling).

name: Coconut Curry, Ladled Off Before the Shrimp
description: A shared coconut curry base simmers with onion, garlic, ginger, and spices, then splits before the shellfish and fish sauce go in -- a full pot of chickpea curry is ladled off first so nothing shellfish or fish ever touches it.
steps: Build the shared curry base: sauté onion, garlic, and ginger, then add curry powder, turmeric, tomato paste, and coconut milk; simmer 10 minutes.
Ladle roughly half the base into a separate pot for the shellfish- and fish-free branch before adding shrimp or fish sauce to the original pot -- this is the branch point.
In the reserved pot, add chickpeas and simmer until warmed through, using its own dedicated spoon throughout.
In the original pot, stir in fish sauce and shrimp; simmer just until the shrimp are pink and cooked through, about 5 minutes.
Cook the rice in one shared pot, then serve both curries over it with cilantro and lime on the side for both.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT serve the shrimp pot to a shellfish allergy -- use the reserved chickpea branch, ladled into a separate pot before shrimp was ever added, with its own dedicated serving spoon.

Do NOT use fish sauce in the branch for a fish allergy -- season the reserved chickpea pot with coconut aminos and extra lime/salt instead, kept in its own separate pot from before fish sauce ever touches the original pot. Use coconut aminos as the default substitute here, not soy sauce: soy sauce would trade a fish allergen for a soy allergen (and usually a gluten one too, since most soy sauce is wheat-brewed), so it should not be used in this branch even for a diner with no known soy/gluten restriction.

name: Sheet-Pan Loaded Nachos with Parallel Toppings
description: One sheet pan of chips, beans, and roasted tomatoes does the heavy lifting -- I split the tray in two right before the seasoned beef and cheese go on, so the dairy-free eater and the beef-avoider both get a tray that was never near the ingredient they're avoiding.
steps: Preheat oven to 400F. Brown ground beef in a skillet with taco seasoning, about 6-8 minutes; drain fat.
Spread chips across a parchment-lined sheet pan and scatter black beans and diced tomatoes over the whole tray -- this is the shared base everyone eats.

THIS IS THE BRANCH POINT: before adding beef or cheese, pull off a portion of the chip/bean/tomato tray onto a separate section of the pan or a second sheet for anyone avoiding beef or dairy, and label it clearly.
On the shared portion, scatter the seasoned beef, then top both portions with cheddar cheese -- swap in a dairy-free shredded cheese on the labeled dairy-free section instead.
Bake 8-10 minutes, until cheese is melted and chips are warmed through.
Top with jalapenos, scallions, and a dollop of sour cream on the standard tray; use a dairy-free sour cream or skip it on the dairy-free section.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use the shared cheddar cheese or sour cream on the dairy-free portion -- substitute a dairy-free shredded cheese and dairy-free sour cream (or cashew crema), added to that section only after the tray has been split. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Swap the seasoned ground beef for an extra can of black beans or seasoned crumbled tempeh on the beef-free portion, added at the same branch point before cheese goes on. Note: tempeh is soy-based -- if that portion also needs to be soy-free, use the extra black beans instead.

name: Peanut-Sesame Noodle Snack Cups
description: Little cups of chilled noodles tossed in a glossy peanut-sesame sauce -- great for grazing, but this one carries three Big-9 allergens in a single sauce, so I build the noodle-and-veggie base first and split it into separate bowls before any peanut, sesame, or soy touches it.

ingredients.name: wheat noodles (spaghetti or lo mein style)

steps: Cook noodles according to package directions; drain and rinse under cold water. This is the shared base.
Toss the cold noodles with shredded carrots, cabbage, and scallions in a large bowl -- still shared, nothing allergen-bearing yet.
THIS IS THE BRANCH POINT: divide the noodle-veggie mix into separate bowls now, before mixing any sauce, so each portion gets its own allergen-safe sauce made in a clean bowl with clean utensils.
For the standard portion, whisk peanut butter, soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, honey, and garlic until smooth; toss with that portion's noodles and spoon into snack cups.
For each allergy-branch portion, make a separate sauce per the swap instructions in a bowl and with a whisk that never touched the standard sauce, and toss into that portion's cups only.
Top with a pinch of sesame seeds on the standard portion only; leave allergy-branch portions unseeded.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use the wheat noodles or regular soy sauce for the gluten-free portion -- substitute rice noodles and a certified gluten-free tamari, cooked and mixed with separate pots and utensils from the wheat noodles. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Do NOT use soy sauce for the soy-free portion -- substitute coconut aminos, mixed in a clean bowl that never touched the soy sauce or the standard sauce. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Do NOT use sesame oil or sesame seeds for the sesame-free portion -- substitute a neutral oil (such as avocado oil) for the sesame oil and omit the seeds entirely, using a clean pan and utensils that never touched sesame oil or seeds. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Peanut butter is structural to this dish's sauce, so this is a full alternate recipe rather than a same-bowl swap -- confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on cross-contact wording (separate bowl/whisk from the start) before this branch goes live.

alternateRecipe.name: Sunflower Seed Butter Noodle Snack Cups
alternateRecipe.description: Same glossy sauce-and-noodle idea, built entirely nut-free with sunflower seed butter standing in for peanut butter -- made in its own bowl, on its own utensils, from the start.

ingredients.name: wheat noodles (spaghetti or lo mein style)

steps: Cook noodles according to package directions; drain and rinse under cold water.
Toss noodles with shredded carrots, cabbage, and scallions.
In a separate, nut-free bowl with clean utensils, whisk sunflower seed butter, soy sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar, honey, and garlic until smooth.
Toss the sauce with the noodle mixture and portion into snack cups.
Chill at least 20 minutes before serving for the best texture.

name: No-Bake Peanut Butter Energy Bites
description: No stove, no oven -- just a bowl and a fridge. I keep the peanut butter and oats as the only two allergen-relevant ingredients so the nut-free branch is a clean split, not a full rebuild.
steps: Stir peanut butter and honey together in a bowl until smooth -- this is the shared base for both branches.
THIS IS THE BRANCH POINT: split the peanut butter/honey base into two bowls now, before the oats go in, so the nut-free branch never touches the peanut butter bowl or its utensils.
Into each bowl, stir in oats, flaxseed, chocolate chips, and vanilla until a sticky dough forms.
Roll each portion into 1-inch balls (about 12 per batch), keeping the two branches on separate plates.
Chill at least 30 minutes so the bites firm up.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular rolled oats for the gluten-free portion -- substitute oats labeled certified gluten-free, scooped with a clean measuring cup that never touched the regular oats. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Do NOT use standard mini chocolate chips (they typically contain milk solids) for the dairy-free portion -- substitute certified dairy-free mini chocolate chips, scooped from a separate bag with a clean spoon. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Peanut butter is the structural binder holding this dough together, so this is a full alternate recipe rather than a same-bowl swap -- confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on cross-contact wording (separate bowl/spoon from the start) before this branch goes live.

alternateRecipe.name: Sunflower Seed Butter Energy Bites
alternateRecipe.description: The same no-bake bites without any nuts anywhere in the process -- sunflower seed butter brings the same sticky base peanut butter would, made in its own bowl from the start.
steps: Stir sunflower seed butter and honey together in a bowl until smooth.
Stir in oats, flaxseed, chocolate chips, and vanilla until a sticky dough forms.
Roll into 1-inch balls (about 12 total).
Chill at least 30 minutes so the bites firm up.

name: Roasted Garlic Hummus & Veggie Platter
description: Roasting a whole head of garlic is the only real cooking here -- the hummus comes together in a blender in five minutes, and the only allergen on the whole platter is the tahini, so this is the simplest branch I make: one swap, one clean blender jar.
steps: Roast the whole garlic head at 400F for about 25 minutes until soft and caramelized (or use pre-roasted garlic to save time); let cool, then squeeze the cloves out.
In a blender, combine chickpeas, roasted garlic, lemon juice, olive oil, and cumin -- this is the shared base before tahini goes in.
THIS IS THE BRANCH POINT: pull off a portion of the blended base now, before adding tahini, for the sesame-free branch.
Blend tahini into the remaining base until smooth and creamy; for the sesame-free portion, blend in an extra tablespoon of olive oil and a splash of water instead, in a clean blender jar.
Arrange both hummus portions in separate bowls on the platter, clearly labeled, with carrot sticks, cucumber, bell pepper strips, and pita chips.
For the gluten-free portion, swap the pita chips for gluten-free crackers or extra veggie sticks.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use tahini for the sesame-free portion -- substitute an extra tablespoon of olive oil plus a splash of water, blended in a clean blender jar that never held tahini. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Do NOT use the pita chips for the gluten-free portion -- substitute certified gluten-free crackers or extra raw veggie sticks, served on a separate part of the platter. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

name: Shrimp & Veggie Spring Roll Snack Platter
description: Rice paper rolls are naturally gluten-free, but this platter carries both shellfish and peanuts -- I cook the shrimp in its own pan, keep a shrimp-free tofu filling going the whole time, and make the peanut dip in a separate bowl so nothing has to be picked out after the fact.
steps: Cook rice vermicelli per package directions, drain, and cool. This noodle-and-veggie prep (carrots, cucumber, mint, cilantro) is the shared base for every roll.

In a small pan, sear the tofu strips until golden on both sides, about 4 minutes; set aside. In a separate small pan with separate tongs, warm the cooked shrimp just until heated through, about 2 minutes.

THIS IS THE BRANCH POINT: lay out the noodles and vegetables, then build shrimp rolls and tofu rolls at separate stations with separate cutting boards, so the shellfish never touches the shellfish-free rolls.

Dip a rice paper wrapper in warm water for a few seconds, lay flat, and fill with noodles, vegetables, herbs, and either shrimp or tofu strips depending on the station. Roll tightly and set seam-side down. Label each side of the platter clearly (shrimp vs. tofu).
Whisk peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, and water into a smooth dipping sauce for the standard platter.
Serve rolls with dipping sauce on the side, keeping shrimp rolls and tofu rolls on visibly separate plates.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use the tofu or soy sauce for the soy-free portion -- substitute sliced grilled chicken for the tofu strips, prepared at its own station with its own cutting board and tongs (do NOT substitute extra shrimp for the tofu -- that would reintroduce shellfish for any diner who also needs to avoid it), and use coconut aminos in place of soy sauce for the dipping sauce, mixed in a separate bowl.

Do NOT use regular soy sauce in the dipping sauce for the gluten-free portion -- substitute a certified gluten-free tamari, mixed in a clean bowl. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Do NOT use peanut butter in the dipping sauce for the nut-free portion -- substitute sunflower seed butter, whisked in a separate bowl with clean utensils. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Shrimp is one of two proteins built in parallel from the very first pan, so this is a full alternate recipe rather than a same-bowl swap -- confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on cross-contact wording (separate station/board/utensils from the start) before this branch goes live.

alternateRecipe.name: All-Tofu Veggie Spring Roll Platter
alternateRecipe.description: The same fresh roll platter built shellfish-free from the very first pan -- extra-firm tofu is the only protein, seared once, on one station.
steps: Cook rice vermicelli per package directions, drain, and cool.
Sear tofu strips in a pan until golden on both sides, about 4-5 minutes.
Dip rice paper wrappers in warm water, fill with noodles, vegetables, herbs, and tofu, and roll tightly.
Whisk peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, and water into a dipping sauce.
Serve rolls with the dipping sauce on the side.

name: Cheesy Chicken Quesadilla Wedges
description: One skillet of shredded chicken and peppers does double duty -- I split it onto separate tortillas before the cheese melts in, so the dairy-free eater gets a wedge that was never touched by shredded cheddar.
steps: Heat olive oil in a skillet and saute peppers and onion until soft, about 4 minutes. Add shredded chicken and cumin and warm through -- this is the shared filling.
THIS IS THE BRANCH POINT: divide the chicken-pepper filling in half before assembling any tortillas, so each branch's tortilla and cheese decision happens separately from here.

Lay a flour tortilla flat, scatter filling and cheddar cheese over one half, fold over, and cook in a dry skillet 2-3 minutes per side until golden and cheese is melted. Repeat for the standard portion.
For the dairy-free branch, use the same folding method but swap in dairy-free shredded cheese, cooked in a clean pan.
For the gluten-free branch, swap the flour tortilla for a corn tortilla, cooked in a clean pan.
Slice each quesadilla into wedges, keeping branches on separate plates, and serve with salsa.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use the flour tortilla for the gluten-free portion -- substitute a corn tortilla, cooked in a clean pan that hasn't touched flour tortillas. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Do NOT use the shared cheddar cheese for the dairy-free portion -- substitute a dairy-free shredded cheese, melted in a separate pan. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.
Swap the shredded chicken for sauteed black beans or extra peppers on the vegetarian portion, split off before cheese goes on.

name: One-Pan Apple Crumble, Split Topping
description: One bowl of spiced apples goes into two dishes, and I only split the topping at the very last step -- regular crumble on one side, gluten-free oat crumble on the other -- so nobody's eating a separate dessert.

ingredients.name: Dairy-free margarine or cold coconut oil

steps: Preheat oven to 375F. Toss apple slices with granulated sugar, cinnamon, and lemon juice in a large bowl.
Divide the apple mixture among three baking dishes (or three sections of one large dish) -- this is your shared base, done splitting.
In a separate bowl, rub together flour, oats, cold butter, brown sugar, and salt until it forms a coarse, clumpy crumble. Sprinkle it over the first dish -- this is the 'everyone' portion.

For the gluten-free branch, make a second small batch of crumble using a gluten-free flour blend and certified gluten-free oats in place of the wheat flour and oats, mixed in a bowl that hasn't touched the wheat batch, and sprinkle it over the second dish.

For the dairy-free branch, make a third small batch of crumble using the same wheat flour and oats as the 'everyone' portion but substituting dairy-free margarine or cold coconut oil for the butter, mixed in its own clean bowl, and sprinkle it over the third dish.
Bake all three dishes 30-35 minutes, until bubbling and golden. Label each dish clearly before serving -- painter's tape works fine.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular flour or rolled oats for the gluten-free portion's topping -- substitute a 1:1 gluten-free flour blend and certified gluten-free oats, mixed in a bowl that hasn't touched the wheat batch. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Do NOT use dairy butter for the dairy-free portion's topping -- the recipe's third topping batch (step 5) substitutes dairy-free margarine or cold coconut oil in the same amount as the butter, mixed in its own clean bowl that hasn't touched the other two batches, and is sprinkled over the third dish. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

name: Brownie Sundae Bar, Split at the Scoop
description: One pan of brownies feeds the whole table -- the branching happens after they're cut, at the ice cream scoop and the topping bowl, so the kitchen only runs one oven, not four dessert stations.
steps: Preheat oven to 350F and grease an 8x8 pan. Also line a small separate pan (a 5x5 pan or 2-3 muffin cups) for anyone who needs the gluten-free or egg-free branch.
Whisk melted butter, sugar, eggs, and vanilla together. Fold in flour, cocoa, and salt until just combined. This is the shared base -- everyone eats the same brownie.

For anyone who needs the gluten-free or egg-free branch, mix a small separate batch in its own bowl before the shared batter goes in the oven: whisk 3 tbsp melted butter, 1/4 cup sugar, and a splash of vanilla with 1 tbsp ground flaxseed mixed into 3 tbsp water (let gel 5 minutes) in place of egg, then fold in the 1:1 gluten-free flour blend, 2 tbsp cocoa, and a pinch of salt. Pour into the separate small pan using its own bowl and spatula -- this batter is both gluten-free and egg-free, so it safely covers either restriction on its own.
Spread the shared batter in the 8x8 pan. Bake both pans 18-22 minutes, checking the smaller pan a few minutes early, until set.
Let cool slightly, then cut the 8x8 pan into bite-size squares and portion into sundae bowls, keeping the separate small pan's squares set aside for whoever needs the gluten-free or egg-free branch.
Branch at the topping: scoop regular vanilla ice cream over most bowls; for the dairy-free branch, scoop a coconut-milk-based frozen dessert instead.
Branch again for nuts: sprinkle chopped walnuts over most bowls; for the nut-free branch, sprinkle toasted pepitas instead, using a topping spoon that hasn't touched the walnuts.
Drizzle hot fudge sauce over the dairy bowls; for anyone dairy-free, use a dairy-free chocolate sauce instead. Label every bowl before it leaves the kitchen.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular flour for the gluten-free portion's brownie base -- the recipe's separate small-pan batch (step 3) substitutes a 1:1 gluten-free flour blend and is baked in its own pan (step 4), not mixed into the shared 8x8 batter. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Do NOT use dairy butter, ice cream, or hot fudge sauce for the dairy-free portion -- substitute dairy-free margarine in the batter, a coconut-milk frozen dessert, and a dairy-free chocolate sauce. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Do NOT use eggs for the egg-free portion's brownie batter -- the recipe's separate small-pan batch (step 3) substitutes 1 tbsp ground flaxseed mixed with 3 tbsp water (gelled 5 minutes) in place of egg, and is baked in its own pan (step 4), not mixed into the shared 8x8 batter. This same separate batch is also gluten-free, so it safely covers a diner who needs only the egg-free branch. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Do NOT scatter walnuts on the nut-free bowls -- substitute toasted pepitas or sunflower seeds, scooped with a spoon that has not touched the walnuts, on a clean plate. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

name: Peanut Butter Blondie Bars, Split at the Swirl
description: One bowl of blondie batter goes into one pan -- I score a line down the middle and swirl peanut butter into one half, sunflower seed butter into the other, so it's one bake, one pan, one cooling rack.
steps: Preheat oven to 350F and line a 9x9 pan. Also line a small separate pan (a 5x5 pan or 2-3 muffin cups) for anyone who needs the dairy-free, egg-free, or gluten-free branch.
Whisk melted butter and brown sugar, then whisk in egg and vanilla.
Fold in flour, baking powder, and salt until just combined. Spread the batter in the 9x9 pan -- this is the shared base, identical for everyone else.

For anyone who needs the dairy-free, egg-free, or gluten-free branch, mix a small separate batch in its own bowl before any peanut butter goes in: whisk 2 tbsp melted dairy-free margarine and 3 tbsp brown sugar, then whisk in 1 tbsp ground flaxseed mixed with 3 tbsp water (gelled 5 minutes) in place of the egg and a splash of vanilla. Fold in 1/3 cup of the 1:1 gluten-free flour blend, a pinch of baking powder, and a pinch of salt. Pour into the separate small pan using its own bowl and spatula -- this batter is dairy-, egg-, and gluten-free, so it safely covers any one of those restrictions on its own.
Score a line down the middle of the 9x9 pan's batter with a knife so you know exactly where the nut split is.
Dollop peanut butter over one side of the 9x9 pan in spoonfuls and swirl gently with a knife, staying on that side of the score line.

For the nut-free branch, dollop sunflower seed butter over the other side of the 9x9 pan instead (or over the separate small pan too, if that diner also needs the dairy/egg/gluten-free batter), swirling with a separate, clean knife.

Bake the 9x9 pan 22-25 minutes and the separate small pan about 16-20 minutes (check it early), until edges pull from the pan(s) and the centers are just set. Let cool, then cut the 9x9 pan along your scored line and label every piece before serving.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy butter in the batter for the dairy-free portion -- the recipe's separate small-pan batch (step 4) substitutes dairy-free margarine in the same ratio and is baked in its own pan (step 8), not mixed into the shared 9x9 batter. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Do NOT use egg in the batter for the egg-free portion -- the recipe's separate small-pan batch (step 4) substitutes 1 tbsp ground flaxseed mixed with 3 tbsp water (gelled 5 minutes) in place of the egg and is baked in its own pan (step 8), not mixed into the shared 9x9 batter. This same separate batch is also dairy-free and gluten-free, so it safely covers a diner who needs only the egg-free branch. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Do NOT use regular flour for the gluten-free portion -- the recipe's separate small-pan batch (step 4) substitutes a 1:1 gluten-free flour blend in the same ratio and is baked in its own pan (step 8), not mixed into the shared 9x9 batter. This same separate batch is also dairy-free and egg-free, so it safely covers a diner who needs only the gluten-free branch. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Do NOT swirl peanut butter into the nut-free half of the pan -- substitute sunflower seed butter, swirled in with its own clean knife, on the side of the score line reserved for the nut-free eater. This branch is genuinely pre-bake segregated via the score-line swirl. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

name: Coffee-Soaked Tiramisu Trifle, Split at the Custard
description: Everybody gets the same coffee-dipped layers -- the branch only happens at the mascarpone custard, where I hold back a cooked-egg-yolk zabaglione for one set of glasses and build an egg-free whipped cream version for the other.
steps: Brew coffee, cool completely, and stir in liqueur if using. This is the shared soak.

Whisk egg yolks and sugar in a heatproof bowl set over simmering water until pale, thick, and doubled in volume, about 5 minutes -- this cooks the yolks to a safe temperature. Remove from heat and whisk in mascarpone until smooth.
Whip heavy cream to soft peaks and fold into the mascarpone mixture.

Dip ladyfingers briefly in the coffee -- don't soak them soggy -- and layer them in a trifle dish or individual glasses. Spoon mascarpone custard over the top, alternating layers, ending with custard.

This is the latest shared point. For the egg-free branch, stop here and use the egg-free mascarpone cream (see alternate recipe) instead of the cooked-yolk custard, layered over its own set of coffee-dipped ladyfingers. For the dairy-free branch, use the dairy-free custard (see alternate recipe) instead, layered over its own set of coffee-dipped ladyfingers.
Dust with cocoa powder and chill at least 4 hours, ideally overnight. Label egg, egg-free, and dairy-free trifles clearly before refrigerating.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use regular ladyfingers -- substitute gluten-free ladyfingers or a gluten-free sponge cake cut into strips. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.
Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

alternateRecipe.name: Dairy-Free Tiramisu Trifle
alternateRecipe.description: The same cooked egg-yolk zabaglione technique, built with a dairy-free cream cheese alternative and whipped coconut cream instead of mascarpone and heavy cream, so the custard is genuinely dairy-free rather than just substituted at the finish.
steps: Brew coffee, cool completely, and stir in liqueur if using. This is the shared soak.

Whisk egg yolks and sugar in a heatproof bowl set over simmering water until pale, thick, and doubled in volume, about 5 minutes. Remove from heat and whisk in the dairy-free cream cheese alternative until smooth.
Whip the chilled coconut cream to soft peaks and fold into the dairy-free cream cheese mixture.
Dip ladyfingers briefly in the coffee and layer in a trifle dish or individual glasses, alternating with the dairy-free custard, ending with custard.
Dust with cocoa powder and chill at least 4 hours, ideally overnight, before serving.

adaptations.instructions: Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

alternateRecipe.name: Egg-Free Mascarpone Cream Trifle
alternateRecipe.description: Skips the cooked egg-yolk zabaglione entirely -- whipped mascarpone and cream sweetened with powdered sugar builds the same silky layer with no egg at all.

ingredients.name: Egg-free ladyfingers or sponge cake strips

steps: Brew coffee and let cool completely.
Whip mascarpone, powdered sugar, and vanilla together until smooth.
In a separate bowl, whip heavy cream to soft peaks, then fold into the mascarpone mixture until light and airy.
Dip egg-free ladyfingers briefly in the coffee and layer in a trifle dish, alternating with the mascarpone cream, ending with cream.
Dust with cocoa powder and chill at least 4 hours before serving.

name: Shared-Ganache Chocolate Mousse Cups
description: Everyone's mousse starts as the exact same melted-chocolate-and-cream base, divided into cups before the whip technique -- and the allergen -- ever gets folded in.
steps: Melt chocolate in a heatproof bowl over simmering water, or in 20-second microwave bursts, stirring until smooth. Let cool slightly. This is the shared base every cup starts with.

Whip 1 cup of the heavy cream to soft peaks; fold half into the cooled melted chocolate to lighten it, then fold in the rest until smooth. Divide this base evenly among serving cups -- this is the latest point where everyone's mousse is still identical.

In a clean, dry bowl, whip the pasteurized egg whites with sugar and salt to stiff, glossy peaks. Pasteurized egg whites are required, not optional -- these whites go into the dessert raw and receive no further cooking, so regular (unpasteurized) egg whites are not a safe substitute here.
Fold the whipped pasteurized egg whites into the cups meant for egg-eaters to create the light, classic mousse texture.
For anyone with an egg allergy, skip the egg whites for their reserved cups and instead fold in whipped aquafaba (see alternate recipe) to get the same airy lift.
Chill all cups at least 2 hours before serving. Label egg vs. egg-free cups clearly -- they look identical once set.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy heavy cream for the dairy-free portion's base -- substitute well-chilled full-fat coconut cream, whipped the same way. Also use certified dairy-free dark chocolate for the chocolate melted in step 1 -- many dark chocolate products contain milk solids even though they aren't labeled 'milk chocolate,' and 'Dark chocolate, chopped' is deliberately left untagged here since certified dairy-free versions exist. Since the melted chocolate is part of the shared base before it's divided into cups, using certified dairy-free chocolate for the whole batch is the safest path whenever a dairy-strict diner is in the mix -- it's safe for everyone else too.

Approved: this branch uses a fully separate whip station (its own clean, dry bowl) and swaps egg whites for chickpea aquafaba, introducing no dairy or other Big-9 allergen in the process -- coconut cream (already used for the dairy-free branch elsewhere in this recipe) and aquafaba are both safe substitutes here.

alternateRecipe.name: Aquafaba Chocolate Mousse Cups
alternateRecipe.description: The same melted-chocolate base, but the whip comes from chickpea brine instead of egg whites -- it sets up just as light, with zero egg.

ingredients.name: Aquafaba (liquid from a can of chickpeas)

steps: Melt chocolate as in the base recipe; let cool slightly.
Whip chilled coconut cream to soft peaks; fold into the melted chocolate until smooth.
In a very clean, dry bowl, whip aquafaba with cream of tartar on high speed until stiff peaks form -- this takes longer than egg whites, about 5-8 minutes -- then whip in the sugar and vanilla.
Fold the whipped aquafaba into the chocolate-coconut base in two additions, keeping as much air as possible.
Spoon into cups and chill at least 2 hours before serving.

name: Sesame-Honey Brittle Bark, Split Before the Topping
description: Hot sugar work doesn't leave room for improvising mid-pour, so I split the caramel onto three separate trays with three separate sets of utensils before a single sesame seed, almond, pepita, or sunflower seed ever comes near any of them.
steps: Line three baking sheets and set them at separate ends of the counter -- this batch is built to split three ways, so keep the surfaces separate from the start.
In a heavy saucepan, cook sugar, honey, and butter over medium heat, stirring constantly, until it reaches a deep amber color, about 8-10 minutes. This is the shared caramel base.
Remove from heat and whisk in baking soda -- it will foam up. Working quickly, pour about a third of the caramel onto each of the three lined sheets.
Immediately scatter sesame seeds and almonds over the first sheet (the 'everyone' tray), pressing gently with a clean spatula reserved only for that sheet.

Scatter toasted pepitas over the second sheet for the sesame-free branch -- this tray gets pepitas only (no sesame seeds and no almonds are ever added to it), so it is safe for both sesame and tree-nut allergies. Use its own utensils and work surface, dedicated to this tray, to avoid cross-contact with sesame.

Scatter toasted sunflower seeds over the third sheet for the nut-free branch -- this tray gets sunflower seeds only (no almonds and no sesame seeds are ever added to it), so it is safe for both tree-nut and sesame allergies. Use its own utensils and work surface, dedicated to this tray, to avoid cross-contact with nuts.

Let all three trays cool completely and harden, about 30 minutes, then break into shards. Finish each with a pinch of sea salt. Bag and label each batch clearly -- brittle looks identical once broken up.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy butter in the caramel -- the caramel (step 2) is a single shared base that gets divided onto all three trays before any topping is added, so a separate 'dairy-free portion' of it can't be made without cooking an entirely separate batch that these steps don't describe. Instead, substitute a dairy-free margarine or coconut oil, in the same amount, for the butter in the one shared caramel batch. This makes the whole batch dairy-free and is safe for everyone, including diners without a dairy restriction.

Do NOT scatter sesame seeds on the sesame-free tray (the second tray) -- substitute an equal amount of toasted pepitas, using a spatula, cooling rack, and storage bag that have never touched sesame. As built, this tray receives only pepitas -- no almonds are ever scattered on it -- so it is safe for both a sesame allergy and a tree-nut allergy. No fourth tray is needed for a diner who needs both restrictions; the second tray already covers them.

Do NOT scatter almonds on the nut-free tray (the third tray) -- substitute toasted sunflower seeds, prepared on a separate work surface with separate utensils to avoid cross-contact. As built, this tray receives only sunflower seeds -- no sesame seeds are ever scattered on it -- so it is safe for both a tree-nut allergy and a sesame allergy. No fourth tray is needed for a diner who needs both restrictions; the third tray already covers them.

name: One-Tray Fudge Brownie Bar
description: One shared pan of glossy fudge batter for the family, with a fully separate pan, bowl, and bake for anyone who needs a dairy-free, egg-free, nut-free, or gluten-free version -- the branch happens before the batter ever touches heat, not by splitting a single pan afterward.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and line a 9x13 pan with parchment, leaving overhang on two sides.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over low heat, then whisk in the sugar until glossy.
Off heat, whisk in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Fold in the cocoa powder, flour, and salt just until no dry streaks remain -- don't overmix.
Fold in the chocolate chips and walnuts.
Pour into the pan, spread level, and bake 26-30 minutes until a toothpick has a few moist crumbs.

Cool completely before lifting out and cutting. This is the shared bake for the base recipe -- diners who need a dairy-free, egg-free, nut-free, or gluten-free version get their own fully separate pan, bowl, and bake from the mixing step onward (see adaptations), not a split of this pan.

adaptations.instructions: Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

alternateRecipe.name: Dairy-Free Fudge Brownie Bar
alternateRecipe.description: Same glossy fudge method, a plant-based butter stick and dairy-free chocolate standing in for the dairy -- mixed and baked in its own pan so it never shares a tray, bowl, or spoon with the dairy batter.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and line its own 9x13 pan with parchment -- keep this pan and any bowl/spoon that touches it away from dairy butter and chocolate.
Melt the plant-based butter in a saucepan over low heat, then whisk in the sugar until glossy.
Off heat, whisk in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Fold in the cocoa powder, flour, and salt just until no dry streaks remain -- don't overmix.
Fold in the dairy-free chocolate chips and walnuts.
Pour into the pan, spread level, and bake 26-30 minutes until a toothpick has a few moist crumbs.
Cool completely before lifting out and cutting.

adaptations.instructions: Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

alternateRecipe.name: Egg-Free Fudge Brownie Bar
alternateRecipe.description: Same glossy fudge method, flax eggs standing in for whole eggs -- mixed and baked in its own pan so it never shares a bowl or spoon with the egg batter.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and line its own 9x13 pan with parchment -- keep this pan and any bowl/spoon that touches it away from whole eggs.
Whisk the ground flaxseed with the water in a small bowl and let rest 5 minutes until gel-like -- this is the flax egg.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over low heat, then whisk in the sugar until glossy.
Off heat, whisk in the flax egg gel, then the vanilla.
Fold in the cocoa powder, flour, and salt just until no dry streaks remain -- don't overmix.
Fold in the chocolate chips and walnuts.
Pour into the pan, spread level, and bake 28-32 minutes until a toothpick has a few moist crumbs.
Cool completely before lifting out and cutting.

adaptations.instructions: Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

alternateRecipe.name: Nut-Free Fudge Brownie Bar
alternateRecipe.description: Same glossy fudge method, toasted sunflower seeds (or no crunch at all) standing in for walnuts -- mixed and baked in its own pan, with its own bowl and spoon, so a stray walnut never reaches it.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and line its own 9x13 pan with parchment -- keep this pan and any bowl/spoon that touches it away from walnuts.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over low heat, then whisk in the sugar until glossy.
Off heat, whisk in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Fold in the cocoa powder, flour, and salt just until no dry streaks remain -- don't overmix.
Fold in the chocolate chips and toasted sunflower seeds (or omit the crunch entirely).
Pour into the pan, spread level, and bake 26-30 minutes until a toothpick has a few moist crumbs.
Cool completely before lifting out and cutting.

adaptations.instructions: Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

alternateRecipe.name: Gluten-Free Fudge Brownie Bar
alternateRecipe.description: Same glossy fudge method, a 1:1 gluten-free flour blend standing in for wheat -- mixed and baked in its own pan so it never shares a tray with the wheat batter.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and line its own 8x8 pan with parchment -- keep this pan and any bowl/spoon that touches it away from wheat flour.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over low heat, then whisk in the sugar until glossy.
Off heat, whisk in the eggs one at a time, then the vanilla.
Fold in the cocoa powder, gluten-free flour blend, and salt just until no dry streaks remain.
Fold in the chocolate chips and walnuts.
Pour into the pan, spread level, and bake 28-32 minutes until a toothpick has a few moist crumbs.
Cool completely before cutting.

name: Backyard Sundae Bar
description: The whole family builds sundaes off the same topping line for dairy swaps -- but for a nut allergy, that bowl gets built in the kitchen ahead of time, so peanuts never make it anywhere near their plate.
steps: Warm the hot fudge sauce gently in a saucepan or microwave until pourable.

If anyone at the table has a nut allergy, build their sundae bowl now, in the kitchen: ice cream, fudge, whipped cream, marshmallows, sprinkles, and a cherry -- no peanuts -- using a scoop and spoons that have not touched the peanut bowl, and set it aside on its own plate before the buffet line opens (see adaptations).
Set out the ice cream, fudge, whipped cream, and all toppings buffet-style down the counter for everyone else.
Scoop 1-2 scoops of ice cream per bowl.
Ladle warm fudge sauce over the top.
Top with whipped cream, a spoonful of peanuts, marshmallows, sprinkles, and a cherry.

This topping line is the branch point for dairy -- swap the ice cream tub, fudge jar, and whipped topping can for dairy-free versions at one end of the counter (see adaptations). Serve the nut-allergic diner's pre-built bowl directly rather than having them queue at the shared line.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy ice cream, fudge sauce, or whipped cream -- substitute a coconut-milk or oat-milk ice cream, a dairy-free fudge sauce, and coconut whipped topping, scooped from their own containers at a separate station. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Do NOT include peanuts anywhere in the nut-allergic diner's bowl -- build their sundae fully in the kitchen before the buffet line opens (ice cream, fudge, whipped cream, toasted coconut flakes for crunch instead of peanuts, marshmallows, sprinkles, cherry), using a scoop, ladle, and spoons that have never touched the peanut bowl, and hand it to them directly rather than having them queue at the shared topping line where scoops cross in close proximity. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety whether this kitchen-prepped, pre-portioned approach is sufficient or a fully staffed/separated serving station is still needed before this branch goes live.

name: No-Bake Rice Krispie Treats with PB Drizzle
description: One pot of marshmallow-butter base splits into two pans before the peanut butter ever comes out -- the nut-free portion gets its own tray, bowl, and knife from that point on, and a gluten-free version starts from its own pot entirely.
steps: Melt the butter in a large pot over low heat.
Add the marshmallows and stir until fully melted and smooth.
Remove from heat and fold in the rice cereal until evenly coated.

Divide the mixture between two greased pans here -- this is the nut branch: press about two-thirds into a greased 9x13 pan for the peanut-butter portion, and the rest into its own smaller greased pan for the nut-free portion, using separate spatulas for each pan. Let both cool 10 minutes.
Warm the peanut butter and chocolate chips together in their own small pot until pourable, then drizzle over the 9x13 pan only, using a bowl, spoon, and pot that never touch the nut-free pan.
For the nut-free pan, drizzle with sunflower seed butter and chocolate chips warmed in a separate pot (see adaptations), or leave plain.
Let both pans set 20 minutes before cutting -- each pan gets its own knife and cutting board; the peanut-butter knife never touches the nut-free pan.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy butter or milk-chocolate chips in the drizzle -- substitute a plant-based butter and dairy-free chocolate chips. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

Do NOT use peanut butter -- substitute sunflower seed butter (confirm it's made in a nut-free facility) for the drizzle, warmed in its own separate pot and poured with its own bowl and spoon that never touch the peanut-butter drizzle. This nut-free portion is pressed into its own separate pan from the point the base is divided (before any peanut butter is added), and is cut with its own knife and board -- never the shared-pan/knife-cut boundary used in earlier versions of this recipe. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety that this two-pan separation is sufficient before this branch goes live.
Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

alternateRecipe.name: Gluten-Free Rice Krispie Treats with PB Drizzle
alternateRecipe.description: Same marshmallow-butter method, a certified gluten-free crisp rice cereal standing in for standard cereal -- made in its own pot and pan so it never shares a spoon or tray with the wheat-milled version.
steps: Melt the butter in its own pot over low heat, kept separate from any pot used for standard rice cereal.
Add the marshmallows and stir until fully melted and smooth.
Remove from heat and fold in the certified gluten-free rice cereal until evenly coated.
Press firmly into its own greased pan and let cool 10 minutes.
Warm the peanut butter and chocolate chips together until pourable, then drizzle over the pan (or substitute a nut-free drizzle per the nuts adaptation).
Let set 20 minutes before cutting with its own knife.

name: One-Pan S'mores Bars
description: A pressed graham crust, a layer of chocolate, and a broil-toasted marshmallow top -- three shared steps in one pan, but the crust itself is the one thing that has to be built separately if it's going gluten-free.

imageAttribution.creator: Rachel from Cupcakes Take the Cake

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and line an 8x8 pan with parchment.
Stir the graham cracker crumbs and melted butter together until it looks like wet sand.
Press firmly into the pan and bake 8 minutes until set; cool 5 minutes.
Lay the chocolate pieces evenly over the crust in a single layer.
Arrange marshmallows on top, cut sides down, covering the chocolate completely.
Broil 1-2 minutes, watching closely, until the marshmallows are toasted golden.

Cool 15 minutes before cutting. The crust-and-broil method is the shared base -- a gluten branch needs a different crust from the very first bowl (see adaptations), while dairy is a same-pan swap of the butter and chocolate.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use dairy butter or milk chocolate -- substitute a plant-based butter and a dairy-free chocolate bar, layered the same way in its own pan. Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.
Confirm with aisha-rahman-allergy-safety on this cross-contact wording before this branch goes live.

alternateRecipe.name: Gluten-Free Graham S'mores Bars
alternateRecipe.description: Same press-toast-broil method, gluten-free graham-style cookies crushed in for the crust so the base itself never touches wheat.
steps: Preheat oven to 350°F and line its own 8x8 pan with parchment, kept apart from the wheat-graham batch.
Stir the gluten-free cookie crumbs and melted butter together until it looks like wet sand.
Press firmly into the pan and bake 8 minutes until set; cool 5 minutes.
Lay the chocolate pieces evenly over the crust in a single layer.
Arrange marshmallows on top, cut sides down, covering the chocolate completely.
Broil 1-2 minutes, watching closely, until the marshmallows are toasted golden.
Cool 15 minutes before cutting.

name: One-Bowl No-Bake Energy Bites
description: Oats, honey, and flax split into two bowls from the very first step -- one with certified gluten-free oats, one with standard -- so nut butter, chocolate, and rolling can branch safely with no shared-bowl step ever putting a gluten-strict diner's portion at risk.
steps: For any diner who needs a gluten-free portion, start with two separate bowls right now, before the oats touch anything: pour standard rolled oats into the main bowl, and certified gluten-free rolled oats (regular oats are commonly cross-contacted with wheat during milling, even though oats themselves are gluten-free) into a dedicated gluten-free bowl. Never combine the two. If no gluten-free portion is needed, one bowl is fine.
In each bowl, stir in that portion's share of the ground flaxseed and vanilla, using a separate spoon per bowl.
Warm the honey slightly so it's pourable, then stir it into each bowl separately, with the same separate spoons.
Into the almond portion's bowl, stir in the almond butter and chopped almonds.
Into the nut-free portion's bowl, stir in sunflower seed butter and toasted pepitas instead, using clean hands and a separate spoon that never touches the almond batch.
Fold chocolate chips (dairy-free chocolate chips for that portion, see adaptations) into each bowl to taste.
Roll each bowl's mixture into 1-inch balls, keeping every batch on its own separate plate, and chill 30 minutes to firm up.

adaptations.instructions: Use certified gluten-free rolled oats in a dedicated bowl from step 1, never combined with standard oats, with its own spoon throughout the whole recipe. Regular rolled oats are commonly cross-contacted with wheat during milling, even though oats themselves are gluten-free.
Do NOT use almond butter or chopped almonds -- substitute sunflower seed butter and toasted pepitas, mixed in their own bowl with their own spoon and rolling plate, never touching the almond batch.
Do NOT use dairy chocolate chips -- substitute dairy-free chocolate chips or cacao nibs, folded into that portion's bowl with a clean spoon.

name: Layered Banana Pudding Parfait
description: A stovetop custard, sliced bananas, and vanilla wafers layer into individual cups -- most of the branching happens right at that layering step, cup by cup, except for the custard itself, which has to be built egg-free or dairy-free from the first whisk if either is needed.
steps: Whisk the milk, egg yolks, sugar, and cornstarch together in a saucepan.
Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until thickened to pudding consistency, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the vanilla, then press plastic wrap directly on the surface and chill 1 hour.
Layer vanilla wafers, banana slices, and cooled pudding in parfait cups, repeating.

Top each cup with whipped cream just before serving. Assembly is where the easy branch happens -- swap in gluten-free wafers right into an individual cup; the egg and dairy branches are the two exceptions, since both the egg yolks that set the custard and the milk it's cooked in are mixed into the one shared pot from the very first whisk (see adaptations, both use a full separate recipe).
Chill assembled parfaits at least 30 minutes before serving.

adaptations.instructions: Do not use dairy milk, cream, or whipped cream, and do not try to split a dairy-free portion off the shared custard pot after the fact -- the milk is cooked into that one shared pot from the very first whisk, the same way the egg yolks are. Use the full alternate recipe below instead: its own pot, plant-based milk from the first whisk, dairy-free whipped topping added at the end with separate utensils.

alternateRecipe.name: Dairy-Free Vanilla Custard Parfait
alternateRecipe.description: Same layered parfait, but the custard is built with a plant-based milk from the very first whisk and cooked in its own pot, kept separate from the dairy custard the whole time.

ingredients.name: full-fat coconut milk (or other plant-based milk, not soy milk unless soy is also safe)
dairy-free whipped topping (e.g. coconut whipped topping)

steps: Whisk the plant-based milk, egg yolks, sugar, and cornstarch together in their own saucepan, kept separate from the dairy custard's pot the entire time.
Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until thickened to pudding consistency, about 8 minutes.
Stir in the vanilla, then press plastic wrap directly on the surface and chill 1 hour.
Layer vanilla wafers, banana slices, and the cooled dairy-free pudding in their own parfait cups, repeating.
Top each cup with a dairy-free whipped topping just before serving, using clean utensils that haven't touched the dairy whipped cream.
Chill assembled parfaits at least 30 minutes before serving.

adaptations.instructions: Do NOT use standard vanilla wafers -- substitute gluten-free vanilla wafers, layered straight from their own box into that cup.
The custard's set depends on the egg yolks cooking into the milk from the first whisk, so a same-pot swap isn't reachable -- use the full alternate recipe below instead.

alternateRecipe.name: Eggless Vanilla Pudding Parfait
alternateRecipe.description: Same layered parfait, a pure cornstarch-and-milk pudding standing in for the egg-yolk custard -- cooked in its own pot from the first whisk.
steps: Whisk the milk, sugar, and cornstarch together in a saucepan, in its own pot separate from any egg-based custard.
Cook over medium heat, whisking constantly, until thickened, about 6-8 minutes.
Stir in the vanilla, then press plastic wrap directly on the surface and chill 1 hour.
Layer vanilla wafers, banana slices, and cooled pudding in parfait cups, repeating.
Top each cup with whipped cream just before serving and chill at least 30 minutes.
